अध्याय ८ (पदोन्नति‑साक्षात्कार) की घटना को लेकर रघुवीर और सुधा की प्रतिक्रियाओं की तुलना करते हुए एक संक्षिप्त अनुच्छेद लिखिए।
उपन्यास के शीर्षक “सारा आकाश” की सार्थकता उत्तरार्ध के अंतिम अध्याय (१०) के संदर्भ में स्पष्ट कीजिए।
ISC परीक्षा‑शैली प्रश्न: “उत्तरार्ध की एपिसोडिक संरचना मध्यवर्गीय यथार्थ को कैसे सशक्त करती है? दो अध्यायों के उदाहरण सहित समझाइए।” (१० अंक)
अध्याय ५ (सहकर्मी‑संवाद) को लेकर एक अनुप्रयोग‑आधारित प्रश्न बनाइए: “यदि रघुवीर सहकर्मी की सलाह मान लेता तो कथानक कैसे बदलता?” उत्तर दीजिए।
(a) उत्तरार्ध की एपिसोडिक संरचना के दो लाभ लिखिए। (b) एक हानि बताइए। (c) परीक्षा में इस संरचना पर पूछे गए प्रश्न का उत्तर देते समय कौन‑सी सावधानी रखनी चाहिए? (प्रत्येक भाग २ अंक)
ISC पूर्व‑पेपर पैटर्न: “उत्तरार्ध के किसी एक अध्याय का चयन कर उसकी घटना‑क्रम, कथावाचक‑दृष्टि और विषय‑अभिव्यक्ति का विश्लेषण कीजिए।” (१५ अंक) एक मॉडल उत्तर रूपरेखा दीजिए।
उत्तरार्ध के अध्याय 3 में छत पर बैठे पात्रों की बातचीत के दौरान गर्मी की लू का वर्णन किस मानसिक स्थिति को दर्शाता है?
(a) अध्याय 5 में छत पर लू का वर्णन पात्रों की आंतरिक स्थिति को कैसे दर्शाता है? (b) यदि लू का वर्णन न हो तो पाठक की समझ में क्या अंतर आएगा?
उत्तरार्ध के अध्याय 1 में पिता सतीश पर कौन‑सा दबाव डालते हैं?
यदि आप सतीश के स्थान पर होते, तो अध्याय 8 की बहस में पिता को कैसे समझाते?

(a) सतीश के आंतरिक मोनोलॉग (अध्याय 4) में कौन‑सी दो विरोधी इच्छाएँ व्यक्त होती हैं? (b) ये इच्छाएँ उसके बाह्य व्यवहार को कैसे प्रभावित करती हैं? (c) एक उदाहरण दीजिए जहाँ वह दोनों को संतुलित करने का प्रयास करता है।

ISC पूर्व‑पेपर पैटर्न: “उत्तरार्ध के अध्याय 1‑10 में किसी एक पात्र के चरित्र‑चित्रण में लेखक ने किन दो साहित्यिक युक्तियों (जैसे: संवाद, आंतरिक मोनोलॉग, प्रतीक) का प्रयोग किया है? उदाहरण सहित समझाइए।” (कुल 4 अंक)
निम्नलिखित कथन पर टिप्पणी करें: 'उपन्यास में पात्रों की चुप्पी उनके आंतरिक संघर्ष को अधिक प्रभावी ढंग से व्यक्त करती है।' (10 अंक)
अध्याय 3 में समर द्वारा कही गई कौन-सी पंक्ति उसके आंतरिक द्वंद्व को दर्शाती है?
उत्तरार्ध के अध्याय 3 में घड़ी का रुकना किसका प्रतीक है?

ISC परीक्षा पैटर्न के अनुसार, निम्नलिखित प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए: "उपन्यास 'सारा आकाश' के उत्तरार्ध में प्रतीकवाद और बिंब विधान के माध्यम से राजेन्द्र यादव ने मध्यवर्गीय परिवार की आंतरिक विडंबना को कैसे उजागर किया है? उदाहरण सहित व्याख्या कीजिए।" (अंक विभाजन: प्रतीकवाद की व्याख्या 3, बिंब विधान की व्याख्या 3, उदाहरण 2, निष्कर्ष 2 = कुल 10 अंक)
अध्याय ३ में पुत्र द्वारा पिता के वेतन‑पत्र की गणना करना आर्थिक विडंबना के किस आयाम को दर्शाता है और क्यों?
मूल्यांकन करें: क्या माँ का पड़ोसन से उधार माँगना (अध्याय ७) केवल आर्थिक आवश्यकता है या सामाजिक प्रतिष्ठा का प्रदर्शन भी है?

(a) उपन्यास के अध्याय २ में पुत्र का स्वप्न देखना (लेखक बनना) आर्थिक विडंबना के किस आयाम से सबसे अधिक प्रभावित है? (b) समझाइए कि यह स्वप्न पिता की अपेक्षाओं से कैसे टकराता है। (c) इस टकराव का पुत्र के चरित्र‑विकास पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है?

लागू करें: यदि आप उपन्यास के पात्र 'माँ' की भूमिका में होते, तो अध्याय ६ की स्थिति (पति का वेतन कटौती, पुत्र की बीमारी) में आर्थिक विडंबना के तीनों आयामों को सन्तुलित करते हुए क्या निर्णय लेते? अपने निर्णय की तर्कसंगत व्याख्या करें।

CISCE पूर्व‑पत्र पैटर्न: "उपन्यास 'सारा आकाश — उत्तरार्ध' में आर्थिक विडंबना के तीनों आयामों की अंतर्क्रिया को दर्शाने वाला एक प्रसंग चुनें और उसका विस्तृत विश्लेषण प्रस्तुत करें। (अंक: 10)" उत्तर की रूपरेखा तैयार करें जिसमें (क) प्रसंग चयन, (ख) तीनों आयामों की पहचान, (ग) चरित्र‑विकास पर प्रभाव, (घ) निष्कर्ष शामिल हों। प्रति उप‑भाग अंक विभाजन दर्शाएँ।
अध्याय ३ के रसोईघर संवाद में नायक के लंबे वाक्य और पत्नी के छोटे वाक्य क्या दर्शाते हैं?
अध्याय ६ में बहन के कथन "तुम नहीं समझोगे" का मनोवैज्ञानिक आशय क्या है?

(a) अध्याय ५ में दो पात्रों के संवाद में प्रयुक्त विशेषणों की सूची बनाएं। (b) बताएं कि ये विशेषण पात्रों की सामाजिक पहचान को कैसे निर्मित करते हैं। (c) एक विशेषण को बदलकर संवाद का अर्थ कैसे बदल जाएगा, उदाहरण दें।
सीआईएससीई पूर्व-पत्र पैटर्न: "उत्तरार्ध के संवादों में मौन की भूमिका पर एक संक्षिप्त टिप्पणी लिखें (१५० शब्द)"।
अध्याय ५ में शशि के आत्मसंवाद में प्रयुक्त “खिड़की” प्रतीक का अर्थ स्पष्ट कीजिए।
अध्याय ८ के पारिवारिक भोज दृश्य में व्यंग्य की भूमिका क्या है? लागू कीजिए।
उत्तरार्ध के किसी एक प्रतीक (खिड़की/आकाश/दीवार) को चुनकर उसके तीन स्तरीय अर्थ (शाब्दिक, मनोवैज्ञानिक, सामाजिक) समझाइए। (५ अंक)
(a) अध्याय ८ के भोज दृश्य में व्यंग्य के दो उदाहरण दीजिए। (b) व्यंग्य यहाँ सामाजिक यथार्थवाद को कैसे सशक्त करता है? (२+४ अंक)
उत्तरार्ध और पूर्वार्ध (नोड ००२ में वर्णित) के कथानक संरचना की तुलना कीजिए: समानताएँ, भिन्नताएँ, और प्रभाव। (६ अंक)
ISC २०२७ पैटर्न अनुसार: “उत्तरार्ध में राजेन्द्र यादव ने मध्यवर्गीय यथार्थवाद को कैसे साधा है? तीन बिंदुओं में पाठ्य-साक्ष्य सहित समझाइए।” (६ अंक)

**APPLICATION:** (a) मान लीजिए आप एक नाट्य‑समूह के निर्देशक हैं और “आषाढ़ का एक दिन” का मंचन 2025 में करना चाहते हैं। राकेश की मूल मंचन‑शैली के किन दो तत्वों को आप अनिवार्य रूप से रखेंगे और क्यों? (b) एक आधुनिक तकनीकी तत्व (जैसे प्रोजेक्शन‑मैपिंग) जोड़ने से नाटक के द्वि‑स्तरीय समय‑बोध पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ेगा?

**COMPARISON:** (a) “आषाढ़ का एक दिन” और बादल सरकार के “एवं इन्द्रजीत” (1963) — दोनों नाटकों में नाटककार की भूमिका और समाज के प्रति उसकी जवाबदेही कैसे भिन्न‑भिन्न व्यक्त होती है? (b) दोनों में मंचन‑शैली का अंतर क्या है? (c) कौन‑सा नाटक अधिक “राजनीतिक” है और क्यों?

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** (a) “आषाढ़ का एक दिन” के प्रथम मंचन का वर्ष, स्थान और निर्देशक लिखें। (1 अंक) (b) नाटक के दो साहित्यिक स्रोतों के नाम लिखें। (2 अंक) (c) समझाएँ कि नाटक की मंचन‑शैली (यथार्थवादी सेट, प्रतीकात्मक प्रकाश, संवाद‑केंद्रित अभिनय) दर्शक को द्वि‑स्तरीय समय‑बोध कैसे देती है। (4 अंक)
अंक 2, दृश्य 1 में राजदूत कौन सा संदेश लाता है?
(a) अंक 2, दृश्य 1 में राजदूत के आगमन का नाटकीय उद्देश्य बताइए। (b) यदि राजदूत न आता तो कथानक कैसे बदलता?
अंक 2, दृश्य 1 और अंक 3, दृश्य 1 (अगले नोड में) में कालिदास के चरित्र विकास की तुलना कीजिए।
पिछले वर्ष के आईएससी प्रश्नपत्र के आधार पर: “आषाढ़ का एक दिन में वर्षा केवल मौसम नहीं, भावनाओं का वाहक है।” इस कथन की पुष्टि अंक 2, दृश्य 1 के संदर्भ में कीजिए।
अंक 2 में कालिदास के राजदरबार वाले दृश्य का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?
पत्र-शैली (एपिस्टोलरी) का प्रयोग अंक 2 में किस नाट्य उद्देश्य की पूर्ति करता है?
अंक 2 में वर्षा/मेघ के प्रतीक का प्रयोग कैसे किया गया है?
अंक 2 का केंद्रीय विषय "कर्तव्य बनाम प्रेम" कैसे प्रकट होता है?
अंक 2 के तीनों दृश्यों को क्रमबद्ध करके उनके पारस्परिक संबंध की व्याख्या कीजिए।
यदि आप मल्लिका की जगह होते, तो कालिदास के दूसरे पत्र का उत्तर कैसे लिखते? अपने उत्तर में अंक 2 के भावबोध को बनाए रखिए।
अंक 2 में कालिदास के चरित्र विकास का मूल्यांकन कीजिए: क्या वह अंक 1 के आदर्शवादी कवि से यथार्थवादी राजकवि बनने की प्रक्रिया में अपने मूल्यों से समझौता करता है?
अंक 1 और अंक 2 में मल्लिका के चित्रण की तुलना कीजिए।
सीआईएससीई परीक्षा पैटर्न के अनुसार: "अंक 2 में पत्र-शैली नाट्य तकनीक के रूप में कैसे प्रयुक्त हुई है? उदाहरण सहित समझाइए।" (अंक विभाजन: 2+3)
(a) दृश्य 3 में कालिदास के संवादों में प्रयुक्त अलंकारों की पहचान करें। (b) बताएं कि ये अलंकार उनके मानसिक द्वंद्व को कैसे व्यक्त करते हैं। (c) एक उदाहरण देकर समझाएं।
(a) दृश्य 3 में मल्लिका की मौन स्वीकृति का नाट्यशैली में क्या महत्व है? (b) इसकी तुलना दृश्य 1 में उसकी मुखरता से करें। (c) नाटक के समग्र चरित्र विकास पर इसका प्रभाव बताएं।
दृश्य 3 की तुलना दृश्य 2 से करें: कथानक गति, संवाद शैली, और प्रतीकवाद के संदर्भ में।
चौथे अंक की तुलना तीसरे अंक (ब्लॉक 3) से करें: **(a)** कालिदास की मनोदशा में क्या परिवर्तन आया? **(b)** मल्लिका की भूमिका कैसे बदली? **(c)** नाट्य तकनीक के प्रयोग में क्या अंतर है?

ISC 2027 पैटर्न के अनुसार, निम्नलिखित प्रश्न का उत्तर लिखें: “आषाढ़ का एक दिन के चौथे अंक में मोहन राकेश ने नाट्य तकनीक का प्रयोग कालिदास के आंतरिक द्वंद्व को बाह्य करने के लिए कैसे किया है? उदाहरण सहित समझाएँ। (10 अंक)”

**CISCE PAST-PAPER PATTERN:** “आषाढ़ का एक दिन के पाँचवें अंक में नाटककार ने वर्षा का प्रयोग केवल वातावरण निर्माण के लिए नहीं, बल्कि पात्रों की आंतरिक स्थिति को व्यक्त करने के लिए किया है।” — इस कथन की पुष्टि पाठ्यांशों के संदर्भ में कीजिए। (12 अंक)

**HOTS:** “आषाढ़ का एक दिन में पत्र‑पाठ केवल संचार‑उपकरण नहीं, बल्कि चरित्र‑निर्माण का माध्यम है।” — इस कथन की पुष्टि खंड 6 के संदर्भ में करते हुए दो अन्य हिंदी नाटकों (जैसे “अंधा युग”, “आधे अधूरे”) में पत्र‑प्रयोग से तुलना कीजिए।
**EVALUATION/CRITIQUE:** “मोहन राकेश ने खंड 6 में मल्लिका को केवल कालिदास की छाया बना दिया है — उसकी स्वतंत्र अस्मिता अनुपस्थित है।” इस आलोचना का मूल्यांकन पाठ‑साक्ष्य सहित कीजिए।
**COMPARISON:** खंड 6 में कालिदास‑मल्लिका के पत्र‑व्यवहार की तुलना कालिदास के ऐतिहासिक “मेघदूत” के यक्ष‑यक्षी संवाद से कीजिए। समानताएँ और भिन्नताएँ स्पष्ट कीजिए।
**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** “आषाढ़ का एक दिन के छठे खंड में नाटककार ने प्रकाश‑योजना और ध्वनि‑संकेतों का प्रयोग चरित्र‑मनोविज्ञान को बाह्यीकरण करने के लिए कैसे किया है? उदाहरण सहित समझाइए।” (10 अंक)
ब्लॉक ६ और ब्लॉक ७ में कालिदास के चरित्र‑विकास की तुलना करें। किन दो प्रमुख परिवर्तनों को आप रेखांकित करेंगे?

**EVALUATION/CRITIQUE (MULTI‑PART):** (a) इस दृश्य में कालिदास के चरित्र‑विकास की सुसंगतता का मूल्यांकन कीजिए। (2 अंक) (b) मल्लिका की प्रतिक्रिया क्या नाटक के समग्र थीम को सुदृढ़ करती है? (2 अंक) (c) यदि दृश्य को आधुनिक परिवेश (कॉर्पोरेट नौकरी) में रूपांतरित किया जाए, तो कौन‑से तत्व परिवर्तित होंगे और कौन‑से अपरिवर्तित रहेंगे? (3 अंक)
**COMPARISON:** अंक 2 के प्रस्थान‑दृश्य (c12_hin_isc_03_008) और इस दृश्य (अंक 3, दृश्य 2) में कालिदास के संवाद‑शैली और उद्देश्य की तुलना कीजिए।

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN (MULTI‑PART):** “आषाढ़ का एक दिन के अंक 3, दृश्य 2 में नाटककार ने ‘कर्तव्य बनाम प्रेम’ थीम को संवाद‑विरोधाभास, मौन, और प्रकाश‑छाया के माध्यम से कैसे उभारा है? तीनों उपकरणों के लिए एक‑एक उदाहरण देकर समझाइए। (6 अंक)”
नाटक के दृश्य‑खंड 9 में राजदूत किसे बुलाने आता है और उसकी भाषा में कौन‑सा शब्द राजसत्ता की अनिवार्यता दर्शाता है?
ISC परीक्षा पैटर्न के अनुसार, दृश्य‑खंड 9 पर एक दीर्घ‑उत्तर प्रश्न का आदर्श उत्तर‑संरचना (intro, textual evidence, analysis, conclusion) क्या होगी?

(a) दृश्य‑खंड 9 में कालिदास के अंतिम निर्णय को प्रभावित करने वाले दो बाह्य कारक बताएं। (b) इन कारकों में से कौन‑सा अधिक निर्णायक है और क्यों? (c) इस निर्णय का मल्लिका के चरित्र पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है?

नाटक के दृश्य‑खंड 9 की तुलना शेक्सपियर के “हैमलेट” के अंतिम दृश्य (Act 5, Scene 2) से करें। (a) दोनों में नियति (fate) की भूमिका, (b) नायिका की प्रतिक्रिया (Ophelia vs. Mallika), (c) कोरस/होरेशियो की टिप्पणीकार भूमिका।

ISC 2027 पैटर्न के अनुसार, दृश्य‑खंड 9 पर एक 15‑अंक का निबंध‑प्रश्न इस प्रकार हो सकता है: “आषाढ़ का एक दिन के अंतिम दृश्य‑खंड में मोहन राकेश ने नाट्य‑तकनीकों (ड्रामेटिक टेक्निक्स) का प्रयोग करके कलाकार‑राज्य द्वंद्व को कैसे उभारा है? उदाहरण सहित समझाएं।” इसके लिए अंक‑विभाजन सहित आदर्श उत्तर‑रूपरेखा तैयार करें।
पिछले वर्षों के ISC प्रश्न‑पत्रों में दृश्य‑खंड 9 से पूछे गए एक वास्तविक प्रश्न का पुनरुत्पादन करें और उसके लिए मॉडल उत्तर (150‑200 शब्द) लिखें।
अंक २ में कालिदास राजदरबार का निमंत्रण स्वीकार क्यों करता है?
अंक ३ में कालिदास की कविता में क्या परिवर्तन आता है?
कालिदास के चरित्र में 'आदर्शवाद' और 'यथार्थवाद' का संघर्ष कैसे चित्रित है? (a) अंक २ में, (b) अंक ३ में।
आईएससी २०२७ पैटर्न के अनुसार कालिदास के चरित्र पर १० अंकों का निबंधात्मक प्रश्न कैसे हल करें? रूपरेखा दीजिए।
मल्लिका की डायरी का एक पृष्ठ लिखिए जो अंक ३ के विद्यालय-प्रस्ताव दृश्य के बाद की मनोदशा दर्शाता हो।
अंक २ के उस दृश्य का सन्दर्भ-प्रसंग दीजिए जहाँ मल्लिका कालिदास से कहती है “तुम्हारी राह अलग है, मेरी अलग”।

(a) मल्लिका के चरित्र में “त्याग” और “स्वाभिमान” का अन्तर स्पष्ट कीजिए। (b) अंक २ के एक संवाद का उदाहरण देकर समझाइए कि मल्लिका त्याग नहीं, स्वाभिमान चुनती है। (c) इस भेद का नाटक के सन्देश पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है?
(a) मल्लिका के चरित्र में “मौन” की भूमिका क्या है? (b) अंक ३ में उसके मौन के दो क्षण पहचानिए और उनकी व्याख्या कीजिए। (c) मौन कैसे उसके प्रतिरोध का साधन बनता है?

ISC 2026 के प्रश्न-पत्र के अनुरूप: “मल्लिका नाटक की नैतिक धुरी है।” इस कथन की विवेचना कीजिए। (अ) मल्लिका के तीन निर्णयों का उल्लेख कीजिए जो इस कथन को सिद्ध करते हैं। (ब) कालिदास के चरित्र के सन्दर्भ में मल्लिका की नैतिक श्रेष्ठता समझाइए। (स) नाटककार मोहन राकेश ने मल्लिका के माध्यम से स्त्री-अस्मिता को कैसे स्थापित किया है?
अंक २ में प्रियंगुमंजरी कालिदास से मिलने क्यों आती है?
(a) अंक २ में प्रियंगुमंजरी के दो संवाद लिखें जो उसके अधिकार भाव को दर्शाते हैं। (b) इन संवादों का मल्लिका पर प्रभाव समझाएं। (c) इस प्रभाव का नाटक के विषय 'प्रेम में स्वामित्व' से संबंध बताएं।
ISC परीक्षा पैटर्न के अनुसार, "सहायक पात्र नायक के चरित्र विकास में उत्प्रेरक का कार्य करते हैं" — इस कथन की पुष्टि आषाढ़ का एक दिन के अंक २ और ३ के संदर्भ में करें।
अंक 2 में कालिदास के राजदरबार में प्रवेश के समय कौन-सा प्रमुख विषय उभरता है?
अंक 3 में कालिदास के उज्जयिनी से लौटने पर मल्लिका का त्याग किस विषय को पुष्ट करता है?

अंक 2 और 3 में कालिदास के चरित्र विकास की तुलना करें। (क) उसके आंतरिक द्वंद्व में क्या परिवर्तन आता है? (ख) नाट्य तकनीक इस परिवर्तन को कैसे दर्शाती है? (ग) इस विकास का नाटक के केंद्रीय विषय पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है?
यदि आप इस नाटक का मंचन करें, तो अंक 3 के अंतिम दृश्य (मल्लिका का त्याग) को दर्शकों के लिए अधिक प्रभावी बनाने के लिए किन तीन नाट्य तत्वों का प्रयोग करेंगे? प्रत्येक का औचित्य दें।
तुलना करें: अंक 2 में कालिदास का राजदरबार प्रवेश और अंक 3 में उसका उज्जयिनी से लौटना — दोनों दृश्यों में नाट्य तकनीक (संवाद, मौन, प्रकाश) का प्रयोग कैसे भिन्न है और क्यों?
अंक 2 में कालिदास के कथन “मैं नहीं जानता कि राजकवि बनना मेरे लिए क्या अर्थ रखता है” का **वक्ता** कौन है और यह संवाद किस **प्रसंग** में बोला गया है?
अंक 3 के अंतिम दृश्य में कालिदास का “मैं लौट आया हूँ” कथन **चरित्र विकास** की किस अवस्था को दर्शाता है?
ISC 2027 के **पिछले वर्ष के प्रश्नपत्र** में “आषाढ़ का एक दिन” से **कौन‑सा उद्धरण** सबसे अधिक पूछा गया?

**(a)** अंक 2 में कालिदास के “मैं नहीं जानता…” संवाद में **कौन‑सा अलंकार** प्रमुख है? **(b)** यह अलंकार **कैसे** कालिदास के **आंतरिक द्वंद्व** को तीव्र करता है? **(c)** यदि छात्र “अनुप्रास” लिख दे, तो **कौन‑सी गलतफ़हमी** प्रकट होती है?
**आवेदन:** मान लीजिए परीक्षा में पूछा जाए — “अंक 3 के अंतिम दृश्य में कालिदास की वापसी **किस प्रकार** नाटक के **संदेश** को सुदृढ़ करती है?” **उत्तर की रूपरेखा** दीजिए।

**(a)** ISC 2027 के **नमूना प्रश्नपत्र** में “आषाढ़ का एक दिन” से **कौन‑सा दीर्घउत्तरीय प्रश्न** संभावित है? **(b)** उसके लिए **अंक‑विभाजन** (Marking Scheme) क्या होगा? **(c)** छात्र **कौन‑सी आम गलती** करता है जिससे **2 अंक** कट जाते हैं?
**तुलना:** अंक 2 के “मैं नहीं जानता…” और अंक 3 के “मैं लौट आया हूँ” — **दोनों संवादों में “मैं” सर्वनाम का प्रयोग** **कैसे** भिन्न‑भिन्न **मनोदशा** दर्शाता है?

ISC २०२३ के प्रश्नपत्र में “लेखक एवं संदर्भ” से संबंधित एक प्रश्न था: “जयशंकर प्रसाद की छायावादी विशेषताओं को ‘दासी’ के संदर्भ में स्पष्ट कीजिए।” इस प्रश्न का आदर्श उत्तर संक्षेप में लिखिए (अधिकतम २०० शब्द)।
ISC परीक्षा शैली में: "दासी" के परिवेश और वातावरण के पारस्परिक संबंध को समझाते हुए एक संक्षिप्त उत्तर लिखिए (लगभग 80 शब्द)।
ISC विगत प्रश्न पत्र पैटर्न: "दासी" में परिवेश और वातावरण के माध्यम से प्रसाद जी ने स्त्री-शोषण की किस सीमा तक अभिव्यक्ति दी है? सप्रमाण व्याख्या कीजिए (200 शब्द)।
**QUESTION:** ISC 2023 प्रश्नपत्र पैटर्न के अनुसार: "दासी कहानी का केंद्रीय विचार स्पष्ट कीजिए और उसके सामाजिक सरोकारों की विवेचना कीजिए।" (10 अंक)
ISC परीक्षा‑शैली में: "दासी" की भाषा‑शैली‑अलंकार त्रयी के परस्पर संबंध को समझाते हुए एक संक्षिप्त उत्तर लिखिए (अधिकतम 150 शब्द)।
“दासी” के किसी एक प्रसंग को लेकर 5-अंकीय प्रश्न का मॉडल उत्तर लिखिए।

CISCE विगत-पत्र पैटर्न प्रश्न: “निम्नलिखित अंश पढ़कर प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए: (अंश ‘दासी’ के नृत्य-प्रसंग से) (क) प्रसंग लिखिए। (ख) वक्ता कौन है? (ग) ‘घुँघरू’ का प्रतीकार्थ स्पष्ट कीजिए। (घ) इस प्रसंग से नायिका की मनोदशा का विश्लेषण कीजिए।” (अंक विभाजन: 1+1+2+4 = 8 अंक)
दासी में सामाजिक यथार्थवाद और प्रतीकवाद के समन्वय की व्याख्या करते हुए बताइए कि यह समन्वय कहानी के केंद्रीय विषय को कैसे उभारता है। (अंक 10)

बोर्ड परीक्षा प्रश्न: 'दासी में सामाजिक यथार्थवाद और प्रतीकवाद के समन्वय द्वारा प्रसाद ने नारी शोषण की त्रासदी को कैसे उभारा है? उदाहरण सहित समझाइए।' (अंक 12) — इस प्रश्न का आदर्श उत्तर लिखिए जिसमें भूमिका, विश्लेषण, उदाहरण, निष्कर्ष हों।
ISC पूर्व-पत्र पैटर्न: “दासी में प्रतीकवाद कथानक को किस सीमा तक सार्वभौमिक बनाता है? उदाहरण सहित समझाइए।” (अंक विभाजन: 2+3+2)
ISC 2023 के प्रश्नपत्र में दासी पर पूछे गए दीर्घउत्तरीय प्रश्न का पैटर्न क्या था? उसके अनुसार आदर्श उत्तर की रूपरेखा दीजिए।
ISC 2023 के प्रश्नपत्र में पूछा गया: "दासी कहानी के शीर्षक की सार्थकता पर आलोचनात्मक टिप्पणी लिखिए।" इसके लिए आदर्श उत्तर की रूपरेखा प्रस्तुत कीजिए, जिसमें अंक-विभाजन भी हो।
**(a)** द्विवेदी जी के जीवन की दो प्रमुख घटनाएँ बताइए जिन्होंने उनके चिंतन को प्रभावित किया। (2 अंक) **(b)** उन घटनाओं का “क्या निराश हुआ जाए” निबंध पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ा? (3 अंक)
**प्रश्न:** “क्या निराश हुआ जाए” निबंध की भाषा-शैली का विश्लेषण करते हुए बताइए कि द्विवेदी जी ने संस्कृतनिष्ठ शब्दावली का प्रयोग करते हुए भी भाषा को बोधगम्य कैसे बनाया? (5 अंक)

**(a)** द्विवेदी जी ने निबंध में निराशा के किन तीन कारणों का उल्लेख किया है? (3 अंक) **(b)** प्रत्येक कारण के लिए वे कौन-सा दार्शनिक उपाय सुझाते हैं? (4 अंक) **(c)** इन उपायों का आधुनिक जीवन में क्या प्रासंगिकता है? (3 अंक)
**तुलनात्मक प्रश्न:** हजारी प्रसाद द्विवेदी और प्रेमचंद के निबंध-लेखन में समानता और भिन्नता के दो-दो बिंदु लिखिए। (6 अंक)
**ISC पूर्व-पत्र पैटर्न प्रश्न:** “हजारी प्रसाद द्विवेदी के निबंध ‘क्या निराश हुआ जाए’ में आशा का संदेश किस प्रकार निहित है? पाठ के किन्हीं तीन प्रसंगों के संदर्भ में समझाइए।” (10 अंक)
यदि आप इस निबंध का सारांश ५० शब्दों में लिखें, तो कौन‑से तीन बिंदु अनिवार्य होंगे?
ISC 2023 के प्रश्नपत्र में इस निबंध पर पूछे गए प्रश्न का पैटर्न देखते हुए, एक संभावित प्रश्न बनाएँ और उसका आदर्श उत्तर लिखें (अंक विभाजन सहित)।
निबंध के वातावरण को दर्शाता एक लघु दृश्य (5-6 पंक्तियाँ) लिखें जो किसी पात्र के आंतरिक मनोभाव को प्रकट करे।

आईएससी परीक्षा में पूछे गए प्रश्न के अनुरूप: "निबंध के परिवेश और वातावरण का विश्लेषण करते हुए द्विवेदी जी की सांस्कृतिक दृष्टि स्पष्ट कीजिए।" (अंक विभाजन: परिवेश विश्लेषण 3, वातावरण विश्लेषण 3, दृष्टि निष्कर्ष 2)
ISC परीक्षा पैटर्न के अनुसार: “निबंध ‘क्या निराश हुआ जाए’ में पात्रों के माध्यम से द्विवेदी जी ने जीवन‑दर्शन को कैसे व्यक्त किया है? संक्षिप्त उत्तर लिखें (लगभग 150 शब्द)।”

ISC २०२३ के प्रश्नपत्र में इस निबंध पर पूछे गए दीर्घउत्तरीय प्रश्न का प्रारूप था: “निबंध के केंद्रीय विचार की व्याख्या कीजिए और उसके आधुनिक जीवन में प्रासंगिकता दर्शाइए।” इसके लिए आदर्श उत्तर संरचना लिखिए और अंक विभाजन बताइए।
(a) निबंध के किस उद्धरण में "धर्म" शब्द प्रयुक्त हुआ है? (b) उस प्रसंग में "धर्म" का अर्थ क्या है? (c) यह शब्द लेखक के दृष्टिकोण को कैसे प्रकट करता है? (अंक: 1+2+2)
निबंध के दो उद्धरण चुनकर दिखाइए कि द्विवेदी जी ने इतिहास और संस्कृति को आशा के साधन के रूप में कैसे प्रयुक्त किया है। अपने उत्तर में दोनों उद्धरणों के पैराग्राफ संख्या अवश्य लिखें। (अंक: 5)
तुलना कीजिए: "क्या निराश हुआ जाए" के उद्धरणों की भाषा-शैली और "अशोक के फूल" (कक्षा 11 गद्य) के उद्धरणों की भाषा-शैली में क्या समानताएँ और अंतर हैं? (अंक: 6)

ISC 2023 प्रश्नपत्र के पैटर्न पर आधारित: "निबंध 'क्या निराश हुआ जाए' से किन्हीं तीन उद्धरणों की सहायता से द्विवेदी जी के आशावाद के तीन स्तरों (व्यक्तिगत, सामाजिक, सांस्कृतिक) की व्याख्या कीजिए।" (अंक: 12)

(2 अंक) (ब) “भक्तिन की भक्ति में प्रदर्शन नहीं, प्रामाणिकता है।” — इस कथन की पुष्टि पाठ के दो प्रसंगों से कीजिए। (4 अंक) (स) भक्तिन के चरित्र में ‘लोक’ और ‘शास्त्र’ का कैसा समन्वय है? तीन बिंदुओं में समझाइए। (6 अंक)

A non‑resident Indian (NRI) files a writ petition under Article 226 challenging a municipal corporation’s decision to demolish a heritage building in his hometown, claiming he visits once a year. Does he have locus standi?

A citizen files a writ petition under Article 32 challenging a State law that bans a religious practice. The citizen does not belong to that religion but claims the law violates the Constitution’s secular fabric. Does the citizen have locus standi? Justify with two reasons.
Compare the locus standi test for a writ petition under Article 32 with that for a civil suit under Order 1 Rule 8 CPC (representative suit). Highlight two similarities and two differences.

Past‑paper style: “Discuss the evolution of locus standi in Indian PIL jurisprudence from *S.P. Gupta* (1981) to *People’s Union for Democratic Rights* (1982) and *Bandhua Mukti Morcha* (1984).” Provide a structured answer with three stages and mark allocation.
Explain why Section 27 of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930 is considered a legislative embodiment of *nemo dat quod non habet*.
A thief steals a motorcycle and sells it to Priya, who pays fair market value and has no knowledge of the theft. Under the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, what title does Priya acquire, and why?

Create a short factual scenario (3‑4 sentences) where the exception of “sale by a mercantile agent” under Section 27 proviso of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930 would protect the buyer, and explain the required conditions.

(a) Define *nemo dat quod non habet* and state its statutory embodiment in the Sale of Goods Act, 1930. (b) Explain the distinction between a void title and a voidable title with one illustration each. (c) Under which section can a bona fide purchaser acquire good title from a seller with a voidable title?

Compare the protection afforded to a bona fide purchaser under the *Sale of Goods Act, 1930* (Sections 27 proviso and 29) with the protection under the *Transfer of Property Act, 1882* (Section 53). Highlight two key differences.

**Past‑paper style:** “X, a thief, steals a painting and sells it to Y, who buys in good faith. Y then sells it to Z, also in good faith. The original owner O sues Z for recovery. Decide with reference to *nemo dat quod non habet* and the Sale of Goods Act, 1930.”

A past ISC question: “Section 3 of the XYZ Act defines ‘vehicle’ as ‘any motor car, motor cycle, scooter, and other mechanically propelled vehicle.’ A battery‑operated wheelchair is challenged as a ‘vehicle.’ Decide using *noscitur a sociis*.” Provide the answer with reasoning.

**Application:** The Income Tax Act, 1961, Section 10(10D) exempts “any sum received under a life insurance policy, including bonus, and other benefits.” A policyholder receives a “loyalty addition” paid by the insurer after 20 years. Is it exempt?

**CISCE Past‑Paper Pattern:** (a) State the maxim *noscitur a sociis* and its literal translation. (2 marks) (b) Explain, with an example from any Indian statute, how the maxim assists in interpreting a general term following specific terms. (4 marks) (c) Distinguish *noscitur a sociis* from *ejusdem generis* in two points. (4 marks)

Given the following excerpt, identify the obiter dictum: “Having held that the impugned order violates Article 14, we need not decide whether it also breaches Article 21. Nevertheless, we observe that any arbitrary state action would offend the dignity guaranteed by Article 21.”
Explain the difference between ratio decidendi and obiter dicta with reference to the Supreme Court’s decision in *Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala* (1973).

Given the facts: “A High Court held that a municipal corporation cannot levy a tax on agricultural land because Article 282 prohibits it.” The court also remarked, “The corporation should instead seek state legislation for such revenue.” Identify the ratio decidendi and the obiter dicta.

In an ISC Legal Studies paper, a 4‑mark question asks: “Distinguish between ratio decidendi and obiter dicta with reference to their binding effect under Article 141.” Outline a model answer structure.

**EVALUATION/CRITIQUE (multi‑part):** (a) Explain the “**necessity test**” for identifying ratio decidendi. (2 marks) (b) Apply the test to the following excerpt: “The court finds the defendant liable for negligence because he owed a duty of care, breached it, and caused damage. The court also observes that the defendant’s insurance policy would cover the loss.” Identify ratio and obiter. (3 marks) (c) Discuss one limitation of the necessity test in complex multi‑issue judgments. (2 marks)

**COMPARISON (multi‑part):** (a) Compare the binding force of a Supreme Court ratio decidendi with that of a High Court ratio decidendi in India. (3 marks) (b) Contrast the treatment of obiter dicta from the Supreme Court versus a High Court when cited in a lower court. (2 marks)

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN (multi‑part):** “Read the following judgment excerpt and answer: ‘The appellant was convicted under Section 302 IPC. The trial court relied on the dying declaration recorded by the magistrate. The High Court upheld the conviction, stating: “A dying declaration recorded by a magistrate is admissible and reliable.” The Supreme Court, on appeal, observed: “While a magistrate’s recording adds credibility, the court must still test the declaration for consistency and voluntariness.”’ (i) Identify the ratio decidendi of the Supreme Court’s observation. (2 marks) (ii) State whether the High Court’s statement is ratio or obiter in its own judgment. (1 mark) (iii) Explain how a Sessions Court should apply the Supreme Court’s ratio when evaluating a dying declaration in a future case. (2 marks)”
A CISCE ISC 2023 paper asked: “Let \(R\) be a relation on \(\mathbb{Z}\) defined by \(aRb \iff a-b\) is a multiple of 3. Prove that \(R\) is an equivalence relation.” Outline the three proof steps.

**APPLICATION:** A software engineer defines a relation \(R\) on the set of all strings over \(\{0,1\}\) by \(xRy \iff\) the number of 1’s in \(x\) equals the number of 1’s in \(y\). (a) Show that \(R\) is an equivalence relation. (b) If the maximum string length considered is 3, how many equivalence classes exist? (c) Give one representative string for each class.

**COMPARISON:** Compare the relations \(R_1 = \{(a,b) \in \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z} \mid a-b \text{ is even}\}\) and \(R_2 = \{(a,b) \in \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z} \mid a-b \text{ is a multiple of 4}\}\). (a) Which relation has more equivalence classes? (b) Are the equivalence classes of \(R_2\) subsets of those of \(R_1\)? Justify. (c) If a relation \(R_3\) is defined by \(a-b\) multiple of 6, how many equivalence classes does \(R_3\) have?

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** (ISC 2022, 4 marks) Let \(A = \{1,2,3,4,5\}\). A relation \(R\) on \(A\) is defined by \(aRb \iff a \le b\). (i) Write \(R\) in roster form. (ii) Determine whether \(R\) is reflexive, symmetric, transitive. (iii) Is \(R\) an equivalence relation? Give reason.

**Application:** A school club has members \(\{A,B,C,D\}\). The “knows” relation \(K\) is recorded as a directed graph where each vertex has a loop. The adjacency matrix of \(K\) has 1’s on the diagonal and some off‑diagonal 1’s. (a) Explain why the loops guarantee reflexivity of \(K\). (b) If the club adds a new member \(E\) but forgets to add a loop for \(E\), is the updated relation still reflexive? Why?
In an ISC 2023 paper, a question asked: “If \(R\) is a symmetric relation on a set \(A\) and \((a,b)\in R\), prove that \((b,a)\in R\).” Write a concise proof.

**ISC 2022 Style Question:** Let \(A=\{1,2,3,4\}\). A relation \(R\) on \(A\) is defined by \(R=\{(x,y)\mid x+y\text{ is even}\}\). **(a)** Write \(R\) explicitly as a set of ordered pairs. **(b)** Prove that \(R\) is symmetric. **(c)** Find the number of equivalence classes of \(R\) and list them.
Consider the relation “has the same remainder when divided by 3” on the set of integers \(\mathbb{Z}\). Is this an equivalence relation? Explain.
Prove that the relation \(R\) on \(\mathbb{Z}\) defined by \(aRb \iff 5 \mid (a-b)\) is an equivalence relation. Write the equivalence classes.
**COMPARISON:** Compare the equivalence relations “congruence modulo 6” and “congruence modulo 3” on \(\mathbb{Z}\). How do their equivalence classes relate? Which is a refinement of the other?

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** (a) Prove that the relation \(R\) on the set \(A = \{1,2,3,4,5\}\) defined by \(R = \{(x,y) \mid x+y \text{ is even}\}\) is an equivalence relation. (b) Write the equivalence classes. (c) How many equivalence relations on \(A\) contain the pair \((1,2)\)? (Marks: 3+2+2)
Prove that the set of all equivalence classes of an equivalence relation \(R\) on a non‑empty set \(A\) forms a partition of \(A\). (CISCE exam‑style, 4 marks)

(Comparison) Compare the equivalence classes of the relation “congruence modulo 4” on \(\mathbb{Z}\) with the partition of \(\mathbb{Z}\) into even and odd integers. (a) How many classes does each have? (b) Is one partition a refinement of the other? (c) Explain the relationship between the two equivalence relations.

(CISCE past‑paper pattern) Let \(R\) be an equivalence relation on a non‑empty set \(A\). (a) Define the equivalence class of an element \(a \in A\). (1 mark) (b) Prove that for any \(a,b \in A\), either \([a] = [b]\) or \([a] \cap [b] = \varnothing\). (3 marks) (c) Hence show that the quotient set \(A/R\) is a partition of \(A\). (2 marks)

**(Application)** A school has 120 students. They are grouped by their house (Red, Blue, Green, Yellow) and also by their grade (11, 12). Each student belongs to exactly one house and one grade. (a) Define an equivalence relation \(R_1\) for “same house” and \(R_2\) for “same grade”. Write the equivalence classes for each. (b) Consider the relation \(R = R_1 \cap R_2\) (i.e., same house **and** same grade). Prove \(R\) is an equivalence relation. (c) How many equivalence classes does \(R\) have at most? Explain.
Let \(R\) be the relation on \(\mathbb{Z}\) defined by \(a\,R\,b \iff a - b\) is a multiple of 3. Prove that \(R\) is an equivalence relation and list its equivalence classes.

An ISC 2023 question: “Let \(R\) be a relation on the set of real numbers defined by \(x\,R\,y \iff x^2 = y^2\). Determine whether \(R\) is an equivalence relation.” Provide a complete solution as expected in the board exam.

(Application) A teacher assigns a project: “Define a relation on the set of all students in Class 12 such that two students are related if they have the same birth month.” Is this an equivalence relation? If yes, how many equivalence classes are there? If the class has 40 students with birth months distributed as: Jan 3, Feb 4, Mar 2, Apr 5, May 3, Jun 4, Jul 3, Aug 4, Sep 2, Oct 5, Nov 3, Dec 2, list the equivalence classes with their sizes.

(Evaluation/Critique) Consider the following student solution to an ISC question: “Let \(R\) be a relation on \(\mathbb{Z}\) defined by \(a\,R\,b \iff a + b\) is even. Reflexive: \(a + a = 2a\) even → true. Symmetric: \(a + b\) even → \(b + a\) even → true. Transitive: \(a + b\) even and \(b + c\) even → \(a + c\) even? Not necessarily. Example: \(a=1, b=1, c=2\). \(1+1=2\) even, \(1+2=3\) odd → fails. So not transitive.” (a) Identify the logical error in the transitivity test. (b) Provide a correct proof or disproof of transitivity. (c) State the final classification of \(R\) with justification. Allocate marks: (a) 2 marks, (b) 3 marks, (c) 1 mark.

(CISCE past‑paper pattern) The following question appeared in ISC 2022: “Let \(A = \{1,2,3,4\}\). Define a relation \(R\) on \(A\) by \(R = \{(1,1), (2,2), (3,3), (4,4), (1,2), (2,1), (3,4), (4,3)\}\). (a) Show that \(R\) is an equivalence relation. (b) Write the equivalence classes. (c) How many equivalence relations on \(A\) contain the pair \((1,2)\)?” Provide a complete solution with mark allocation: (a) 3 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 3 marks.

A ramp is built such that its slope is \(\frac{3}{4}\). Find the angle of inclination \(\alpha\) using \(\tan^{-1}\). If the ramp length is 10 m, compute the vertical rise. (Use \(\tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4}\approx 0.6435\) rad.)
A student sketches y = tan⁻¹ x with a vertical asymptote at x = 0. Identify the error and correct it.
Design a piecewise function that matches the graph of y = sec⁻¹ x for x ≥ 1 and y = csc⁻¹ x for x ≤ ‑1.
Sketch the graph of y = cot⁻¹ x, indicating domain, range, intercepts, and asymptotes. (4 marks)
A pendulum’s angular displacement θ (in radians) satisfies sin θ = 0.6. Use the graph of y = sin⁻¹ x to estimate θ and discuss the principal value.

(a) Sketch the graph of y = cot⁻¹ x, showing domain, range, intercepts, and asymptotes. (3 marks) (b) State the domain and range of cot⁻¹ x. (1 mark) (c) Find the x‑coordinate of the point where the graph crosses the line y = π/4. (1 mark)

A surveyor measures the angle of elevation to the top of a tower from two points A and B on level ground, 100 m apart. From A the angle is \( \tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4} \); from B it is \( \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{2} \). Assuming the tower stands on the line AB, find the height of the tower.
State the formula for sin⁻¹x + sin⁻¹y when x² + y² ≤ 1.
Explain why the condition x² + y² ≤ 1 is sufficient (but not necessary) for the sum sin⁻¹x+sin⁻¹y to lie in the principal branch without adding π.

A ladder 10 m long rests against a vertical wall. The foot of the ladder is pulled away from the wall at 0.5 m/s. Let \(\theta\) be the angle between the ladder and the ground. **(a)** Express \(\theta\) as an inverse trigonometric function of \(x\), the distance of the foot from the wall. **(b)** Find \(\frac{d\theta}{dt}\) when \(x = 6\) m. **(c)** Interpret the sign of your answer.

**ISC 2022 pattern:** If \(y = \arctan\left(\frac{1-x}{1+x}\right)\), find \(\frac{dy}{dx}\). **(a)** Simplify the expression using an appropriate substitution. **(b)** Differentiate the simplified form. **(c)** State the final derivative and its domain.

(a) Derive the formula for sin⁻¹x + sin⁻¹y, stating the condition under which no π‑adjustment is required. (b) Extend the result to three terms: write sin⁻¹x + sin⁻¹y + sin⁻¹z as a single inverse sine, indicating the necessary constraints on x, y, z. (c) For x = 0.6, y = 0.8, determine whether the sum sin⁻¹x + sin⁻¹y lies in the principal branch; if not, give the corrected value.
Solve for x: tan⁻¹(x) + tan⁻¹(1/x) = π/2, x > 0.

Consider the equation sin⁻¹(x) + sin⁻¹(y) = π/2. (a) Show that x² + y² = 1. (b) Determine the number of solutions (x,y) in the domain [−1,1]×[−1,1]. (c) Discuss whether the identity sin⁻¹(x) + sin⁻¹(y) = sin⁻¹(x√(1−y²)+y√(1−x²)) holds for these solutions.
Solve for x: cos⁻¹(x) − sin⁻¹(x) = π/6. (Typical ISC 2023 pattern)
What is the order of the matrix \(M = \begin{bmatrix}5 & -2 & 0\\ 1 & 3 & 7\end{bmatrix}\)?

In an ISC 2023 paper, a question asked: “If \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 0\\1 & 3\end{bmatrix}\), find \(AB\) and \(BA\). Are they equal?” Solve and comment.

**APPLICATION:** A school stores marks of 3 students in 4 subjects as a matrix \(M\) of order \(3 \times 4\). The principal wants the average mark per subject across all students. Describe how to obtain a \(1 \times 4\) row matrix of averages using matrix operations (no programming loops). Assume a column matrix \(W\) of appropriate order exists.

**EVALUATION/CRITIQUE (multi-part):** (a) A student claims that for any two matrices \(A\) and \(B\) of the same order, \((A+B)^T = A^T + B^T\). Is this always true? Justify. (2 marks) (b) The same student says \((AB)^T = A^T B^T\) for any conformable \(A, B\). Is this correct? Provide a counterexample if false. (3 marks) (c) State the correct transpose rule for a product and explain why the order reverses. (2 marks)

**COMPARISON (multi-part):** Compare the following pairs of matrices in terms of (i) order, (ii) symmetry property, (iii) invertibility. \(X = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1\\-1 & 3\end{bmatrix}\) and \(Y = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 4\\-4 & 0\end{bmatrix}\). (a) Order comparison. (1 mark) (b) Symmetry classification. (2 marks) (c) Determinant and invertibility. (2 marks)

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN (multi-part):** In an ISC 2022 question, matrix \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 0\\1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\) were given. (a) Compute \(AB\) and \(BA\). (3 marks) (b) Verify whether \(AB = BA\). (1 mark) (c) Find \((AB)^T\) and compare with \(B^T A^T\). (3 marks) (d) If \(C = A + B\), find \(C^T\) and check if \(C^T = A^T + B^T\). (2 marks)
Given \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\4 & 5 & 6\end{bmatrix}\), state its order and the element \(a_{23}\).
If a matrix has 12 elements, list all possible orders it can have.
**HOTS:** A matrix \(A\) has order \(p \times q\). Its transpose \(A^T\) has order \(q \times p\). If \(A\) has 20 elements and \(p > q\), find all possible ordered pairs \((p,q)\).

**APPLICATION:** A spreadsheet contains data in 5 rows and 7 columns. Represent this as a matrix order and state the total number of cells. If a new column is inserted, what is the new order and new total?
**COMPARISON:** Compare the order of a row matrix and a column matrix that each contain 12 elements. How do their orders differ, and what does this imply for addition?

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** (a) Define the order of a matrix. (b) A square matrix has 24 elements. Find its order. (c) Explain why a \(3 \times 4\) matrix cannot be added to a \(4 \times 3\) matrix.

Which of the following matrices is a row matrix? A) \(\begin{bmatrix}2\\5\\-1\end{bmatrix}\) B) \(\begin{bmatrix}3 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}\) C) \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\) D) \(\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0\\0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\)
Explain why the matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}5 & 0\\0 & 5\end{bmatrix}\) is both a scalar matrix and an identity matrix multiplied by 5.
Given \(B = \begin{bmatrix}0 & -2 & 5\\2 & 0 & -3\\-5 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix}\), verify whether \(B\) is skew‑symmetric.

In an ISC 2023 paper, a question asked: “If \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix}0 & -1\\1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\), identify the type of each matrix.” Write the expected answer.

**CISCE past‑paper pattern (multi-part):** In an ISC 2022 question, a matrix \(X = \begin{bmatrix}a & b\\c & d\end{bmatrix}\) is given to be both symmetric and skew‑symmetric. (i) Write the conditions on \(a,b,c,d\). (ii) Solve for \(a,b,c,d\). (iii) State the resulting matrix.
Given \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 4 \\ 5 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\), verify the commutative property \(A+B = B+A\) by explicit calculation.

If \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 \end{bmatrix}\), and \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 9 & 10 \\ 11 & 12 \end{bmatrix}\), evaluate \((A+B)+C\) and \(A+(B+C)\) to illustrate associativity.
Solve for the matrix \(X\) in the equation \( \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} + X = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 5 \\ -2 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \).
Construct two different \(2\times2\) matrices \(P\) and \(Q\) such that \(P+Q = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\) but neither \(P\) nor \(Q\) is the zero matrix.

An ISC 2023 question: If \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & x \\ y & -2 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 4 \\ 5 & 6 \end{bmatrix}\) satisfy \(A+B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 9 \\ 8 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\), find \(x\) and \(y\).

**APPLICATION:** A school stores marks of two sections in matrices \(S_1 = \begin{bmatrix} 78 & 85 & 90 \\ 65 & 70 & 75 \end{bmatrix}\) (Section A) and \(S_2 = \begin{bmatrix} 82 & 88 & 92 \\ 68 & 73 & 78 \end{bmatrix}\) (Section B), where rows are subjects (Math, Science) and columns are students (1,2,3). Compute the total marks matrix \(T = S_1 + S_2\) and find the average marks per student across both sections.

**EVALUATION/CRITIQUE:** A student solves \( \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix} + X = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 \end{bmatrix} \) by writing \(X = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 8 \\ 10 & 12 \end{bmatrix}\). Critique the solution and provide the correct answer.

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN (multi‑part):** (a) If \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 4 \\ 5 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\), find \(A+B\). (2 marks) (b) Verify that \((A+B)+A = A+(B+A)\) for the above matrices. (3 marks) (c) Find a matrix \(X\) such that \(A+X = O\) (the zero matrix of order \(2\times2\)). (2 marks)
Compute the product of \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix}5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8\end{bmatrix}\).
If \(A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 4 & -2\end{bmatrix}\), find \(AB\) and \(BA\). Comment on whether \(AB = BA\).

A transformation is represented by matrix \(M = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\) applied to vector \(v = \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}\). (a) Find \(Mv\). (b) If \(M\) is applied twice, find \(M^2 v\). (c) Interpret geometrically what \(M\) does.

(a) If \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\), find \(AB\) and \(BA\). (2 marks) (b) Verify that \((AB)^T = B^T A^T\). (2 marks) (c) If \(C = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\), find \(AC\) and \(CA\). (1 mark)
What is the result of multiplying a 2 × 3 matrix by the scalar 0?
If \(A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}\) and \(k = -2\), compute \(kA\) and explain why each entry changes sign and magnitude.
Given \(B = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6\end{bmatrix}\), find scalar \(k\) such that \(kB = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 & 6 \\ 8 & 10 & 12\end{bmatrix}\).
Construct a 2 × 2 matrix \(A\) and a scalar \(k\) such that \(kA = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\) but \(A \neq O\) and \(k \neq 0\). Explain why this is impossible.
Let \(A\) be a 2 × 2 matrix such that \(A^2 = O\) (zero matrix) but \(A \neq O\). Find a scalar \(k\) such that \((kA)^2 = O\). Discuss whether any non‑zero \(k\) works.

A school timetable is represented by a 5 × 6 matrix \(T\) where entry \(t_{ij} = 1\) if a class is scheduled in period \(i\) on day \(j\), else 0. The principal wants to simulate a double‑period schedule by scaling the matrix. Explain why scalar multiplication by 2 is not appropriate and propose a correct matrix operation.

(a) If \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}\), compute \(2A - 3B\). (b) Verify that \((2A - 3B)^T = 2A^T - 3B^T\). (c) State the property used in (b).
Given \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\4 & 5 & 6\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix}7 & 8\\9 & 10\\11 & 12\end{bmatrix}\), compute \((AB)^{T}\) and \(B^{T}A^{T}\) and confirm they are equal.
Create a \(3 \times 2\) matrix \(C\) such that \(C^{T}C\) is a diagonal matrix with entries 5 and 13 on the diagonal.
ISC 2023 style: If \(A = \begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta & -\sin\theta\\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta\end{bmatrix}\), prove that \(A^{T}A = I_{2}\) for all \(\theta\).
**CISCE Past‑Paper Pattern:** (a) If \(A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 3\\ 1 & 4\end{bmatrix}\), find \(A^{T}A\). (b) Show that \((A^{T}A)^{T}=A^{T}A\). (c) What does this imply about the matrix \(A^{T}A\)?
If \(A\) is a skew‑symmetric matrix of order 3, what are the possible values of its diagonal entries?
Given \(A = \begin{bmatrix}4 & -2 & 5\\ 1 & 3 & -4\\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{bmatrix}\), find its symmetric part \(S\) and skew‑symmetric part \(K\). Verify \(A = S+K\).
Create a 2 × 2 matrix that is neither symmetric nor skew‑symmetric, then decompose it into symmetric and skew‑symmetric parts.
ISC 2023 style: If \(A\) is a square matrix such that \(A + A^{\mathsf{T}} = 0\), prove that \(A\) is skew‑symmetric and deduce the value of \(\operatorname{tr}(A)\).

**APPLICATION:** A 2 × 2 symmetric matrix \(S = \begin{bmatrix}a & b\\ b & c\end{bmatrix}\) represents the quadratic form \(Q(x,y) = ax^2 + 2bxy + cy^2\). Find conditions on \(a,b,c\) for \(Q\) to be positive definite.

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** (a) Show that the matrix \(A = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 & -2\\ -1 & 0 & 3\\ 2 & -3 & 0\end{bmatrix}\) is skew‑symmetric. (b) Find a symmetric matrix \(S\) and a skew‑symmetric matrix \(K\) such that \(A = S + K\). (c) Verify that \(S\) and \(K\) are unique.
A \(3\times3\) matrix \(P\) has determinant 5. After performing the operation \(R_2 \rightarrow 4R_2\) on \(P\), what is the determinant of the resulting matrix?
Given \(A = \begin{pmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\0 & 1 & 4\\5 & 6 & 0\end{pmatrix}\), determine if \(A\) is invertible. If yes, find \(A^{-1}\) using elementary row operations.

**HOTS:** (a) Prove that for any 3×3 matrix \(A\), \(\det(A^T)=\det(A)\). (b) Using this, explain why the determinant of a symmetric matrix equals the determinant of its transpose. (c) If a symmetric matrix has determinant zero, what does it imply about its eigenvalues? **MARKS:** (a) 2, (b) 1, (c) 2

**APPLICATION:** A 3×3 matrix \(M\) represents the transformation from coordinates in a robot arm’s base frame to its end‑effector frame. If \(\det(M)=0.5\), what does this tell you about the transformation’s effect on volume? If the robot picks up a cube of side 2 cm, what is the volume of the transformed shape? **MARKS:** 3

**EVALUATION/CRITIQUE:** (a) A textbook states “The adjoint of a matrix is always invertible.” Critique this statement. (b) Provide a counterexample using a 2×2 singular matrix. (c) State the correct condition for the adjoint to be invertible. **MARKS:** (a) 2, (b) 2, (c) 1

**COMPARISON:** Compare the matrix method \(X=A^{-1}B\) and Cramer’s rule for solving a 3×3 system \(AX=B\). Discuss (a) computational efficiency, (b) applicability when \(\det(A)=0\), (c) numerical stability. **MARKS:** (a) 2, (b) 2, (c) 2

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** (a) If \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\0&1&4\\5&6&0\end{pmatrix}\), compute \(\det(A)\). (b) Find \(\operatorname{adj}(A)\). (c) Hence write \(A^{-1}\). (d) Solve \(AX=\begin{pmatrix}6\\8\\10\end{pmatrix}\) using the matrix method. **MARKS:** (a) 2, (b) 3, (c) 1, (d) 2
Explain why the determinant of the identity matrix \(I_3\) is 1.
Compute the determinant of \(\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 & 0 \\ 3 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -2\end{bmatrix}\).
If each element of a 3×3 matrix *A* is multiplied by 2, what is |2*A*| in terms of |*A*|?
Evaluate whether the following statement is true: “If |*A*| = 0 for a 3×3 matrix *A*, then *A* must have two identical rows.”
Given |*A*| = 5 for a 3×3 matrix *A*, find |*A*<sup>T</sup>| and |*A*⁻¹| (assuming *A* is invertible).
Create a 3×3 matrix *B* (with integer entries) such that |*B*| = 0 but no two rows are identical and no row is a scalar multiple of another.
**Comparison:** Compare the effect on the determinant of (i) swapping two rows, (ii) multiplying a row by –1, (iii) adding –1 times row 1 to row 2.

**CISCE past‑paper pattern (multi‑part):** Given the matrix \[ P = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 & 3\\ 4 & 0 & 6\\ 1 & 2 & -1 \end{pmatrix}, \] (a) Use row operations to convert *P* to an upper‑triangular matrix *U*, stating the effect of each operation on the determinant. (b) Hence write |*P*| in terms of the diagonal entries of *U*. (c) Compute the numerical value of |*P*|.
Write the matrix equation **AX = B** for the system: 3x – 2y = 5 ; 4x + y = 6.
Solve the system using the matrix method: x + 2y = 3 3x – y = 4
Construct a 2×2 linear system whose unique solution is (x, y) = (2, -3) and whose coefficient matrix has determinant 5.
(CISCE exam style) For the system 2x + y – z = 1 x – y + 2z = 3 3x + 2y + z = 4 (a) Write the matrix equation **AX = B**. (b) Find |A|. (c) State whether a unique solution exists.

(HOTS) For the system x + 2y + 3z = 9 2x + 3y + z = 8 3x + y + 2z = 7 (a) Find |A|. (b) Compute **A⁻¹**. (c) Solve for (x, y, z). (d) Discuss what would happen if the third equation were replaced by 6x + 2y + 4z = 14.
(Application) A shop sells pens and notebooks. 3 pens + 2 notebooks cost ₹ 80; 5 pens + 3 notebooks cost ₹ 130. Form the matrix equation and find the price of one pen and one notebook.

(CISCE past‑paper pattern) Given the system x + y + z = 6 x + 2y + 3z = 14 x + 4y + 9z = 36 (a) Write the coefficient matrix **A** and find its determinant. (b) Using the matrix method, solve for x, y, z. (c) Verify the solution by substituting into the third equation.
State the value of \(\det\begin{pmatrix}2 & 0 & 1\\ 0 & 3 & 0\\ 4 & 0 & 5\end{pmatrix}\) without full expansion.
An ISC 2022 question: “Solve the system \(x+2y+3z=6,\; 2x+3y+z=4,\; 3x+y+2z=5\) by the matrix method.” Outline the steps and give the solution.

(Application) A triangular plot of land has vertices at \((0,0), (a,0), (0,b)\) with \(a,b>0\). The municipal authority requires the area to be at least 200 sq. m. Using the determinant area formula, derive the condition on \(a\) and \(b\). If \(a=20\) m, find the minimum integer \(b\).

(CISCE past‑paper pattern) The following question appeared in ISC 2021: “Given \(A = \begin{pmatrix}1 & 2 & -1\\ 2 & 1 & 2\\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{pmatrix}\), find \(A^{-1}\) and hence solve the system \(x+2y-z=3,\; 2x+y+2z=1,\; -x+2y+z=2\).” (a) Compute \(\det(A)\). (b) Find \(\operatorname{adj}(A)\). (c) Write \(A^{-1}\). (d) Solve for \(x,y,z\). Provide marks allocation as per ISC scheme (total 6 marks).
A CISCE ISC 2023 paper asked: “If \(f(x)=\begin{cases}ax^2+b,&x\le1\\2x+3,&x>1\end{cases}\) is differentiable at \(x=1\), find \(a\) and \(b\).” Solve it.
ISC 2023 style: (a) Differentiate \(y = \sqrt{\sin(2x+3)}\). (b) Hence find the value of \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) at \(x = \frac{\pi}{6}\).
**APPLICATION:** The temperature \(T\) (in °C) of a cooling object follows \(T(t) = 20 + 80 e^{-0.05 t}\) where \(t\) is minutes. Find the rate of temperature change at \(t = 10\) min.
What is the derivative dy/dx of the relation x² + y² = 16 obtained by implicit differentiation?
Explain why the chain rule must be applied to y² when differentiating x² + y² = 25 implicitly with respect to x.
Find the equation of the tangent to the curve x² + xy + y² = 7 at the point (1,2).

A CISCE ISC 2023 question: If x^2 + y^2 = a^2, prove that (1 + (dy/dx)^2)^(3/2) = a^2 / |y^3|. (This is a multi-part question: (a) find dy/dx, (b) compute 1+(dy/dx)^2, (c) simplify to the given expression.)

Application: A ladder 10 m long rests against a vertical wall. The bottom slides away at 0.5 m/s. How fast does the top slide down when the bottom is 6 m from the wall? Use implicit differentiation on x^2 + y^2 = 100.

Evaluation/Critique: A student claims that for the curve x^2 + y^2 = 4, the second derivative d^2y/dx^2 = - (y^2 + x^2)/y^3. (a) Verify the first derivative. (b) Compute the second derivative correctly. (c) Identify the error in the student's expression.
Comparison: Compare implicit differentiation of x^2 + y^2 = 25 and parametric differentiation of x = 5 cos t, y = 5 sin t. Show both yield the same dy/dx at a given point.
CISCE past-paper pattern: (a) If x^2 + y^2 = a^2, prove that y d^2y/dx^2 + (dy/dx)^2 + 1 = 0. (b) Hence find the radius of curvature at any point (x,y) on the circle.
Evaluate the derivative of y = arctan(3x²) at x = 1.
An ISC 2023 paper asks: “If sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2, prove that d/dx(sin⁻¹x) = ‑d/dx(cos⁻¹x).” Provide the proof.
**HOTS:** Prove that for x > 0, d/dx[tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹(1/x)] = 0, and explain the geometric meaning.

**APPLICATION:** A camera tracks a rocket launched vertically. The camera is 1 km from the launch pad. If the rocket’s height is h km, the camera angle θ satisfies tan θ = h. Find dθ/dt when h = 2 km and dh/dt = 0.5 km/s.
**EVALUATION/CRITIQUE:** A textbook states: “The derivative of sec⁻¹x is 1/(x√(x²‑1)) for all x ≠ 0.” Critique this statement.
Find the derivative of *g*(*x*) = 3 *e*^{2*x*} at *x* = 1.
Create a function *h*(*x*) whose derivative is *h*′(*x*) = 5 *h*(*x*).
**HOTS:** Suppose *f*(*x*) = *a*^{*g*(*x*)} where *g* is differentiable and *a* > 0, *a* ≠ 1. Prove that *f*′(*x*)/*f*(*x*) = *g*′(*x*) ln *a*.
**Application:** The population *P* (in thousands) of a city follows *P*(*t*) = 200 *e*^{0.03 t}, *t* in years. Find the year when the instantaneous growth rate reaches 9 thousand per year.
**CISCE past-paper pattern:** (a) Differentiate *y* = 3^{2*x*+1} with respect to *x*. (b) Hence find the equation of the tangent to the curve *y* = 3^{2*x*+1} at the point where *x* = 0.
Explain why the derivative of \( \ln x \) is \( 1/x \) using the fact that \( \ln x \) and \( e^x \) are inverse functions.
Find the derivative of \( f(x) = \ln(3x^2 + 5) \) at \( x = 1 \).
Differentiate \( y = \log_3(5x^2 + 2) \) with respect to \( x \). (CISCE exam style)
**Application:** Find the equation of the tangent to the curve \( y = \ln(x^2+1) \) at \( x = 1 \).

**Evaluation/Critique:** (a) A student says “The function \( f(x) = \ln|x| \) is differentiable for all \( x \neq 0 \).” Is this true? (b) Is the derivative \( f'(x) = 1/x \) for all \( x \neq 0 \)? (c) Explain any discrepancy between the domain of \( f \) and the formula for \( f' \).

**CISCE past-paper pattern:** (a) Differentiate \( y = \log_2(3x+4) \) with respect to \( x \). (b) Hence find the value of \( x \) for which \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 1 \). (c) Verify that the function is increasing for all \( x \) in its domain.
A CISCE ISC 2023 paper asks: “If \(y = x^{x^x}\), find \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) using logarithmic differentiation.” Outline the steps and give the final expression.
Given x = t² + 1, y = t³ – 3t, find dy/dx at t = 1.
Find the slope of the tangent to the curve x = 2 cos θ, y = 3 sin θ at θ = π/4.

**APPLICATION:** A projectile is launched with parametric equations x = 20t, y = 20t – 5t² (distances in metres, t in seconds). Find the angle of projection (the slope at t = 0) and the time when the projectile reaches its maximum height.

**COMPARISON:** Compare the process of finding dy/dx for the circle x² + y² = 25 using (i) implicit differentiation and (ii) parametric differentiation with x = 5 cos θ, y = 5 sin θ. Discuss any differences in the final expression and domain restrictions.
What are the four main applications of derivatives covered in ISC Class 12 Chapter 6?
A student claims that any point where f′(x) = 0 is automatically a maximum or minimum. Evaluate this claim.
Find the equation of the tangent to the curve y = x² − 4x + 3 at x = 2.
An ISC 2023 paper asked: “If the radius of a sphere increases at 0.2 cm/s, find the rate of increase of its volume when r = 5 cm.” Identify the derivative concept used and write the formula.

A function f(x) = x⁴ − 4x³ + 6x² − 4x + 1 is given. (a) Find f′(x) and f″(x). (b) Determine all critical points and classify each using the second derivative test. (c) State the intervals of increase and decrease.

A rectangular sheet of metal 30 cm × 20 cm has squares of side x cm cut from each corner and the flaps folded to form an open box. (a) Write the volume V(x) of the box. (b) Find the value of x that maximises V. (c) Verify that this x gives a maximum.

Consider the curve y = x³ − 3x + 2. (a) Find the equation of the tangent at the point where the curve crosses the y‑axis. (b) Find the coordinates of the point where this tangent meets the curve again. (c) Determine the area of the triangle formed by this tangent, the x‑axis, and the y‑axis.

ISC 2022 Question: “The radius of a circular ripple in a pond increases at a constant rate of 3 cm/s. How fast is the area increasing when the radius is 10 cm?” (a) Write the relationship between area A and radius r. (b) Differentiate with respect to time t. (c) Compute dA/dt at r=10 cm.

**Application:** Water is poured into an inverted conical tank (vertex down) of height 12 m and top radius 4 m at a rate of 2 m³/min. How fast is the water level rising when the water is 6 m deep? **Given:** Volume of cone \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). By similar triangles, \(r/h = 4/12 = 1/3\) → \(r = h/3\).

**Evaluation/Critique:** A solution to “Find the rate of change of \(y=\sqrt{x}\) at \(x=4\)” writes: “Average rate from 4 to 5 is \(\frac{\sqrt{5}-2}{1}\approx0.236\), so the instantaneous rate is 0.236.” Critique this solution.

**CISCE Past‑Paper Pattern (Multi‑part):** A particle moves along the curve \(y = x^2 - 4x + 5\). At the instant when \(x = 3\), the \(x\)-coordinate is increasing at 2 units/s. (a) Find the rate of change of the \(y\)-coordinate at that instant. (b) Determine the speed of the particle at that instant. (c) If the particle continues with the same \(dx/dt\), will the speed increase, decrease, or stay the same as \(x\) increases beyond 3? Justify.
Find the dimensions of a rectangle with perimeter 40 cm that maximises its area.
An ISC 2023 question: “If \(y = \sqrt{x}\), find the approximate value of \(\sqrt{0.082}\) using differentials.” Provide the solution with steps.

**EVALUATION/CRITIQUE:** A student solves an ISC problem: “Find the approximate value of \((1.999)^5\) using differentials.” The student chooses \(f(x)=x^5\), \(a=2\), \(dx=-0.001\) and computes \(dy = 5(2)^4(-0.001) = -0.08\). Approximation = \(32 - 0.08 = 31.92\). The student writes: “Since \(dx\) is negative, the approximation is less than the exact value.” Critique this statement and provide the correct reasoning.

(Application) The volume \(V\) of a spherical balloon changes with radius \(r\) as \(V(r)=\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). If the radius increases from 5 cm to 7 cm, use LMVT to show that at some radius the rate of change of volume with respect to radius equals the average rate of change. Find that radius.
(CISCE past‑paper pattern) (a) Verify Lagrange’s Mean Value Theorem for \(f(x)=\sin x\) on \([0,\pi]\). (b) Hence prove that \(\sin x < x\) for all \(x>0\). (Marks: 3+2)
Find the equation of the tangent to the curve y = x² + 2x at the point where x = 1.
**APPLICATION** A cylindrical tank of radius 2 m is being filled with water at a constant rate of 0.5 m³/min. How fast is the water level rising when the depth of water is 3 m?

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN** (a) Find the coordinates of the point on the curve y = x² where the tangent is parallel to the line y = 4x + 1. (2 marks) (b) Find the equation of the normal to the curve at that point. (2 marks) (c) Calculate the area of the triangle formed by this tangent, the normal, and the x‑axis. (3 marks)
Consider f(x) = sin x on [0, π]. (a) Find the indefinite integral ∫ sin x dx. (b) Evaluate the definite integral ∫₀^π sin x dx. (c) Explain the geometric meaning of the result in (b).
A car’s velocity is given by v(t) = 4t m/s for t in seconds. Find the distance travelled in the first 3 seconds using a definite integral.
Critique the use of a left Riemann sum with n = 4 to approximate ∫₀¹ eˣ dx. Compute the approximation and compare with the exact value.

ISC 2023 style: (a) State the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. (b) Evaluate ∫₀² (3x² – 2x + 1) dx. (c) Use the property ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = ∫ₐᵇ f(a+b–x) dx to show that ∫₀^π x sin x dx = (π/2) ∫₀^π sin x dx.
Write the indefinite integral of f(x) = 7x⁴ – 3/x + 2eˣ with respect to x.
ISC 2023 style: Evaluate ∫(3x² + 2/x – 4sin x) dx.
(HOTS) Determine ∫(x³ + 2x)/√(x⁴ + 4x² + 5) dx by identifying a suitable standard form after algebraic manipulation.
(CISCE past-paper pattern) (a) Evaluate ∫(2x³ – 3/x + 4cos x) dx. (b) Hence find the value of the constant k if the curve y = ∫(2x³ – 3/x + 4cos x) dx passes through (1, k) and has y-intercept 5.
Design a definite integral of a simple polynomial that equals 5.
Evaluate ∫_1^2 (2x + 3/x) dx. Show all steps.
(HOTS) A function f is continuous on [0, 2] and satisfies ∫_0^2 f(x) dx = 5. Define g(x) = ∫_0^x f(t) dt. Find g'(1) and explain your reasoning.
(Application) The velocity of a particle moving along a line is v(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9 m/s for t ∈ [0, 4]. Find the displacement and the total distance travelled in the first 4 seconds.

(Comparison) Compare the evaluation of ∫_0^1 x^2 dx using (i) the limit of Riemann sums with right endpoints, and (ii) the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. Discuss the relative efficiency and the conceptual insight each method provides.
A CISCE ISC 2023 question: “If \(F(x)=\int_0^x (t^3-2t)\,dt\), find \(F'(2)\).”

**APPLICATION:** The rate of water flow into a tank is \(r(t)=10-2t\) litres/minute for \(0\le t\le5\). Write an expression for the volume \(V(t)\) of water in the tank at time \(t\) if the tank initially contains 20 litres. Compute \(V(3)\).
**COMPARISON:** Compare the use of FTC Part 1 to evaluate \(\int_0^1 x^2\,dx\) with the Riemann sum definition. Which is more efficient and why?
**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** (a) State the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1). (b) Evaluate \(\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin x\,dx\). (c) If \(F(x)=\int_{1}^{x} \frac{\ln t}{t}\,dt\), find \(F'(e)\).
ISC 2022 style: (a) Prove ∫₀^π x f(sin x) dx = (π/2) ∫₀^π f(sin x) dx. (b) Hence evaluate ∫₀^π x sin³x dx.

**HOTS (Higher Order Thinking Skills):** (a) Prove that for any continuous f on [0, a], ∫₀^a f(x) dx = ∫₀^a f(a–x) dx. (2 marks) (b) Use this to evaluate ∫₀^π/2 (sin x)/(sin x + cos x) dx. (3 marks) (c) Generalise the result of (b) for ∫₀^π/2 (sinⁿ x)/(sinⁿ x + cosⁿ x) dx, n ∈ ℕ. (2 marks)

**Application:** A particle moves along the x‑axis with velocity v(t) = t² – 4t + 3 (m/s) for t ∈ [0, 4] s. (a) Find the displacement from t=0 to t=4 using additivity at the roots of v(t). (3 marks) (b) Find the total distance travelled in the same interval. (3 marks)

**Evaluation/Critique:** A textbook claims: “For any integrable f on [a,b], ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = ∫ₐᵇ f(a+b–x) dx. Therefore, if f is increasing, the integral is larger than if f is decreasing.” (a) Identify the logical flaw. (2 marks) (b) Provide a counterexample with a specific increasing f and decreasing g on [0,1] where the integrals are equal. (3 marks)

**Comparison:** Compare the use of additivity versus symmetry (King’s property) for evaluating ∫₀^π x f(sin x) dx. (a) Show how additivity alone cannot simplify this integral. (2 marks) (b) Show how King’s property reduces it to (π/2)∫₀^π f(sin x) dx. (3 marks) (c) Explain why King’s property is more powerful for integrals with linear factor x multiplied by a symmetric function. (2 marks)
**CISCE Past‑Paper Pattern (ISC 2023, 5 marks):** Evaluate ∫₀^π/2 (x sin x cos x)/(sin⁴ x + cos⁴ x) dx.
A student computes the area between \(y=x^2\) and \(y=x\) from \(0\) to \(2\) as \(\int_0^2 (x^2-x)\,dx = -\frac23\). Evaluate the error.
A student writes ∫₀¹ (1/x) dx = [ln|x|]₀¹ = ln1−ln0 = 0−(−∞)=∞. Evaluate the correctness of this solution.
A particle moves along a straight line with velocity v(t) = 3t² − 2t + 1 m/s. Find its displacement from t=0 s to t=2 s.
State the definite integral that represents the area under the curve y = f(x) from x = a to x = b, assuming f(x) ≥ 0 on [a, b].
A student writes the area between y = sin x and y = cos x on [0, π/2] as ∫₀^{π/2} (sin x – cos x) dx. Evaluate this setup.
Find the area of the region bounded by y = x², y = 0, x = 1, and x = 3.
An ISC 2023 paper asked: “Find the area of the region bounded by the curve y = 4 – x² and the x‑axis.” Write the integral and compute the area.

**HOTS:** A region R is bounded by y = eˣ, y = e⁻ˣ, and the line x = 1. (a) Sketch R and determine whether vertical or horizontal slicing is simpler. (b) Set up the integral(s) for the area of R. (c) Evaluate the area.

**APPLICATION:** A farmer wants to fence a plot of land bounded by the river (modelled by y = 4 – x² for x ≥ 0) and the straight road along the x‑axis from x = 0 to x = 2. Find the area of the plot to estimate the amount of grass seed needed (1 kg per 10 m²). Give the seed required in kg.

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** (a) Find the area bounded by the curve y = x³ – 3x² + 2x and the x‑axis. (b) Hence, or otherwise, find the area between this curve and the line y = x – 1 on the interval where they enclose a finite region.
A CISCE exam question: “The area bounded by the curve \(y = \sqrt{x}\), the x‑axis, and the line \(x = 9\) is?” Choose the correct option. Options: (A) 9 (B) 12 (C) 18 (D) 24

Two curves are given: \(y = x^{2}\) and \(y = 4-x^{2}\). (a) Find their points of intersection. (b) Set up the integral(s) for the area of the region enclosed by them. (c) Evaluate the area. (d) A student integrates \(\displaystyle \int_{-2}^{2} (x^{2}-(4-x^{2}))dx\) and gets 0. Identify the error.

A water tank is being filled at a rate \(r(t)=5+2\sin(\pi t/6)\) litres per minute, where \(t\) is time in minutes. (a) Determine the total volume of water added from \(t=0\) to \(t=12\) minutes. (b) If the tank initially contained 20 litres, find the volume at \(t=12\). (c) A student approximates the rate as constant \(r\approx5\) litres/min and computes the added volume as \(5\times12=60\) litres. Quantify the error in this approximation. (d) Explain why the sinusoidal term does not affect the net volume over a full period.
A student sets up the area between \(y = x^2\) and \(y = x\) from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 2\) as \(\int_0^2 (x^2 - x) \, dx\). Evaluate whether this setup is correct.
Find the area between the curves \(y = 4 - x^2\) and \(y = x + 2\).
Design a pair of curves that intersect at \(x = 0\) and \(x = 3\) such that the area between them equals 12 square units. Provide the equations and verify.
A farmer's land is bounded by the river \(y = x^2\) and the road \(y = 4 - x^2\). Find the area of the land between them.
Compare the process of finding area between two curves when integrating with respect to \(x\) versus with respect to \(y\). Illustrate with the curves \(x = y^2\) and \(x = 2 - y^2\).
A student writes the area between x = y^2 and x = 4 as ∫_{0}^{4} (√x − (−√x)) dx. Is this correct for horizontal strips? Explain.
Find the area of the region bounded by x = y^3, x = 0, and y = 2 using horizontal strips.
A past ISC paper asks: “Find the area of the region bounded by the curve x = 4 − y^2 and the y‑axis.” Set up the integral and compute the area.

(a) Find the area of the region bounded by x = y^3, x = 0, and y = 1. (b) If the same region is described using vertical strips, write the integral (do not evaluate). (c) Explain why the horizontal‑strip integral is simpler.

A farmer’s land is bounded by the river x = 4 − y^2 (for y ≥ 0) and the straight road x = 0 (the y‑axis). The farmer wants to plant crops on this land. Set up the integral for the area and compute it. If the crop yield is 50 kg per square unit, find the total yield.

Consider the region bounded by x = y^2 and x = 2 − y^2. (a) Find the y‑coordinates of intersection. (b) Set up the horizontal‑strip integral for the area. (c) Evaluate the integral. (d) If a student mistakenly uses vertical strips and writes ∫_{0}^{1} (√x − (−√x)) dx + ∫_{1}^{2} (√(2−x) − (−√(2−x))) dx, explain why this gives the same area but is more work.
Compare the effort required to find the area between x = y^2 and x = 4 using horizontal strips versus vertical strips. Which method would you recommend for an ISC exam and why?

An ISC 2023 paper question: “Find the area of the region bounded by the curve x = 2y − y^2 and the y‑axis.” (a) Find the points of intersection with the y‑axis. (b) Write the definite integral for the area using horizontal strips. (c) Evaluate the integral. (d) If the region is revolved about the y‑axis, write the integral for the volume (do not evaluate).
Given the curves \(x = y^2\) and \(x = 4 - y^2\), decide whether the area between them from \(y = -1\) to \(y = 1\) is correctly given by \(\int_{-1}^{1} [(4 - y^2) - y^2] \, dy\). Justify.
ISC 2023 style: The curves \(x = y^2\) and \(x = 2y\) enclose a region. (a) Find the points of intersection. (b) Set up the integral for the area using horizontal strips. (c) Evaluate the area.

**Application:** A swimming pool has a cross‑section shaped like the region between \(x = y^2\) and \(x = 4\) for \(y \in [-2, 2]\). If the pool is 10 m long (perpendicular to the cross‑section), find the volume of water it can hold.

**CISCE Past‑Paper Pattern:** The curves \(x = y^2\) and \(x = 4 - y^2\) enclose a region. (a) Find the points of intersection. (b) Sketch the region (describe in words). (c) Find the area of the region using horizontal strips. (d) Verify the area by using vertical strips (set up the integrals only, do not evaluate).
Explain why the horizontal‑strip method is preferred over vertical strips for the region bounded by x = y² and x = 4.
Evaluate the claim: "If the curves intersect at y = −1 and y = 2, the area between x = y² and x = y + 2 is ∫_{−1}^{2} (y² − (y + 2)) dy."
Find the area of the region bounded by x = y² and x = 2 − y².
A past ISC paper asks: "Find the area of the region bounded by the curve x = y² − 4 and the line x = 0." Solve it completely.

**APPLICATION:** A swimming pool has a cross‑section (vertical plane) bounded by the curves x = y² (left wall) and x = 6 − y² (right wall), with y measured in metres from the bottom (y = 0) to the water surface (y = 2). Find the cross‑sectional area of the water.
**COMPARISON:** Compare the horizontal‑strip and vertical‑strip methods for finding the area of the region bounded by x = y² and x = 4. Discuss advantages and disadvantages of each.

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** (Adapted from ISC 2022) Find the area of the region bounded by the curve x = 3y − y² and the y‑axis. (a) Find the points of intersection of the curve with the y‑axis. (b) Sketch the region (describe in words). (c) Set up the definite integral for the area using horizontal strips. (d) Evaluate the integral and give the area in square units.
A student sets up the integral for the area between x = y² and x = y + 2 using vertical strips (with respect to x). Evaluate whether this approach is correct and explain.
Find the area of the region bounded by x = y² and x = 4 using horizontal strips.

**APPLICATION:** A farmer's field is bounded by a straight canal (x = 2y) and a curved fence (x = y² + 1). The field extends from y = 1 to y = 3. Find the area of the field in square meters if 1 unit = 10 m.
**CISCE PAST-PAPER PATTERN:** (a) Find the area of the region bounded by the curves y² = 4ax and x² = 4ay, a > 0. (b) If a = 2, compute the numerical area.
(Application) A rectangular garden has a curved fence described by \(y = 4 - x^2\) (with \(y\) in metres) from \(x = -2\) to \(x = 2\). The ground is the \(x\)-axis. Find the area of the garden.

(Evaluation/Critique) A student claims: “To find the area between \(y = x^2\) and \(y = 2 - x^2\), I can just integrate \((2 - x^2) - x^2 = 2 - 2x^2\) from the intersection points.” Critique this statement and provide the correct area.
An ISC 2023 paper asked: “Find the integrating factor of the linear differential equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{2}{x}y = x^2\).” Write the integrating factor and explain the steps.

A tank initially contains 100 L of brine with 20 kg of salt. Fresh water enters at 5 L/min and the well‑mixed solution leaves at 5 L/min. Let \(S(t)\) be the amount of salt (kg) at time \(t\) (min). (a) Formulate the differential equation for \(S(t)\). (b) Solve for \(S(t)\). (c) Find the time when the salt amount drops to 5 kg.

ISC 2022 Question: “Solve the differential equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x+y+1}{x+y-1}\).” (a) Identify the type of equation. (b) Use an appropriate substitution to solve it. (c) Express the solution in implicit form.
A student writes the degree of \(\left(\frac{d^3y}{dx^3}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right) = 5\) as 2. Is this correct? Justify.
Construct a differential equation of order 2 and degree 3.

**Application:** The simple harmonic motion of a mass‑spring system is modeled by \(\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} + \omega^2 x = 0\). (a) State the order and degree. (b) If a damping force proportional to velocity is added, the equation becomes \(\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} + 2\beta\frac{dx}{dt} + \omega^2 x = 0\). State the order and degree of the damped equation. (c) Explain why the degree remains 1 in both cases.
**Evaluation/Critique:** A student claims, “All first‑order differential equations have degree 1.” Critique this statement with examples.

**CISCE Past‑Paper Pattern:** (a) Write the order and degree of \(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = 0\). (b) For the differential equation \(\left(\frac{d^3y}{dx^3}\right)^2 + \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\), state whether the degree is defined. (c) Construct a differential equation of order 2 and degree 4.
Solve the initial‑value problem \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 e^{-y},\; y(0)=\ln 2 \). Give the particular solution in explicit form.
An ISC 2023 paper asked: “Solve \( \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y\cos x}{1+\sin x} \) given \(y(0)=1\).” Write the complete solution as expected in the board answer script.
Create a homogeneous differential equation of degree 3 whose general solution is \(x^{3}+y^{3}=Cxy\).
A CISCE ISC 2023 paper asked: “Solve \(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{x+y}{x-y}\).” Outline the complete solution steps and give the final implicit relation.

ISC 2022 Question: “Solve the differential equation \((x^{2}+y^{2})dx-2xy\,dy=0\) and find the particular solution passing through \((1,1)\).” (a) Write the equation in the form \(\frac{dy}{dx}=f(y/x)\). (b) Perform the substitution \(y=vx\) and separate variables. (c) Integrate and apply the initial condition to obtain the particular solution. (d) State the domain of the particular solution.

Create a first‑order linear differential equation that models a population \(P(t)\) growing at a rate proportional to its size with a constant immigration of 500 individuals per year. Write the equation and solve it for \(P(0)=1000\).
An ISC 2023 paper asked: “Find the integrating factor of \(\frac{dy}{dx}+ \frac{y}{x} = \sin x\).” Write the integrating factor and the general solution.

**CISCE Past‑Paper Pattern (2022):** (a) Find the integrating factor of \(\frac{dy}{dx}+ \frac{2}{x}y = x^2\). (b) Hence solve the differential equation given \(y(1)=2\). (c) Determine the value of \(y\) when \(x=2\).
State the condition for a differential equation M(x,y)dx + N(x,y)dy = 0 to be exact.
Given M = 3x²y + 2y and N = x³ + 2x, determine whether the DE M dx + N dy = 0 is exact.
Solve the exact DE: (2x + y)dx + (x - 3y²)dy = 0.
Solve the differential equation: (2xy + y²)dx + (x² + 2xy)dy = 0. (CISCE exam‑style)
Consider the DE (ax + by)dx + (bx + cy)dy = 0. (a) Find the relationship between a, b, c for the DE to be exact. (b) Hence solve the DE for a=2, b=3, c=4.
The rate of change of a chemical concentration is modeled by (2x + y)dx + (x - 3y²)dy = 0. Find the general solution and interpret the constant of integration in context.
A student claims that the DE (x² + y²)dx + 2xy dy = 0 is not exact because M and N are not symmetric. Critique this reasoning and provide the correct analysis.
Solve the differential equation: (x² + y²)dx + 2xy dy = 0. (a) Show that the DE is exact. (b) Find the general solution. (c) Find the particular solution given y(1) = 2. (CISCE past‑paper pattern)

Compare the solution behaviours of the following two models for the same physical situation: Model A (linear): \(\displaystyle \frac{dT}{dt}=-k(T-T_{s})\) Model B (Bernoulli, \(n=2\)): \(\displaystyle \frac{dT}{dt}=-k(T-T_{s})^{2}\) where \(T\) is temperature, \(T_{s}\) is surrounding temperature, and \(k>0\). Discuss how the time to reach within 1 % of \(T_{s}\) differs between the models.
An ISC 2022 question: “Solve \((x+y)\frac{dy}{dx}=x-y\) given \(y(0)=1\).” Identify the type, solve, and write the particular solution.

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN (multi‑part):** The 2021 ISC paper included: “(a) Show that the differential equation \((x^2-y^2)dx+2xy\,dy=0\) is exact. (b) Solve it. (c) Find the particular solution satisfying \(y(1)=2\).” Answer all parts.
A drone flies 30 m east, then 40 m north. Represent the total displacement as a vector in component form and find its magnitude.
(a) Find the magnitude of \(\vec{w}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+12\hat{k}\). (b) Determine its direction cosines. (c) Verify that the sum of squares of the direction cosines equals 1.
**EVALUATION/CRITIQUE:** A student claims that a direction cosine can be greater than 1 because the component \(a_1\) can be larger than the magnitude \(|\vec{a}|\). Critique this statement.

**EVALUATION/CRITIQUE:** A student finds the unit vector along the position vector \(\vec{r}=6\hat{i}-8\hat{j}\) by writing \(\hat{u}=6\hat{i}-8\hat{j}\) and claims its magnitude is 1 because “the components are the direction cosines.” Critique this method.
A vector **a** has magnitude 13 and direction ratios 2, 3, 6. Find its scalar components.
Create a vector of magnitude 10 that makes equal angles with the three coordinate axes and write it in component form.
(ISC 2023 style) If **a** = 2**i** – **j** + 3**k** and **b** = **i** + 4**j** – 2**k**, find the scalar components of the vector **c** = 3**a** – 2**b**.

(HOTS) A vector **r** has direction cosines (l, m, n) satisfying l : m : n = 2 : –3 : 6. If the magnitude of **r** is 21, find its components and verify that the sum of squares of direction cosines equals 1.
(Application) A drone flies from point A(2, –1, 3) to point B(5, 4, –2). Express the displacement vector **AB** in component form, find its magnitude, and determine the direction cosines.
Evaluate the statement: “If **a·b = 0**, then either **a = 0** or **b = 0**.” Justify your answer.
Create a pair of non‑zero vectors in 3‑D whose dot product is 12 and whose magnitudes are 3 and 5 respectively. Show one possible pair.
ISC 2023 style: If **a = 2i – j + 3k** and **b = λi + 4j – 2k** are perpendicular, find λ. Hence find the projection of **a** on **b** when λ takes that value.

(HOTS) Let **a** and **b** be non‑zero vectors such that **|a + b| = |a – b|**. (a) Prove that **a·b = 0**. (b) If |a| = 5 and |b| = 12, find |a + b|. (c) Explain the geometric significance of the condition **|a + b| = |a – b|**.
If **a** × **b** = **0**, what can you conclude about the vectors **a** and **b**? Explain your reasoning.
A 10 N force acts on a block that moves 5 m east. If the force is directed 60° north of east, calculate the work done by the force.
A force vector **F** = (3 \(\hat{i}\) + 4 \(\hat{j}\)) N acts on an object that undergoes displacement **d** = (5 \(\hat{i}\) – 2 \(\hat{j}\)) m. Compute the work done.
Design a situation where a constant force of 20 N does exactly –40 J of work on an object. State the required displacement magnitude and its direction relative to the force.
A particle moves from point A(1,2,3) to B(4,6,9) under a constant force **F** = (2, –1, 3) N. Calculate the work done.

A force of magnitude 20 N acts at an angle of 120° to the displacement of 4 m. (a) Compute the work done. (b) State whether the force speeds up, slows down, or does not change the kinetic energy of the object, and justify.

A particle moves from (0,0,0) to (2,2,2) under a constant force **F** = (1, –2, 3) N. (a) Find the work done. (b) If the displacement were doubled while keeping the same force, what would be the new work?

A 50 N force pulls a sled 10 m horizontally. The rope makes an angle θ with the horizontal. (a) Derive an expression for work done as a function of θ. (b) Determine the angle at which the work done is half the maximum possible work. (c) Explain why work done cannot exceed the value obtained when θ=0°.

Compare the work done by a force **F** = (3, 4, 0) N acting on two different displacements: **d₁** = (6, 8, 0) m and **d₂** = (–6, –8, 0) m. Compute each work and discuss the physical meaning of the results.

A block of mass 2 kg is pushed across a frictionless floor by a constant force of 10 N applied at 30° to the horizontal. The block moves 5 m. (a) Calculate the work done by the applied force. (b) Using the work‑energy theorem, find the block’s final speed if it started from rest. (c) If the same force were applied vertically upward while the block moves horizontally, what would be the work done and the resulting speed?
Construct a non‑zero vector **c** such that its scalar projection onto \(\mathbf b = 2\mathbf i + \mathbf j\) is exactly 5 units.

A ramp of length 5 m is inclined at 30° to the horizontal. A box is pulled up the ramp with a force of 50 N applied at an angle of 10° above the ramp. Find the effective component of the force that does work in moving the box up the ramp.
Given a line passing through (2, −1, 3) with direction ratios (4, 5, −2), write its vector equation.
Two lines have direction cosines (1/√3, 1/√3, 1/√3) and (1/√2, 0, −1/√2). Find the angle between them.
A student claims that the Cartesian equation (x−1)/2 = (y+3)/−1 = (z−4)/5 represents a line with direction cosines (2, −1, 5). Evaluate this claim.

A line L₁ passes through (1, −2, 3) and has direction ratios (2, 1, −2). Another line L₂ passes through (4, 0, −1) and has direction ratios (4, 2, −4). (a) Show that L₁ and L₂ are parallel. (b) Find the shortest distance between them. (c) If a third line L₃ is perpendicular to both L₁ and L₂ and passes through the midpoint of the segment joining the given points on L₁ and L₂, write its vector equation.

ISC 2023 Paper Question (adapted): The lines L₁: **r** = (2**i** + 3**j** − **k**) + λ(**i** + 2**j** + 3**k**) and L₂: **r** = (4**i** − **j** + 2**k**) + μ(2**i** + **j** − **k**) are given.
