एक अपरिचित चित्र (जैसे: ग्रामीण कुएँ पर पानी भरती स्त्रियाँ) देखकर 1 मिनट में मौखिक वर्णन तैयार करने की रणनीति क्या होगी? चरणबद्ध बताएँ।
CISCE परीक्षा शैली: "निम्नलिखित चित्र का वर्णन लगभग 80 शब्दों में कीजिए।" — इस निर्देश में छिपी तीन प्रमुख अपेक्षाएँ कौन-सी हैं?

APPLICATION: कक्षा 7 के छात्रों को 'स्वच्छता अभियान' पर विद्यालय स्तरीय चित्र वर्णन प्रतियोगिता के लिए तैयार करना है। 3-सप्ताह की चरणबद्ध योजना बनाइए जिसमें प्रत्येक सप्ताह का लक्ष्य, गतिविधि और आकलन सूचक शामिल हो।

CISCE PAST-PAPER PATTERN: "निम्नलिखित चित्र को देखकर उसका वर्णन लगभग 100 शब्दों में कीजिए। चित्र: एक रेलवे स्टेशन का दृश्य — प्लेटफॉर्म पर भीड़, कुली सामान उठाए, गाड़ी आ रही है, घोषणा हो रही है, एक परिवार चिंतित खड़ा है।" — इस प्रश्न के लिए आदर्श उत्तर की रूपरेखा (outline) दीजिए जिसमें अंक-विभाजन भी हो।

परीक्षा-शैली: (क) संवाद-लेखन में भूमिका-पंक्ति का काम एक वाक्य में लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) चार भाषा-नियमों के नाम लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ग) बताइए कि 'निपटारा' कितने रूपों में हो सकता है — दो उदाहरण-वाक्य दीजिए। (2 अंक) (घ) निम्न उत्तर की त्रुटि पहचानिए — प्रश्न: 'संवाद में वारी-अनुशासन क्या है'; उत्तर: "वारी-अनुशासन से संवाद अच्छा बनता है और सबको शिष्टता आती है।" (1 अंक)

परीक्षा-प्रारूप प्रश्न: (क) संवाद के चार ढाँचा-अंगों के नाम क्रम से लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) 'वारी-अनुशासन' का अर्थ दो वाक्यों में लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ग) स्थिति: "स्थान: मोहल्ले की बहन-जी के घर; पात्र: रेखा (माँ) और बहन-जी; उद्देश्य: बच्चों के स्कूल-यात्रा के लिए एक दिन पड़ोस की देखभाल माँगना।" — पाँच आरोह-अवरोह का ढाँचा-नोट और पूर्ण संवाद (आठ-दस वाक्य) लिखिए। (4 अंक) (घ) मूल्यांकन कीजिए — "प्रीति कहती है: 'संवाद में मुझे जो अच्छा लगे वह लिख देती हूँ; उद्देश्य से क्या फ़र्क़ पड़ता है।'" (2 अंक) (च) यह नोड अगले कौशल 'वाद-विवाद' की तैयारी कैसे करता है — दो बिंदु। (2 अंक)
कक्षा 7 के लिए उपयुक्त वाद-विवाद विषय का चयन करते समय शिक्षक को किन दो बातों का ध्यान रखना चाहिए?
CISCE ICSE कक्षा 7 की परीक्षा में वाद-विवाद मूल्यांकन के लिए किस प्रकार का प्रश्न पूछा जा सकता है?
कक्षा 7 के छात्र को “पर्यावरण संरक्षण” विषय पर 2 मिनट का भाषण देना है। वह कौन-से तीन तर्क चुन सकता है जो आयु-उपयुक्त और साक्ष्य-समर्थित हों?
CISCE ICSE कक्षा 7 के पूर्व-पेपर पैटर्न में वाद-विवाद मूल्यांकन के लिए किस प्रकार का प्रश्न पूछा गया है?

परीक्षा-शैली: (क) आशुभाषण की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) एक-मिनट रूपरेखा के चारों खानों के नाम क्रम से लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ग) दो-मिनट का समय-बजट अंकों सहित लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) त्रुटि पहचानिए — प्रश्न: 'आशुभाषण में घबराहट से निपटने की पद्धति बताइए'; उत्तर: "घबराहट नहीं करनी चाहिए; हिम्मत रखकर बोलना चाहिए और सब कुछ अच्छा हो जाएगा।" (1 अंक)

परीक्षा-प्रारूप प्रश्न: (क) आशुभाषण की तीन शर्तें लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) घबराहट से निपटने की तीन चालों के नाम और काम लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ग) विषय 'मेरा प्रिय त्योहार' के लिए चार-खाना रूपरेखा और पक्का आरंभ-वाक्य लिखिए। (3 अंक) (घ) निम्न प्रदर्शन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए — कविता ने रूपरेखा बनाई, आरंभ पक्के वाक्य से किया, पर दो-मिनट सीमा में केवल कारण-खाने का एक बिंदु ही पूरा हुआ — गति अत्यंत धीमी रही। (2 अंक) (च) बताइए कि यह नोड अगले कौशल 'बहुमाध्यम प्रस्तुति' की तैयारी कैसे करता है — दो बिंदु। (2 अंक)

सामग्री-चयन की कसौटी क्या है? इस कसौटी पर निम्न चार तत्वों को स्वीकृत/अस्वीकृत बताइए — विषय 'विद्यालय का पुस्तकालय': (1) पुस्तकालय के कमरे का विस्तृत चित्र; (2) 'पुस्तकें ज्ञान का द्वार' लिखा बड़ा सुंदर पोस्टर; (3) साप्ताहिक उधारी-संख्या का छोटा चार्ट; (4) आपके पड़ोसी बच्चे का फोटो जिसमें वह हँस रहा है।

परीक्षा-शैली: (क) बहुमाध्यम प्रस्तुति की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) सामग्री-चयन की तीन शर्तें लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ग) तत्व-बदल के समय की चाल बताइए — नेत्र-ठहराव क्यों चाहिए। (2 अंक) (घ) त्रुटि पहचानिए — प्रश्न: 'प्रस्तुति में तत्व-संख्या की सीमा क्यों रखी जाती है'; उत्तर: "सीमा इसलिए कि ज़्यादा चित्र बनाने में मेहनत लगती है।" (1 अंक)

परीक्षा-प्रारूप प्रश्न: (क) बहुमाध्यम प्रस्तुति के तीन स्तंभों के नाम क्रम से लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) सेवा-प्रश्न लिखिए और बताइए कि वह किस स्तंभ की कसौटी है। (2 अंक) (ग) विषय 'स्वच्छ भोजन' के लिए चार तत्वों की सामग्री-सूची और तीन-मिनट खाना-चार्ट बनाइए। (3 अंक) (घ) निम्न प्रदर्शन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए — पूजा की प्रस्तुति में पाँच तत्व थे, सब ठीक समय पर खुले, पर उनमें से दो (बादलों की तस्वीर, एक कार्टून-चरित्र) किसी वाक्य को नहीं समझाते थे। (2 अंक) (च) यह नोड (और पूरा अध्याय) अगले अध्याय 'पढ़ना एवं लिखना' की तैयारी कैसे करता है — दो बिंदु। (2 अंक)

नीचे दिए गद्यांश को पढ़िए और प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए — "समय वह अमूल्य धन है जो किसी बाज़ार में नहीं मिलता। जो क्षण बीत गया, वह फिर लौटकर नहीं आता। गाँव का किसान सूर्योदय से पहले खेत की ओर चल पड़ता है, क्योंकि वह जानता है कि बूँद-बूँद से ही घड़ा भरता है। जो विद्यार्थी आज का काम कल पर टाल देता है, वह परीक्षा के दिन पसीना छोड़ता है। जो समय का पालन करता है, उसके पीछे सफलता दौड़ती चलती है।" (क) किसान सूर्योदय से पहले क्यों चल पड़ता है? (1 अंक) (ख) टालने वाला विद्यार्थी परीक्षा के दिन क्या करता है? (1 अंक) (ग) 'अमूल्य' का प्रसंग-अर्थ लिखिए। (1 अंक)

परीक्षा-शैली: (क) पठन-बोध की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) उत्तर-लेखन के तीन नियम लिखिए (प्रश्न-रूप, सूचना-स्रोत, भाषा-रूप)। (2 अंक) (ग) 'गद्यांश' और 'पद्यांश' में एक मूल अंतर लिखिए। (1 अंक) (घ) त्रुटि पहचानिए — प्रश्न: 'लेखक का आशय स्पष्ट कीजिए'; उत्तर: "मेरी राय में समय ही सबसे बड़ा धन है क्योंकि मैंने दादाजी से सुना है।" (1 अंक)

परीक्षा-प्रारूप प्रश्न: (क) पठन-बोध के चार स्तर क्रम से लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) तीन-पठन चाल और चार प्रश्न-प्रकारों में कौन-सा संबंध है — दो वाक्यों में स्पष्ट कीजिए। (2 अंक) (ग) नीचे दिए लघु गद्यांश के चारों प्रकार के प्रश्न बनाइए और उत्तर लिखिए। (3 अंक) "गाँव की चौपाल पर हर साँझ बुज़ुर्ग बैठते हैं। चाय के प्यालों के बीच उनकी बातें खेतों से निकलकर स्कूलों तक चली जाती हैं। पंचायत के बड़े-बड़े निर्णय भी यहीं गूँजते हैं। चौपाल गाँव की खुली सभा है।" (घ) निम्न प्रदर्शन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए — मीरा ने अंश एक बार पढ़ा, सारे प्रश्नों के उत्तर सही लिखे, पर उत्तरों के साथ अपनी टिप्पणियाँ ("मुझे गाँव बहुत अच्छा लगता है") भी जोड़ दीं। (2 अंक) (च) यह नोड (और पढ़ने का यह ढाँचा) इसी अध्याय के लेखन-नोडों (पत्र, निबंध) की तैयारी कैसे करता है — दो बिंदु। (2 अंक)

सीआईएससीई परीक्षा में निबंध लेखन के लिए शब्द सीमा २५०-३०० शब्द होती है। यदि विद्यार्थी १५० शब्द लिखता है तो क्या प्रभाव पड़ेगा? क) पूरे अंक मिलेंगे ख) अंक कटेंगे क्योंकि विचार अपूर्ण रहेंगे ग) कोई प्रभाव नहीं घ) अतिरिक्त अंक मिलेंगे

परीक्षा-शैली: (क) निबंध की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) तीन विधाओं (वर्णनात्मक, विचारात्मक, कथात्मक) में भेद करके प्रत्येक का एक विषय-उदाहरण लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ग) उपसंहार में नया बिंदु क्यों नहीं रखना चाहिए — कारण सहित। (1 अंक) (घ) त्रुटि पहचानिए — प्रश्न: 'समय का मूल्य' पर दो सौ शब्दों का निबंध; उत्तर: चार सौ पचास शब्दों में लिखा, अंत में यह भी लिखा "जितना अधिक लिखोगे, उतने अंक मिलेंगे।" (1 अंक)

परीक्षा-प्रारूप प्रश्न: (क) निबंध की तीन धुरियों के नाम क्रम से लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) विचारात्मक और वर्णनात्मक विधा में बिंदु-संग्रह की दिशा का भेद स्पष्ट कीजिए। (2 अंक) (ग) 'मेरी प्रिय पुस्तक' (वर्णनात्मक, दो सौ शब्द) के लिए चार-खाना रूपरेखा और प्रस्तावना का आरंभ-वाक्य लिखिए। (3 अंक) (घ) निम्न प्रदर्शन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए — राहुल ने 'मेरी प्रिय पुस्तक' पर निबंध लिखा: उसकी सभी वाक्य-रचनाएँ शुद्ध थीं, मात्राएँ भी सहीं, पर पुस्तक के लेखक की जीवनी के तीन अनुच्छेद और पुस्तक की बात आधी पंक्ति में। (2 अंक) (च) यह नोड (निबंध-लेखन) अगले नोड (डायरी और विज्ञापन) की तैयारी कैसे करता है — दो बिंदु। (2 अंक)

उद्देश्य और विधेय का भेद क्या है? निम्न वाक्यों का उद्देश्य-विधेय विभाजन कीजिए — (1) "पापा सुबह बाज़ार गए।" (2) "हमारी कक्षा में चालीस विद्यार्थी पढ़ते हैं।" साथ ही मेल-नियम लिखिए और बताइए कि वाक्य 2 की क्रिया 'पढ़ते हैं' किससे मिली है।

निम्न वाक्यों में लिंग/वचन बदलिए और क्रिया का मेल ठीक कीजिए — (1) "लड़का धीरे-धीरे चलता है।" (स्त्रीलिंग एकवचन) (2) "कविता अच्छे निबंध लिखती है।" (बहुवचन) (3) "पिताजी खेत जोतते हैं।" (बहुवचन) — साथ ही लिखिए कि प्रत्येक बदलाव में किन-किन पदों को छूना पड़ा।

परीक्षा-शैली: (क) पद-भेद की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न वाक्य में उद्देश्य और विधेय अलग कीजिए और कर्ता-पद पहचानिए — "कक्षा में बैठे सभी विद्यार्थी कहानी सुन रहे हैं।" (2 अंक) (ग) मेल-नियम एक वाक्य में लिखिए। (1 अंक) (घ) त्रुटि पहचानिए — उत्तर-पुस्तिका में लिखा: "'सुंदर' हमेशा विशेषण होता है, इसलिए 'उसकी सुंदर देखी मैंने तारीफ़ की' में भी विशेषण है।" (1 अंक)

'ने' वाले वाक्यों में क्रिया का मेल एक विशेष मोड़ लेता है। (क) निम्न चारों वाक्यों में क्रिया-रूप सही है या नहीं — नियम-संकेत सहित लिखिए: (1) "मैंने पुस्तक पढ़ी।" (2) "मैंने पुस्तकें पढ़ा।" (3) "लड़के ने दूध पिया।" (4) "लड़कियों ने गीत गायी।" (ख) यह विशेष मोड़ एक नियम-वाक्य में लिखिए।

परीक्षा-प्रारूप प्रश्न: (क) वाक्य-संरचना के दो मूल अंगों के नाम लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) कारक-चिह्नों के चार रिश्ते उदाहरण सहित लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ग) "बड़े भैया ने कल मुझे एक नई कहानी की पुस्तक दी।" — इस वाक्य की पूर्ण पद-तालिका बनाइए और मेल-जाँच लिखिए। (3 अंक) (घ) निम्न प्रदर्शन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए — प्रीति ने पद-तालिका पूरी सही बनाई, पर अपने सुधार-सुझाव में लिखा: "भेद याद करने के लिए शब्द-सूची रट लो — जितनी लंबी सूची, उतनी अच्छी तैयारी।" (2 अंक) (च) यह नोड अगले नोड (वाक्य-शोधन और विराम-चिह्न) की तैयारी कैसे करता है — दो बिंदु। (2 अंक)

पर्यायवाची का चयन प्रसंग-पट्टी से क्यों होता है? निम्न दो प्रसंगों में 'जल' के उपयुक्त रूप चुनकर कारण दीजिए — (1) ग्राम-सभा का औपचारिक प्रस्ताव: "गाँव में ______ की आपूर्ति बढ़ाई जाए।" (2) कविता की पंक्ति: "सावन आया, ______ से भर गए तालाब।" साथ ही विलोम की 'भाव-अक्ष' चाल से बताइए कि 'सूर्य' का विलोम 'चाँद' क्यों नहीं हो सकता।

निम्न शब्द-समूह वाक्यों के लिए एक शब्द लिखिए — (1) जो सब कुछ जानता हो; (2) जिसका कोई सानी न हो; (3) जो कभी न मरे; (4) जहाँ पुस्तकें पढ़ने-उधार लेने को मिलें; (5) जो पहले कभी न हुआ हो। — साथ ही अपनी चाल (धुरी-पकड़ → नाम-खोज → वापस-बैठाओ) के तीन क़दम वाक्य 2 पर दिखाइए।
निम्न मुहावरों के अर्थ लिखिए और प्रत्येक का एक वाक्य-प्रयोग कीजिए — (1) आँखों का तारा होना; (2) नाक में दम करना; (3) नौ-दो ग्यारह होना; (4) आसमान सिर पर उठाना।

परीक्षा-शैली: (क) पर्यायवाची और विलोम का भेद एक-एक उदाहरण सहित लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ख) 'आशा' का विलोम उपसर्ग-पट्टी से बनाइए और बताइए कि यह पट्टी कौन-सा उपसर्ग लेती है। (1 अंक) (ग) मुहावरे का वाक्य में स्थान क्या होता है — पूर्ण वाक्य या वाक्य-अंश? कारण सहित। (1 अंक) (घ) त्रुटि पहचानिए — प्रश्न: 'सूर्य' के दो पर्यायवाची लिखिए; उत्तर: "सूर्य के दो पर्यायवाची हैं — चाँद और तारे।" (1 अंक)

मुहावरा और लोकोक्ति का भेद परीक्षा में पूछा जाता है। (क) निम्न तीन कथनों को मुहावरा/लोकोक्ति बताइए, कारण सहित: (1) "एक और एक ग्यारह।" (2) "घी सीधे हाथ से निकलना" (3) "घर का भेदी लंका ढाए।" (ख) 'घी सीधे हाथ से निकलना' का अर्थ लिखकर एक वाक्य बनाइए।

परीक्षा-प्रारूप प्रश्न: (क) शब्द-भंडार के चार खानों के नाम क्रम से लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) 'संभव' का विलोम उपसर्ग-पट्टी से बनाइए और उस पट्टी के दो अन्य युग्म दीजिए। (2 अंक) (ग) निम्न तीन शब्द-समूहों के लिए एक-एक शब्द लिखिए — (1) जो देश के लिए प्राण देने को तत्पर रहे; (2) जो कभी न मरे; (3) जहाँ पुस्तकें पढ़ने को मिलें। (3 अंक) (घ) निम्न प्रदर्शन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए — रोहन ने 'आँखों का तारा होना' का अर्थ सही लिखा ("बहुत प्रिय होना"), पर वाक्य लिखा: "पेड़ की आँखों का तारा सूर्य की किरण है।" (2 अंक) (च) यह नोड अगले नोड (उपसर्ग-प्रत्यय) की तैयारी कैसे करता है — दो बिंदु। (2 अंक)
उपसर्ग-पहचान की 'छील-चाल' के तीन क़दम लिखिए। फिर निम्न शब्दों पर चाल लगाइए — (1) निर्मल; (2) संयम; (3) दुर्गंध — प्रत्येक में उपसर्ग, बचा मूल और संधि-परिवर्तन का संकेत लिखिए।
निम्न उपसर्गों से दो-दो शब्द बनाइए और प्रत्येक का अर्थ-पलटाव/विशेषता एक पंक्ति में लिखिए — (1) अ-; (2) निर्-; (3) दुर्-; (4) बे-; (5) बद-; (6) ना-।

प्रत्ययों की पट्टी से शब्द-परिवार बनाइए — (1) 'सुंदर' + -ता; (2) 'बच्चा' + -पन; (3) 'धन' + -वान; (4) 'बल' + -हीन; (5) 'लिख' + -आवट — प्रत्येक में लिखिए कि पद-परिवार कैसे बदला (विशेषण→संज्ञा, व्यक्ति-सूचक, अवस्था-संज्ञा आदि)।

परीक्षा-शैली: (क) उपसर्ग की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न शब्दों में उपसर्ग पहचानकर लिखिए और बचा मूल भी दीजिए — (1) अध्ययन; (2) अपमान। (2 अंक) (ग) हिंदी-पट्टी के दो उपसर्ग उदाहरण सहित लिखिए। (1 अंक) (घ) त्रुटि पहचानिए — उत्तर-पुस्तिका में लिखा: "'अजगर' में 'अ-' उपसर्ग है, मूल है 'जगर', अर्थ यह कि जगर नहीं करता।" (1 अंक)

उपसर्ग और प्रत्यय एक ही शब्द-परिवार में साथ चल सकते हैं। (क) निम्न चारों शब्दों में कौन-सी मशीन चली — लिखिए: (1) अभिनय; (2) महानता; (3) दुर्बल; (4) लिखावट। (ख) एक ऐसा शब्द बनाइए जिसमें उपसर्ग और प्रत्यय दोनों मशीनें चली हों — बनावट और दोनों के काम लिखिए (संकेत: 'असावधानी' — 'अ' + 'सम्' + 'धान' + '-ई' की पट्टी)।

परीक्षा-प्रारूप प्रश्न: (क) उपसर्ग और प्रत्यय में भेद की दो कसौटियाँ लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न तीन शब्दों की छील-पट्टी (छीला-बचा-पलटा) भरिए — (1) अनुचित; (2) दुर्गंध; (3) पराजय। (3 अंक) (ग) एक मूल शब्द चुनकर चार-शाखा शब्द-वृक्ष बनाइए और प्रत्येक शाखा पर मशीन-निशानी लगाइए। (3 अंक) (घ) निम्न प्रदर्शन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए — किरण ने 'विश्राम' की छील-पट्टी भरी: छीला 'वि', बचा 'श्राम', पलटा "श्राम का विपरीत", और संधि-संकेत खाली छोड़ दिया। (2 अंक) (च) यह नोड (और पूरा व्याकरण-अध्याय) कक्षा 8 की भाषा-शृंखला की तैयारी कैसे करता है — दो बिंदु। (2 अंक)
Explain why the division of the empire after the death of Theodosius in 395 CE hurt the western half more than the eastern half.
Evaluate this claim: "Christianity spread rapidly only because Emperor Constantine made it legal in 313 CE."
Construct a labelled timeline with the six turning points of this node — 64 CE, 303 CE, 313 CE, 330 CE, 380 CE and 395 CE — each with a one-line caption stating who acted and what changed.
Answer in CISCE exam style: "State any four causes that led to the decline of the Western Roman Empire." (4 marks)

After 476 CE the western government, its tax system and its courts had all failed — yet schools, record-keeping, care for the poor and letters continued in Europe. Name the institution that took over these functions and apply the general lesson: what happens to the services of a collapsed state, and who inherits them?

Weigh the two emperors: Constantine (tolerance, 313 CE; new capital, 330 CE) and Theodosius I (state religion, 380 CE; last ruler of both halves, died 395 CE). Which of the two did more to shape the medieval world, and why? Defend your choice against the obvious objection.

Answer in the style of a CISCE past-paper question: "The Western Roman Empire was destroyed less by the attacks of its enemies than by its own internal weaknesses." Discuss this statement with reference to any four internal weaknesses, and conclude whether the statement is fully justified. (5 marks)
Which battle of 378 CE destroyed a Roman army and killed a reigning emperor? Name the battle, the emperor, and the enemy.
Explain, step by step, how a Gothic request for refuge in 376 CE ended in the sack of Rome in 410 CE.
Evaluate: "The Battle of Adrianople was more damaging to Rome than the sack of Rome in 410 CE."
Answer in CISCE exam style: "Describe the circumstances that forced the Visigoths to enter the Roman Empire in 376 CE, and state one result of their admission." (4 marks)

Compare the Gothic settlement under Theodosius with the later Gothic kingdom of Theodoric in Italy: what changed between 382 CE and 493 CE in how Goths and Romans related, and what does the change prove about the empire's trajectory?

Answer in the style of a CISCE past-paper question: "The Visigoths whom Rome admitted in 376 CE were refugees; the Visigoths who entered Rome in 410 CE were conquerors. Trace the stages by which one became the other, and state which single party's conduct mattered most in the change." (5 marks)
When did the Vandals sack Rome, under which king, and how did this sack differ from the Gothic sack of 410 CE? Give any two differences.
Explain why Gaiseric's capture of Carthage in 439 CE was, strategically, a heavier blow to Rome than the sack of Rome itself in 455 CE.
Create a labelled route map (describe it in words, stage by stage) of the Vandal migrations from 406 to 439 CE, giving for each stage the year, the place and one line on what happened there.
Answer in CISCE exam style: "Describe the achievements of Gaiseric as king of the Vandals." (4 marks)

Answer in the style of a CISCE past-paper question: "The Vandal kingdom rose on Rome's grain and fell on Rome's church." Explain the two halves of this statement — how Africa's wealth built the kingdom and how Africa's Catholic majority helped destroy it — and state the single year that begins the fall. (5 marks)
Evaluate: "The Battle of Tours (732 CE) saved Europe from Islam."
Answer in CISCE exam style: "State any four achievements of Charlemagne." (4 marks)

Compare the imperial coronations of Charlemagne (800 CE) and the fall of the western empire (476 CE): between those two dates, what changed in the relationship between the Pope, the emperor and the West? Answer with the three-part argument the coronation itself displays.

Answer in the style of a CISCE past-paper question: "From Clovis to the Treaty of Verdun, the Frankish story is the transformation of a barbarian kingdom into the heir of Rome." Trace this transformation in four dated stages, and state which single stage mattered most for the medieval West. (5 marks)
Construct a timeline of six Byzantine landmarks — 330, 532, 537, 565, 718 and 1054 CE — each with a one-line caption identifying the ruler or event and what it changed.
Answer in CISCE exam style: "Describe any four achievements of Justinian I." (4 marks)

Two women stand behind the throne's survival: Theodora in 532 CE and the earlier Western empresses of the dying West. More precisely, weigh Theodora's recorded role in the Nika crisis against Justinian's achievements: can an empire's history justly turn on one person's refusal to flee? Defend a verdict.

Answer in the style of a CISCE past-paper question: "Byzantium's thousand-year survival was the work of its position, its reforms and its culture, in that order of importance." Discuss the three factors, state whether you accept the stated order, and justify any reordering. (5 marks)
Which battle of 1071 CE opened Asia Minor to the Turks? Name the battle, the Byzantine emperor defeated, and the Seljuk sultan.
Create a timeline of seven landmarks of this node — 1055, 1071, 1095, 1099, 1144–1149, 1187 and 1192 CE — each with a one-line caption naming the actor and the change.
Answer in CISCE exam style: "State any four causes of the Crusades." (4 marks)

The First Crusade's victory in 1099 was so complete that its founders assumed the conquest was permanent; within ninety years the kingdom was gone. Diagnose the founders' error: what did they misunderstand about the land they had taken, and which two structural facts made their states unviable from the start?
Compare the effects of Manzikert (1071 CE) on Byzantium with the effects of the Crusades on Western Europe: which event benefited its own losers more, and why? Give two effects on each side.

Answer in the style of a CISCE past-paper question: "The Crusades began as a war for the holy places and ended as a school for Europe." Discuss this statement: describe the original purpose, and explain any three lasting effects of the Crusades on Europe, stating which was most important. (5 marks)
Create a table of the four great later monastic foundations — Cluny (910), Citeaux (1098), the Franciscans and the Dominicans — with founder or founding figure, and the specific need each answered.
Answer in CISCE exam style: "Describe any four ways in which monasteries served medieval society." (4 marks)

Monastic reform kept recurring — Benedict's Rule, then Cluny (910), then Citeaux (1098), then the friars — each generation finding the previous one corrupted. Apply the pattern: why does any institution built on voluntary discipline drift toward worldliness, and what two design features let the monastic movement repair itself repeatedly?

Answer in the style of a CISCE past-paper question: "The monasteries were the universities, hospitals, hotels, farms and libraries of early medieval Europe — all under one roof and one Rule." Justify each of the five claims with one concrete feature of monastic life, and state which single feature would be hardest for the medieval world to replace. (5 marks)
Evaluate: "The sack of 1204 did more to destroy Byzantium than the Ottoman conquest of 1453."

A great trading city-state lends an army the money it cannot repay, then directs the army against the lender's commercial rivals. Apply the Venetian mechanism of the Fourth Crusade: name the three structural dangers of financing war by contract, and match each to the events of 1201–1204.
Create a timeline of six landmarks of this node — 1204, 1212, 1229, 1258, 1299 and 1453 CE — each with a one-line caption naming the actor and the change.
Answer in CISCE exam style: "State any four consequences of the fall of Constantinople in 1453 CE." (4 marks)

Two sultans define the Turkish story in this theme: Alp Arslan at Manzikert (1071) and Mehmed II at Constantinople (1453). Compare their achievements — what each conquered, what each founded, and which of the two changed world history more profoundly. Defend the verdict.

Compare the sack of Constantinople in 1204 with the Gothic sack of Rome in 410 (node c7_histciv_icse_01_002): two structural similarities, two decisive differences, and the meaning of the fact that each city never fully recovered what was lost in its own sack.

Answer in the style of a CISCE past-paper question: "The Middle Ages began with the fall of one great city (476 CE) and ended with the fall of another (1453 CE), and in both cases the fall was prepared by centuries." Compare the two endings — what fell in each, what rose in each, and which single connecting thread runs through both stories. (5 marks)

Create the voice of the age: you are a Meccan merchant of the Quraysh showing your young cousin around the city during the fair season. Write a short speech (about 150 words) in which you point out the three institutions that make your city great — the Kaaba, the sacred months, and the caravan trade — explaining each in character.
Answer in CISCE exam style: "State any four features of the religious condition of Arabia before the rise of Islam." (4 marks)

Answer in the style of a CISCE past-paper question: "Before Islam, Arabia had cities, trade and poetry, but no nation and no law above the tribe." Explain this judgement with reference to: (a) the tribal organisation of society, (b) the place of Mecca and the Kaaba in the life of the peninsula, and (c) any two social evils of the age. (5 marks)
A Muslim family earns ₹12,00,000 annually, has essential expenses of ₹8,00,000, and holds gold worth ₹2,00,000 (above nisab). Calculate their Zakat liability for the year.
Create a one‑page poster that explains the Five Pillars to a Class 5 student using only pictures and three‑word captions.
“Describe the significance of Hajj in fostering unity among Muslims worldwide.” (CISCE 2023, 4 marks)
**APPLICATION:** A Muslim business owner earns ₹50,00,000 profit, has ₹10,00,000 essential expenses, and owns silver worth ₹3,00,000 (above nisab). Compute Zakat due.
**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** “Write short notes on: (a) Shahada (b) Sawm (c) Zakat.” (3 × 2 = 6 marks)
CISCE exam‑style: “Explain two ways in which the Hijrat changed the course of Islamic history.” (4 marks)
Comparison: Compare the Hijrat (622 CE) with the migration of the early Christians from Jerusalem to Pella (c. 66 CE) in terms of motives, leadership, and outcomes.
CISCE past‑paper pattern: “Describe the significance of the Hijrat for the Muslim community. (6 marks)”
Explain, step by step, how the conquest of Mecca in January 630 CE succeeded with almost no bloodshed.

A general wins a city that has fought his movement for twenty years. Apply the Meccan precedent of 630 CE: name three decisions a victor must take in the first days after entry to convert conquest into reconciliation, and match each to what the Prophet actually did.
Create a timeline of five landmarks of the return to Mecca — 622, 628, 630, 632 (pilgrimage) and 632 (death) CE — each with a one-line caption naming the event and its consequence.
Answer in CISCE exam style: "Describe the main teachings of the Farewell Sermon delivered during the Prophet's pilgrimage to Mecca in 632 CE." (4 marks)

Here is a puzzle of statecraft: after 630 CE the Prophet held the greatest city of Arabia, the allegiance of its old ruling tribe, and an army no tribe could face — yet he went back to Medina, an oasis he had entered as a refugee. Diagnose the reasoning: what did choosing Medina as the continuing capital protect, and what would ruling from Mecca have destroyed?

Reconciliation after civil conflict is one of the hardest problems in any age. Apply the Meccan precedent of 630 CE to a modern scenario: a divided nation signs a peace after decades of violence. State the three mechanisms the precedent supplies, explain what each achieves, and identify the one condition without which the whole pattern fails.

Evaluate the Farewell Sermon of 632 CE as a social charter: which three of its teachings most directly reversed the specific conditions of the Jahiliyyah taught in node c7_histciv_icse_02_001, and why does that reversal — rather than any general wisdom — make the Sermon a turning point in Arabian history?

Compare the two journeys that frame the Prophet's mission — the Hijrat of 622 CE to Medina (node c7_histciv_icse_02_004) and the return to Mecca of 630 CE: direction and manner of travel, the numbers involved, the legal or political instrument each journey produced, and the meaning of each in the structure of the story. Then state the single respect in which the two journeys were alike.

Answer in the style of a CISCE past-paper question: "The return to Mecca in 630 CE completed in peace what ten years of struggle could not compel — and the two years that followed completed what even the conquest could not." Explain this judgement with reference to: (a) the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and the cause of the march, (b) the entry, amnesty and cleansing of the Kaaba, and (c) the Year of Delegations and the Farewell Pilgrimage. (5 marks)

The Caliphate of 632 CE solved one succession crisis and the Caliphate of 656–661 CE failed another. Apply the comparison: state the problem each crisis posed, the mechanism by which each was handled, and derive the two conditions a succession mechanism must meet to survive.
Answer in CISCE exam style: "Name the first four Caliphs of Islam in order, with the period of each, and state any one important achievement of Umar." (4 marks)

Here is a constitutional puzzle: the Caliphate of 632 CE was elective, yet it produced no elections in the modern sense — no campaigns, no votes counted by majority. Diagnose the actual mechanism: by what process was authority conferred in 632, and why did that mechanism work in Medina but break down across an empire by 656?

Evaluate: "The speed of the conquests of 634–656 CE was possible only because the community was united; and the conquests, in turn, destroyed the unity." Test both halves of the claim against the record and give a verdict.

Compare the two deaths that bracket this period — the Prophet's in 632 CE and Ali's in 661 CE: the crisis each produced, the solution found each time, and what the difference in outcome proves about how the community had changed in thirty years.

Answer in the style of a CISCE past-paper question: "Between 632 and 661 CE the Muslim community changed from an Arabian brotherhood into a world empire — and paid for the change with the principle that had made it." Explain this judgement with reference to: (a) the election of Abu Bakr and the unity of Arabia, (b) the conquests and administration of Umar and Uthman, and (c) the civil war under Ali and the end of the elective Caliphate. (5 marks)
Critique the view that the Mongol sack of Baghdad in 1258 was the sole cause of the end of Islamic scientific progress.
“Explain the significance of the Battle of the Zab (750 CE) in the transition from Umayyad to Abbasid rule.” (CISCE past‑paper style)

Apply: The year is 1191. A Rajput council advises Prithviraj Chauhan after Tarain. Using the military facts of the period, draft the three-line warning the wise minister should give about Muhammad Ghori, name the two military disadvantages Rajput armies carried against Turkish cavalry, and state what the council should have prepared for in 1192 — and what actually happened.

Create: Design the single examination timeline-card a Class 7 student should carry for this node: choose eight dates, order them, give each a one-line event, and write the one connecting sentence that turns the eight dates into the story of the Sultanate's foundation.

CISCE exam-style: (a) Between which years did Mahmud of Ghazni raid India, and how many raids did he undertake? (b) Name the temple he raided on the Gujarat coast and the year. (c) Name the Rajput king defeated at the Second Battle of Tarain and the year. (d) Whose general was Qutbuddin Aibak, and what did he found in 1206?

HOTS: "Mahmud's seventeen raids were, without his intending it, Ghori's greatest ally." Unpack the claim: state three ways the raiding century (1000–1027) prepared the conquest century (1175–1206), and judge which of the three was the most decisive — with the reason.

HOTS: Two historians argue about Tarain. Historian P: "1192 was won by the Turks' superior weapons." Historian Q: "1192 was won by the Turks' superior organisation, which the Indians could have copied and did not." Using the evidence of 1191 (when the same weapons lost), the conduct of the second battle, and the fate of the north after the victory, judge between P and Q and state the one piece of further evidence that would settle the matter beyond argument.

Application: A heritage society is marking the Somnath raid with a plaque. Three draft wordings are proposed: (A) "Here in 1026 Mahmud of Ghazni looted the temple of Somnath." (B) "Here in January 1026 the temple of Somnath was raided by Mahmud of Ghazni, who carried its treasure to Ghazni — one of seventeen raids that emptied north India's temples between 1000 and 1027." (C) "Here the invader's fury destroyed our sacred land forever." State which draft a history-teacher would approve, why the other two fail (one is incomplete, one is polemic), and rewrite (C) into a defensible one-sentence plaque line.

Past-paper pattern: Study the extract and answer the questions. EXTRACT: "In the twelfth century's last quarter a ruler of Ghor turned from plunder to annexation: Multan and Uch fell in 1175, Lahore in 1186, and when the prince of Delhi and Ajmer was beaten on the plain of Tarain in the year 1192, the rich plain of the Ganga lay beyond him undefended. Within a decade his slave-officers had carried the crescent standard to Bihar's monasteries and the swamps of Bengal; and when the master died in 1206, one of these slaves did not return the land to anyone — he called it his own." (i) Name the "ruler of Ghor" and the "prince of Delhi and Ajmer". (ii) Why does the extract call the Ganga plain "undefended" after 1192? (iii) Name the "slave" who called the land his own, the year, and what historians call the state he founded. (iv) State the one design-word that separates this invader from Mahmud of Ghazni, as the extract's own first line says. (v) Assess the extract's last clause — why is "he did not return the land to anyone" historically important?
A historian finds a coin inscribed “Sikandar Shah” dated 1490. To which dynasty does this ruler belong, and why?
Explain the significance of the five dynasties in shaping the Delhi Sultanate’s political legacy. (CISCE exam‑style, 4 marks)
CISCE past‑paper pattern: “Describe the major contributions of the Tughlaq dynasty to the Delhi Sultanate.” (4 marks)
Past‑paper style: “Describe the role of the *Wazir* in the central administration of the Delhi Sultanate.” (4 marks)
What was the primary objective of Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s token copper currency introduced in 1329?
Why did the forced shift of the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (1327) fail within two years?
Apply the concept of “over‑centralisation” to explain why Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s Doab tax increase (c. 1330) led to reduced revenue.
Application: Design a modern public‑policy checklist (5 items) for a government planning a demonetisation, drawing on lessons from Tughlaq’s token currency failure.
CISCE past‑paper pattern: "Explain any two reasons why Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s scheme of token currency failed." (3 marks)
“Describe the development of Indo‑Islamic architecture during the Delhi Sultanate with reference to three monuments.” (CISCE past‑paper style, 6 marks)
Which Tughlaq sultan shifted the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad in 1327?
Apply the concept of “geographic distance weakening central authority” to explain why the Vijayanagar founders could establish an independent kingdom in 1336.

**APPLICATION:** Using a map of the 14th‑century Indian subcontinent, mark the approximate territories controlled by the Tughlaqs in 1330 and the emergent Vijayanagar and Bahmani zones by 1350. Explain how the map illustrates the disintegration process.
**COMPARISON:** Compare the reasons for the rise of Vijayanagar (1336) and Bahmani (1347) in terms of (a) leadership, (b) geographic base, and (c) immediate trigger.
**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** “State two administrative experiments of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and explain how each contributed to the decline of the Tughlaq empire.” (4 marks)
CISCE exam‑style: “Describe two factors that led to the simultaneous rise of the Vijayanagar and Bahmani kingdoms in the 14th century.” (3 marks)
CISCE past‑paper pattern: “State two reasons why the Vijayanagar and Bahmani kingdoms became rivals soon after their foundation.” (2 marks)

A CISCE exam asks: “Assess the impact of Krishnadeva Raya’s victory at the Battle of Raichur (1520) on the political landscape of the Deccan.” Provide a structured answer with introduction, three points, and conclusion.
Explain the role of the ‘Amaranayaka’ system in the Vijayanagar administration. (4 marks)
Critique the view that Vijayanagar’s decline was caused solely by the Battle of Talikota (1565).
Past‑paper style: “Describe the main features of the Vijayanagar administration with special reference to the nayankara system.” (6 marks)
Design a poster that highlights three key features of Gol Gumbaz for a Class 7 history exhibition.
A merchant from Goa arrives at Hampi Bazaar in 1520. List two goods he would likely sell and two he would buy, based on the city’s trade connections.
Critique the view that Hampi’s decline was solely due to the 1565 Battle of Talikota.
A past CISCE paper asked: “Describe the main features of the Vittala Temple complex at Hampi.” Provide a model answer structured for 5 marks.
Why did the Bahmani capital shift from Gulbarga to Bidar in 1425?
If you were a commander in 1526, how would you adapt Babur’s tulughma tactic to a modern battlefield scenario?
Explain the causes and consequences of the First Battle of Panipat in about 80 words.
Compare the First Battle of Panipat with the Battle of Khanwa (1527) in terms of tactics and outcomes.
Apply the concept of “loss and recovery” to explain how Humayun regained his throne in 1555.
Critique the view that Humayun’s restoration in 1555 was solely due to Persian military aid.
A past CISCE paper asks: “State two reasons why Humayun failed to consolidate his empire after 1530.” Write a concise answer.

A merchant in 1543 wants to send a urgent message from Sonargaon to Attock. Using Sher Shah’s infrastructure, describe the steps the message would take and estimate the time saved compared with pre‑Sher Shah conditions.
**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** “Explain how Sher Shah Suri’s administrative measures facilitated the consolidation of the Mughal Empire under Akbar.” (6 marks)
**CISCE past‑paper pattern:** “Explain how Akbar’s mansabdari system helped in maintaining a large standing army without burdening the imperial treasury with cash payments.” (4 marks)

Reasoning: A pargana's ten-year average produce is 900 maunds of grain and its ten-year average price is 40 dams per maund. Show, step by step, how the dahsala rule converts these into the state's cash demand, and explain at each step why the rule's design (average, fraction, cash) protects one side — the farmer or the treasury — and how the other side is protected in turn.

Create: Design a four-column "revenue ledger page" a pargana official might keep under the dahsala system — name the columns, state what enters each, show one filled row for a polaj field using the averages (ten-year average produce 600 maunds, average price 30 dams per maund), and write the one sentence the ledger's completeness makes possible that a guess-based system never could.

Application: A film-maker is shooting a scene "Todar Mal's office, 1582" and asks your class for four props on the diwan's table, each anchored to a real feature of the revenue system — name the four props, what each must show, and the one anachronism to avoid on the table at all costs.

Past-paper pattern: Study the extract and answer the questions. EXTRACT: "The emperor's surveyors carried one rod into every province; the record-keepers divided the fields by the years they rested; and the diwan ordered that no village be asked for more than a third of the harvest its last ten years had averaged, reckoned in money at those years' mean price. Where the rod could not go, the heap itself was divided; where the records were old, the past was continued; and in the year the river rose, the collector's book showed words no collector loves: remitted." (i) Name the rod, the record-keeper's four field classes, and the diwan. (ii) Compute, from the extract's rule, the demand of a village averaging 750 maunds at 32 dams per maund. (iii) Match the extract's three fallbacks ("the heap", "the past", "the rising river") to the system's methods and valves. (iv) State the one protection the extract's rule gives the farmer that a current-crop share would not. (v) Assess the extract's last sentence — why is a remission entry in the collector's book the system's defining evidence?
What tax did Akbar abolish in 1564 to demonstrate religious neutrality?
A past CISCE paper asked: “Explain how Akbar’s religious policy strengthened the Mughal Empire.” Provide a model answer structured for 4 marks.
A past CISCE paper asks: “Explain two reasons why the loss of Kandahar in 1622 was a setback for the Mughal Empire.” Provide a model answer.

Reasoning: Explain, step by step, the buffer-states paradox: why the annexation of Bijapur and Golconda in 1686–87 — the policy's greatest apparent successes — actually worsened Aurangzeb's Maratha problem.

Apply: An examination map shows the Deccan with five numbered marks: (1) Raigad, (2) Purandar, (3) Agra, (4) Bijapur, (5) Jinji (Gingee). State the event each mark belongs to with its year, order the five chronologically, and state which two events prove the war's geographic spread from the Maratha homeland to the far south.

CISCE exam-style: (a) Between which years did Aurangzeb's personal Deccan campaign last, and where did he die? (b) Name the treaty of 1665 and its main term. (c) Name the fortress to which Rajaram escaped in 1689 and the year it fell. (d) State two costs of the Deccan policy to the Mughal Empire.

HOTS: "Every Mughal remedy for the Deccan enlarged the disease." Test the claim against three remedies — the Purandar treaty (1665), the annexations (1686–87), and the execution of Sambhaji (1689) — stating for each what it intended, what it actually produced, and deliver the judgment the three tests jointly support.
If you were a Mughal noble in 1720, what steps would you take to secure your position given the weakening central authority?
Write a short note on the role of the Marathas in the decline of the Mughal Empire (4 marks).
Compare the impact of Nadir Shah’s invasion (1739) and Ahmad Shah Abdali’s invasion (1761) on the Mughal Empire.
Explain any three causes for the decline of the Mughal Empire after Aurangzeb’s death. (3 marks)
Create a short verse (4 lines) that could have been sung by both a Bhakti saint and a Sufi saint, reflecting their shared values.

In a CISCE exam, a question asks: “Explain how the use of vernacular languages by Bhakti and Sufi saints contributed to the spread of their teachings.” Write a model answer (3–4 sentences) that would earn full marks.

A past CISCE paper asked: “Explain how the Bhakti and Sufi movements contributed to the development of a composite culture in medieval India.” Write a concise answer (150 words) structured for full marks.

Application: A Class 7 student has one examination minute to explain "why Guru Nanak matters to composite culture". Draft the three-sentence spoken answer that covers his teaching, his practice and his book — and state the single term from the three that the examiner will listen for.
Create a brief outline (three bullet points) for a Class 7 answer to the question: “How did Shankara contribute to the making of India’s composite culture?”
In a CISCE exam, a question asks: “State two ways in which Shankara’s teachings differ from the Bhakti emphasis on personal devotion.” Write a model answer worth 2 marks.
A past CISCE paper asks: “State two contributions of Adi Shankaracharya to the preservation of Hindu philosophy.” Write a concise answer for 2 marks.
Critique the view that Dnyaneshwar’s early samadhi at age 21 limited his historical impact.
**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** “Explain how the Alwars and Nayanars contributed to the making of a composite culture in early medieval South India.” (4 marks)
CISCE exam‑style: “Describe two contributions of the Chishti order to the development of composite culture in medieval India.” (4 marks)
CISCE past‑paper pattern: “Explain how the Chishti silsila contributed to the growth of a composite culture in North India between the 13th and 16th centuries.” (6 marks)
A Class 7 student is asked to design a poster showing composite culture from the Bhakti‑Sufi era. List three visual elements the poster should include and justify each.
A Class 7 student writes in an exam: “The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 January 1950.” Identify the error and give the correct date with its significance.
**EVALUATION/CRITIQUE:** “The word ‘socialist’ in the Preamble has lost relevance after the 1991 economic reforms.” Assess this view.
**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** “State two reasons why the Constituent Assembly took almost three years to frame the Constitution.” (2 marks)
Evaluate the decision to have the Constituent Assembly also serve as the provisional Parliament until 1952.
Compare the Indian Constituent Assembly with the American Constitutional Convention of 1787 in terms of composition and duration.
Describe the main functions of the Constituent Assembly. (4 marks)
Explain the significance of the date 26 November 1949 in the context of the Indian Constitution.

Evaluate: A classmate claims: "Adding 'Socialist' and 'Secular' in 1976 changed the Constitution's meaning — before that, India was neither." Assess the claim: state what is right in it, what it misses, and the balanced verdict a careful student gives.

HOTS: Two students quarrel over the 1976 additions. Student A: "Adding 'Socialist' and 'Secular' was unnecessary — the Constitution was already both; the words were decoration." Student B: "They were essential — words in the Preamble are commitments, not decorations." Judge the two: state what each gets right, the test that decides between them, and the answer you would write in an examination.
Which Preamble ideal is directly reflected in Article 14 of the Constitution?
Apply the four ideals to evaluate whether a policy reserving 50 % of government jobs for a single community aligns with the Constitution’s vision.
Create a short poster slogan that captures the interdependence of Justice, Equality, Fraternity and Liberty for a Class 7 audience.
Design a poster for a Class 7 civics exhibition that illustrates how the nine ideals support each other. Describe the layout and symbols you would use.
A past ICSE question asked: “Explain how the Preamble reflects the philosophy of the Constitution.” Write a model answer structured for 4 marks.
How does the welfare‑state feature of social justice differ from the Fundamental Right to equality (Article 14)?
Compare the welfare‑state feature of participatory governance (Article 40) with the 73rd Constitutional Amendment’s Panchayati Raj provisions.

Recall: In which part and articles do the Directive Principles sit? State Article 37's two rules in words as close to the text as possible. Define "the State" for this part. Name the country whose Constitution was the source of the DPSPs.

Reasoning: A student objects: "If no court can enforce the Directive Principles, they are just advice — and advice can be ignored. Why did the framers waste Part IV on advice?" Unravel the objection using the three loads of the meaning, Article 37's second rule, and the difference between judicial and political enforcement.

Evaluate: A student claims: "Article 37 contradicts itself — the same article says the principles cannot be enforced and then calls them fundamental. A constitution should not speak in riddles." Assess the claim: state what looks contradictory, show the two sentences answer two different questions, and give the verdict.

CISCE exam-style: (a) What are the Directive Principles of State Policy? (b) State the two rules laid down in Article 37. (c) Why did the framers of the Constitution make the Directive Principles non-enforceable, yet call them fundamental? (d) From which Constitution were the Directive Principles borrowed?

HOTS: "Article 37 is a hinge: it swings Part IV away from the courtroom and into the law-book." Test the claim: state what swings in each direction, identify which ONE clause keeps Part IV visible to the courts at all, and assess whether the hinge could have been set the other way (courtroom yes, law-book no) — with the consequence.

Create: Design a two-shelf library display called "The Republic's To-Do Shelves" that teaches the classification without quoting full article texts: state what stands on each shelf (four objects per shelf, each object standing for one article), and write the shelf-talker that handles the Articles 47–48 straddle honestly.

HOTS: "The Gandhian shelf is the general shelf written in village grammar." Test the claim by translating three Gandhian articles into their general-shelf equivalents — Article 40 into 38's terms, Article 43 into 39's terms, Article 46 into 39A's terms — and state where the translation fails, i.e., what the Gandhian article carries that no general article does.

HOTS: Two students quarrel over the map's authority. Student A: "Since Articles 47 and 48 straddle both shelves, the whole classification is useless — teach Part IV as one list." Student B: "The straddle proves the map needs an honesty-flag, not a funeral — the two-shelf map still teaches more than one flat list." Judge the two: state what each gets right, design the map-rule the straddle forces, and give the verdict on which tool a Class 7 student should use.
Explain why a citizen cannot file a writ petition to enforce Article 40 (organisation of village panchayats).
**HOTS:** “If the Parliament amends the Constitution to move Article 40 from Part IV to Part III, what would be the immediate legal consequence for citizens?”
**COMPARISON:** Compare the enforceability of Article 21 (Right to Life) and Article 47 (Duty to raise nutrition levels).
Recall: State the conversion mechanism. Pair these six with their laws or programmes and years: Article 39(d); Article 39A; Article 41 (old-age); Article 45 (education); Article 40; Article 48A.

Reasoning: A student asks: "If MGNREGA and the RTE are so enforceable, why were they not written as Fundamental Rights in 1950 — why route them through Part IV first?" Unravel the answer using capacity, sequencing and the upgrade pathway.

CISCE exam-style: (a) What is meant by "conversion" of Directive Principles into action? (b) Name the constitutional amendment that gave constitutional status to panchayats, with its year, and state any two features it introduced. (c) How was the education directive of Article 45 converted? (d) Name two environment statutes born of Article 48A with their years.

HOTS: Two students quarrel over the panchayat journey's starting line. Student A: "Article 40's action began in 1992 — everything before was experiments." Student B: "It began in 1959 — Nagaur was the action, 1992 the guarantee." Judge the two: state what each gets right, the experiment-versus-guarantee distinction that reconciles them, and the examination answer with the three dates in order.

Past-paper pattern: Study the extract and answer the questions. EXTRACT: "The state kept a promise-journal. One page records a commission for the spinning wheel, 1956. One records two coins made equal, 1976. One records a van that carries justice to the forest villages. One records a chair in every village square that no officer may now cancel, 1992. One records a hundred days of work on demand, 2005. And the last page is stamped twice — 2002, when the promise left its old chapter, and 2009, when the law came to deliver it." (i) Name the five conversions with their parent articles. (ii) Explain the journal's mechanism — how a promise "records" into enforceable action. (iii) Which page records a STRUCTURE rather than a statute, and why is that the Gandhian shelf's crown? (iv) Unpack the double-stamped page: what left which chapter, and what arrived? (v) Assess the journal as evidence against the claim that Part IV is a dead letter — state the two strongest exhibits and the one exhibit that proves conversions are still continuing.
Evaluate the statement: “Article 50 (separation of judiciary from executive) has been fully implemented in India.”
Create a one‑sentence slogan that captures the spirit of the Liberal‑Intellectual Principles for a Class 7 poster.

Which of the following pairs correctly matches a Liberal‑Intellectual Principle with its Article number? (a) Uniform Civil Code – Article 45, (b) Separation of judiciary – Article 50, (c) Promotion of international peace – Article 48, (d) Modern agriculture – Article 51.

A state government decides to introduce a common marriage law for all communities, citing Article 44. Opponents claim this violates religious freedom under Article 25. How would you resolve this conflict using constitutional hierarchy?

Compare the focus of Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code) and Article 40 (organisation of village panchayats). Which category does each belong to, and what does this contrast reveal about the Constitution’s approach?
Past CISCE paper pattern: “Explain the significance of Article 51 in shaping India’s foreign policy.” Write a concise answer worth 4 marks.
In a CISCE short‑answer question (3 marks), you are asked: “State two differences between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.” Write a model answer.

**APPLICATION:** A state government proposes a law banning alcohol statewide, citing Article 47. Identify the DPSP category, and discuss whether a court can strike down this law if challenged under Article 19(1)(g) (freedom of trade).
**COMPARISON:** Compare the judicial approach to conflicts between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles in *Champakam Dorairajan* (1951) and *Minerva Mills* (1980).
**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** “Write a short note on the significance of Directive Principles in the Indian Constitution.” (5 marks) Provide a model answer structured for CISCE marking.
Define a ratio and state its two essential conditions. In a class of 40 students with 16 girls, write the ratio of boys to girls in lowest terms, and state what fraction of the class the girls form.
Express the ratio 45 minutes : 2 hours in its lowest terms, showing the unit conversion at the correct place. Then state why "45 : 2" is unlawful.
A student writes "the ratio of 25 paise to ₹1 is 25 : 1". Evaluate the claim, give the correct ratio, and state the general conversion principle the student missed.
Divide ₹720 among Anu, Bilal and Chetan in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Show every step and verify your answer. Then state how much more Chetan receives than Anu.

Design a 2-ingredient sharbat recipe task for your group: the syrup-to-water ratio must be 1 : 6 and the jug holds 2.1 litres of sharbat. (a) State how much syrup and how much water to pour. (b) A group member pours 500 mL syrup and 1.5 L water. Evaluate the mix against the target ratio and state the correction.

In the CISCE examination style: (a) Name the first and second terms of a ratio. (1 mark) (b) Check whether 6 : 9 and 14 : 21 form a proportion, stating the rule used. (2 marks) (c) Find x if 4 : x :: 12 : 15. (2 marks) (d) Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 7 and their sum is 96. Find the numbers. (3 marks)

A stationery shop keeps pens, pencils and erasers in stock in the continued ratio 2 : 3 : 4. There are 54 items in all. (a) Find each count. (b) During the week, 6 pens and 6 pencils are sold. Write the new ratio of pens : pencils : erasers in lowest terms. (c) State, with a reason, whether the erasers are now more than half the stock.

Find the unknowns: (a) 15 : 25 :: x : 40. (b) The numbers 28, y, 63 are in continued proportion (28 : y :: y : 63). Find y. (c) Two numbers are in the ratio 7 : 9; if 2 is subtracted from each, the new ratio is 3 : 4. Find the original numbers.

A map of a district uses the scale 1 cm : 5 km. (a) Two towns are 4.8 cm apart on the map. Find the actual distance. (b) A river's true length is 32 km. Find its map length. (c) A student measures two towns as 3 cm apart and claims they are 15 km apart; the atlas's table says 14 km. Decide which source is more trustworthy for a map-reading exercise and why, given the scale.

Evaluate each claim with working: (i) "Rice at ₹96 for 2 kg is better value than ₹150 for 3 kg." (ii) "If a : b = 4 : 5, then 3a : 3b = 12 : 15, and all three ratios are the same comparison." (iii) "A 7 : 5 sharing where the total rises from ₹600 to ₹900 keeps both shares' DIFFERENCE unchanged."

In the CISCE past-paper pattern: (a) The ratio of the number of boys to girls in a school of 630 students is 4 : 5. Find the number of girls. (2 marks) (b) Check whether the numbers 10, 20, 25, 50 are in proportion. (2 marks) (c) ₹1,020 is divided among A, B and C so that A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 2 : 5. Find C's share. (4 marks) (d) State one situation from daily life where a ratio must be kept fixed even as quantities change, and name the quantity that adjusts. (2 marks)
If 8 pens cost ₹96, what is the cost of 1 pen?
A car covers 240 km in 4 hours. How far will it travel in 7 hours at the same speed?
Evaluate: “If 5 kg of wheat costs ₹200, then 12 kg will cost ₹480.” Is the statement correct?
A recipe needs 3/4 litre of milk for 6 servings. How much milk is needed for 10 servings?
CISCE exam‑style: “If 9 identical books weigh 13.5 kg, find the weight of 14 such books.”

**HOTS:** “If 9 workers can build a wall in 12 days, how many days will 6 workers take to build the same wall, assuming they work at the same rate?” Explain why the unitary method as taught (direct proportion) cannot be applied directly, and describe the correct approach.
**APPLICATION:** A school buys 40 boxes of chalk, each box containing 12 sticks, for ₹960. What is the cost of 25 sticks?
**COMPARISON:** Compare the unitary method and the ratio‑proportion method for solving “A car travels 180 km in 3 hours. How long to travel 300 km?” Highlight one advantage of each.
**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** “If 8 kg of rice costs ₹520, find the cost of 15 kg of rice.”

State the unitary method in your own words and the one condition that must hold for it to be lawful. Then solve: 8 identical school badges cost ₹96. Find the cost of 13 badges, showing both lines of working and the verification.

A box of 6 soap bars costs ₹198. (a) Find the price of one bar. (b) How many bars can be bought with ₹330? (c) How many with ₹350, and what happens to the extra money? State why fractional answers are or are not acceptable in (b) and (c).
Evaluate this student's solution, find the error, and write the correct solution: "12 pens cost ₹90, so 1 pen costs 12 ÷ 90 = ₹0.133; therefore 20 pens cost 0.133 × 20 = ₹2.66."

Two bills from the same stationery shop: Bill 1 — 5 identical drawing sheets and 4 identical colour packs cost ₹290. Bill 2 — 5 identical drawing sheets and 7 identical colour packs cost ₹380. Find the price of one sheet and one colour pack, showing how the mixture was dissolved.

In the CISCE examination style: (a) 15 identical notebooks cost ₹262.50. Find the cost of 22 notebooks. (3 marks) (b) A worker earns ₹1,875 in 6 days at the same daily rate. How much does she earn in 11 days? (3 marks) (c) State the one condition without which neither answer would be valid. (2 marks)

A machine fills identical ink cartridges; it completes 18 cartridges in 24 minutes at a steady pace. (a) How long for 33 cartridges? (b) The operator claims: "In 60 minutes the machine finishes MORE than twice the 18 done in 24 minutes, because 60 is more than twice 24." Evaluate the claim with the unit line. (c) State the general principle the claim tests.

A water tanker supplies identical overhead tanks. It fills 5 tanks in 3 hours 45 minutes. (a) How long does one tank take? (b) How many tanks can be filled in 9 hours? (c) The driver plans a route: "6 tanks in the morning shift, which runs 9:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m." Decide whether the plan is feasible, showing all working in minutes.

A bookshop's festival offer: "Buy at ₹48 per notebook; on orders of 25 or more, the unit price drops to ₹42." A school needs 60 notebooks. (a) Compute the order cost without and with the offer. (b) Another school has ₹2,100. How many notebooks can it order at best, using the offer if worthwhile? (c) Evaluate: "The offer's unit-price drop is 12.5%." Check the claim.

Evaluate each statement TRUE or FALSE with working: (i) "If 14 identical chairs cost ₹4,200, then 5 chairs cost ₹1,500." (ii) "In a reverse unitary problem with a remainder, rounding UP gives the customer the best deal and is therefore the right answer." (iii) "The unitary method and the parts-machine (divide in a ratio) both begin by finding the value of one part."

In the CISCE past-paper pattern: (a) 25 identical pastries cost ₹875. Find the cost of 17 pastries. (2 marks) (b) A cyclist covers 30 km in 2½ hours at uniform speed. How far in 4 hours? (2 marks) (c) A hostel allocates identical food packets: 40 packets last 5 days for its residents. How many days will 56 packets last, at the same daily consumption? (3 marks) (d) State the condition common to (a), (b) and (c) that makes each solvable by a single unit line, and name ONE situation in (c) that would break it. (3 marks)

Write the general expression for the unitary method in letters, name every letter, state the condition of validity, and verify the expression by substitution. Then evaluate it for m = 8, c = 344, n = 14.

Derive the reverse form "number of units affordable with amount A" from the general expression, showing every algebraic step. Then use it: 12 identical lamps cost ₹1,560; how many lamps can be bought for ₹2,730?

Evaluate this student's claim, find the error, and repair it: "If 6 chairs cost ₹2,160, then 10 chairs cost (6 × 10) ÷ 2160 × 100... roughly ₹2.78 — wait, chairs can't cost that. The formula must be wrong."

Using the general expression, answer WITHOUT full computation first, by scale-reads, then verify: (a) If 15 identical bags cost ₹5,850, what happens to the cost of 30 bags — and what is it? (b) What would 5 bags cost? (c) If instead the 15-bag total had been ₹11,700, what would 15 bags cost — and what does this reveal about doubling c?

In the CISCE examination style: (a) Write the general expression that gives the cost of n articles when m identical articles cost ₹c. (1 mark) (b) Using the expression, find the cost of 27 articles when 9 cost ₹423. (2 marks) (c) Using the reverse form, find how many articles can be bought for ₹2,538 at the same rate. (2 marks) (d) State the substitution that verifies your expression, and carry it out for the numbers in (b). (2 marks)

The expression is used with m = 40, c = 1,900. (a) Evaluate for n = 65, stating the unit value exactly as a fraction and as a decimal to the nearest paisa. (b) A student insists the decimal answer "proves the problem is wrong since shopkeepers don't split paise." Evaluate the insistence and state the two lawful endings for such a quotient. (c) For the reverse question with A = ₹3,040, decide whether an exact whole-unit answer exists, showing the working.

A water board's tariff: m = 5 units of 1,000 litres each cost c = ₹187.50. A household used n = 17 such units this month. (a) Compute the bill from the general expression. (b) The board announces: "from next month, the unit value rises by 4%." Predict the new unit value and the new cost of 17 units WITHOUT recomputing from m and c, using the expression's structure. (c) Verify the prediction by recomputing with a new c.

A courier's rate card: ₹90 for the first identical parcel-weight slab and the SAME rate for every further slab. A shipment of 12 slabs costs ₹1,080. (a) Write the cost of x slabs as an expression. (b) A customer has ₹560 — how many slabs can she ship? (c) The courier adds a FLAT ₹40 handling fee per shipment (not per slab). Rewrite the cost expression and decide whether the unitary expression (c ÷ m) × n still prices this new scheme honestly. (6 lines maximum)

In the CISCE past-paper pattern: (a) State the general expression for the cost of n articles when m identical articles cost ₹c, and verify it by substitution. (2 marks) (b) 16 identical steel bottles cost ₹3,888. Find the cost of 21 bottles by the expression. (2 marks) (c) How many bottles can be bought for ₹3,164? (2 marks) (d) Without recomputing fully, state the cost of 42 bottles if the unit value were 50 paise higher, and explain the structural rule used. (2 marks) (e) A rival shop sells the same bottles at ₹245 each. State which shop is cheaper and by how much on a 21-bottle purchase. (2 marks)

State what "per cent" means and what the symbol % denotes. On a 10 × 10 percent-grid, how many small squares must be shaded to show 38%? What percentage does a fully shaded grid show, and what does a grid with 12 squares shaded in ONE row and column pattern show if 2 rows and 8 single squares are shaded?

Meera scores 34 out of 40 in Mathematics and Arjun scores 52 out of 65 in Science. (a) Whose performance is better, decided FAIRLY? (b) A third student claims "Arjun is better because 52 is bigger than 34." Name the exact error in the claim. (c) Express both performances on the hundred-scale.
Estimate each mentally using the friendly-percentage set, stating the composition you used, then verify exactly: (a) 50% of ₹740; (b) 25% of 620 mL; (c) 10% of 5,500 steps; (d) 35% of ₹640.

A shop board reads "FLAT 30% OFF on curtains marked ₹1,200" and a second board "SPECIAL: pay 70% of the marked price". (a) Show that both offers are the same, computing both payable amounts. (b) The shopkeeper says "30% off is better for you because 30 is bigger than 70." Evaluate the claim. (c) Name the whole (the 100%) in this situation.

Design a 10 × 10 percent-grid task that teaches all three boundary cases at once — a percentage equal to 100%, one above 100%, and one below 1% — and write the answer key explaining each case on the grid. Choose specific percentages and describe the shading.

In the CISCE examination style: (a) Write 45% as a fraction in lowest terms. (2 marks) (b) A cricket team won 60% of its 15 matches. How many matches did it win? (2 marks) (c) On a 10 × 10 grid, a figure shades 5 full rows and 4 single squares. State the percentage shaded and the percentage unshaded, and verify the two add to 100%. (3 marks)

A 10 × 10 grid represents a village panchayat of 100 votes (each square = 1 vote). Candidate A's squares number 43, Candidate B's 39, and the rest are NOTA. (a) State each share as a percentage. (b) In the REAL panchayat there are 1,250 voters with the SAME percentages. Find each candidate's votes. (c) B demands a recount claiming "only 4 squares separate us, so the real gap is 4 votes." Evaluate the claim.

A filament uses 0.8% of a 2.5 kW connection's safe load. (a) Find the filament's power in watts. (b) A second appliance draws 150% of the filament's power. Can it run on the same 2.5 kW connection without exceeding the safe load — and at what percentage of the connection? (c) State the two different "wholes" at work in (a) and (b) and why keeping them distinct matters.

A school library survey: fiction 45%, textbooks 30%, comics 8%, and the rest "other". (a) Find the "other" share and verify the sum. (b) The library holds 3,200 books; find the number in each category. (c) Next year the library grows to 4,000 books and comics stay at 8%. A student claims "comics increased by 8%." Evaluate the claim with correct language.

Evaluate each claim TRUE or FALSE with justification: (i) "40% of 50 and 50% of 40 are equal." (ii) "A percentage can be written as a ratio: 35% is 35 : 100, i.e. 7 : 20." (iii) "If A's share is 10 percentage points above B's, then A's amount is 10% more than B's amount."

In the CISCE past-paper pattern: (a) Express 18% as a fraction in lowest terms and as a ratio. (2 marks) (b) A class has 46 students; 26 attended the workshop. What percentage attended, correct to one decimal place? (2 marks) (c) A vendor promised "65% of my 400 mangoes are ripe"; inspection found 238 ripe. Decide whether the promise was kept, showing the percentage arithmetic. (3 marks) (d) On a 10 × 10 grid for (c)'s data, state how many squares would be shaded for ripe mangoes and how the fractional part of the percentage is shown. (3 marks)

State the denominator-100 definition of percentage. Write 45% as a fraction in lowest terms, and convert 7/20 to a percentage by the equivalent-fraction route, showing the scaling factor and the verification.

Express: (a) 24 as a percentage of 64; (b) ₹135 as a percentage of ₹540; (c) 750 grams as a percentage of 1½ kilograms. For each, write the full three-slot sentence and verify by reapplying the percentage.

Keep it exact: (a) write 2/3 as a percentage with a fractional remainder, and show that your percentage of 300 returns exactly 200. (b) Write 9/8 as a percentage and explain why the answer may exceed 100. (c) A student writes 2/3 ≈ 66.67% and calls it exact. Evaluate the wording.

In the CISCE examination style: (a) Write 32% as a fraction in its lowest terms. (2 marks) (b) Express 17/25 as a percentage, showing the scaling factor. (2 marks) (c) Express ₹63 as a percentage of ₹700, writing the full sentence and verifying. (3 marks)

The re-unitising route meets an awkward whole: express 7 as a percentage of 12. (a) Show the exact percentage with any fractional remainder, unsimplified-decimal-free. (b) Verify it on 1,200. (c) A student scales 12 → 100 with factor 8⅓ and writes 7 × 8⅓ = 58⅓%, then writes "= 58.33% exactly". Evaluate the second statement.

A photo is scaled on three screens: 4/5 of original, 95% of original, and 19/20 of original. (a) Dress all three on the denominator-100 scale and rank them. (b) The original is 2,400 pixels wide; find each scaled width. (c) A fourth screen shows 124% of original. Is that lawful by the definition, and what width results?

A two-step chain: 40% of a tank is filled; then HALF of the REMAINING capacity is filled. (a) What percentage of the tank is filled now? (b) Express the second stage's addition as a percentage of the tank. (c) The caretaker reports "we added 50%, so the tank is now 90% full." Diagnose the error precisely and give the correct report.

Evaluate each claim TRUE or FALSE with justification: (i) "Every fraction has an exact percentage." (ii) "9/16 = 56¼%." (iii) "If a is p% of b, then b is (100/p × a) — so the whole can be recovered from the part and the percentage."

In the CISCE past-paper pattern: (a) Express 3/8 as a percentage. (1 mark) (b) Express 108% as a fraction in lowest terms. (2 marks) (c) A student scored 203 marks out of 280. Express the score as a percentage, exact, and state the fraction form used. (3 marks) (d) A water filter has cleaned 697 L of a 2,050 L supply. Express the cleaned part as a percentage of the whole, exact, and verify. (2 marks) (e) Of two schemes, A returns 17/20 of the investment and B returns 82%. Which returns more, and by how many percentage points? (2 marks)
Convert 0.625 to a percentage.
A student says 45% = 0.045. Is this correct? Explain.
In a class of 40 students, 60% are girls. How many girls are there?
Create a fraction in simplest form that converts to 37.5%.
A student claims that converting 0.02 to a percentage gives 0.2%. Critique this claim.
Compare the percentage equivalents of 1/3 and 0.33. Which representation is more accurate and why?

Define cost price and selling price, state the profit and loss conditions with their formulas, and solve: a trader buys a radio for ₹920 and sells it for ₹1,035. Find the profit and the profit percentage.

A shopkeeper sells a saree for ₹1,530 and loses 15%. (a) Find the cost price. (b) Verify your answer. (c) A classmate computes CP = 1,530 + 15% of 1,530 = ₹1,759.50. Diagnose the error precisely and test the classmate's CP against the given SP.

A dealer buys a bicycle for ₹2,400, spends ₹180 on repairs, and sells it for ₹2,808. (a) Compute the true CP and the profit. (b) Find the profit percentage. (c) The dealer's assistant reports "profit ₹408 on a ₹2,400 purchase — 17% profit". Evaluate the report line by line.

Two stalls at a fair: Stall P sold kites bought for ₹900 at a profit of ₹270. Stall Q sold diyas bought for ₹600 at a profit of ₹210. (a) Compute each stall's profit percentage. (b) Which stall's money worked harder, and what would each earn on an equal investment of ₹3,000 at the same rate? (c) State why the raw-profit comparison (270 > 210) gives the wrong crown.

In the CISCE examination style: (a) A goldsmith buys 25 g of gold ornaments-making material for ₹56,000 and sells it for ₹59,500. Find the profit percent. (2 marks) (b) A toy costing ₹350 is sold at a loss of 8%. Find the selling price. (2 marks) (c) A washing machine sold for ₹17,920 yields a profit of 12%. Find the cost price and the profit. (3 marks)

A trader's margin rule: "I price everything at 33⅓% above cost, then offer 10% off during sales." (a) Express the sale price as a percentage of cost, exactly. (b) If an article's sale price is ₹1,200, find the cost price. (c) The trader advertises "big savings — pay 77% of cost!" Evaluate the advertisement using (a).

A farmer sells 50 kg of rice to a wholesaler at 20% profit on his production cost of ₹28/kg. The wholesaler sells the same rice to a retailer at 10% profit on HIS purchase. The retailer sells it at ₹41.58/kg. (a) Find each price in the chain: farmer-to-wholesaler, wholesaler-to-retailer. (b) Verify the final price. (c) The consumer claims "the rice rose 48.5% from farm to plate (20 + 10 + 18.5)". Evaluate the claim with the correct total rise and why the pieces do not add.

A shop's two departments:electronics bought goods at ₹80,000 and sold at ₹92,000; books bought at ₹45,000 and sold at ₹51,300. (a) Compute each department's profit percent. (b) The owner plans to invest next quarter's ₹2,00,000 entirely in one department at the same rates. Compare the projected profits. (c) The electronics manager objects: "compare absolute profits, not percents — we earned more." Settle the objection for a ₹2,00,000 stake.

Evaluate each claim TRUE or FALSE with working: (i) "A 25% profit on CP and a 20% profit on SP are the same rupee profit on the same article." (ii) "If two transactions have equal profit percent, the bigger CP made the bigger rupee profit." (iii) "Selling at 80% of CP always means a 20% loss."

In the CISCE past-paper pattern: (a) A trader buys 40 identical shirts for ₹14,000 and sells 30 of them at ₹420 each. Find his profit percent on the shirts sold so far, taking cost per shirt as your base. (3 marks) (b) The remaining 10 shirts are sold at ₹308 each. Find the profit or loss percent on that batch. (2 marks) (c) Compute the overall profit or loss percent on the whole lot. (3 marks) (d) The trader says "batch 1's profit cancels batch 2's loss." Verify or refute with rupees. (2 marks)
If the principal is ₹1 500, the rate is 8 % per annum, and the time is 3 years, what is the simple interest? Show the substitution steps.
A man borrows ₹4 000 at 7 % per annum simple interest for 5 years. How much total amount must he repay at the end of the period?
A CISCE‑style question: "The simple interest on a sum of money for 2 years at 5 % per annum is ₹250. Find the sum." Solve and give the answer in rupees.
**HOTS:** If the simple interest on a sum for 5 years at 4 % per annum is ₹800, what would be the simple interest on the same sum for 7 years at 5 % per annum?

**Application:** A school library deposits ₹12 000 in a fixed deposit at 6 % per annum simple interest for 2 years. The interest earned is used to buy books costing ₹150 each. How many books can be bought?
**Comparison:** Compare the growth of ₹1 000 at 10 % simple interest and at 10 % compound interest (annually) over 3 years. Present the amounts in a table and state the difference.

**CISCE past‑paper pattern:** "The simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 5 % per annum is ₹200. Find the compound interest on the same sum for the same period at the same rate, compounded annually."
Define speed and write its formula with the two rearrangements. A train covers 260 km uniformly in 6½ hours. Find its speed in km/h and in m/s, showing the conversion factor used.
Convert exactly, showing the fraction used: (a) 63 km/h to m/s; (b) 14 m/s to km/h; (c) 5½ m/s to km/h; (d) State which is faster: 16.5 m/s or 58 km/h.

A scooter covers 90 km in the first 2 hours and 60 km in the next 1½ hours. (a) Find the average speed for the whole journey, exact. (b) A student averages the two leg-speeds (45 and 40 km/h) and reports 42.5 km/h. Diagnose the error and explain why the correct answer differs. (c) State the condition under which averaging the two speeds WOULD give the right answer.

An express train runs at a uniform 25 m/s. (a) Express its speed in km/h. (b) How far does it travel in 2 hours 24 minutes? (c) How long will it take to cross a 1,080 km route? Answer in hours and minutes. (d) Verify (b) and (c) by substitution.

In the CISCE examination style: (a) A bus covers 180 km in 4 hours. Find its average speed in m/s. (2 marks) (b) A motorbike travels at 66 km/h for 2½ hours. Find the distance covered. (2 marks) (c) At a uniform 15 m/s, how long will a van take to cover 81 km? Give the answer in minutes. (3 marks)

Two friends commute the same 12 km route. Priya cycles at a steady 4 m/s but waits 6 minutes at a railway crossing. Qasim cycles at 3.6 m/s with no stop. (a) Find each friend's total travel time, in minutes. (b) Compute each friend's average speed over the 12 km. (c) Qasim claims "I may be slower on the road, but my average is better." Evaluate the claim with the numbers.

A cable-car climbs 1,800 m in 4 minutes, then descends the same 1,800 m in 3 minutes. (a) Find the climb and descent speeds in m/s. (b) Find the average speed for the full up-and-down trip. (c) The operator advertises "average 8.75 m/s — just add the two speeds and halve." Evaluate the advertisement with the exact answer.

A delivery drone's controller works in mixed units: the drone cruises at 12 m/s, must cover a 27 km line, may fly only 40 minutes on one charge, and needs 4 minutes on the ground to swap batteries at the halfway point. (a) Compute the flying time for 27 km at cruise. (b) Decide whether the mission fits one charge, or two charges with the swap. (c) Compute the mission's average speed INCLUDING the battery swap, exact, and state which time the exclude-the-swap average would report.

Evaluate each claim TRUE or FALSE with working: (i) "Walking at 5.4 km/h is the same as walking 1.5 m/s." (ii) "If speed triples and time triples, distance grows nine times." (iii) "For a fixed distance, time and speed are inversely related: doubling speed halves the time."

In the CISCE past-paper pattern: (a) A car covers 240 km in 3 hours 45 minutes. Find its average speed in m/s, exact. (2 marks) (b) A second car averages 16 m/s. Express this in km/h and find the time it needs for 504 km. (2 marks) (c) A cyclist rides 18 km at 12 km/h, then 12 km at 18 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole ride, exact. (3 marks) (d) A third rider covers the same 30 km route in 2 hours flat. State whether the third rider's average beats the cyclist's, and by how much in km/h. (2 marks) (e) State the one definition that decides (c) and (d), and name the shortcut it outlaws. (1 mark)
What is the distance covered by a car travelling at a constant speed of 50 km/h for 2 hours?
A cyclist rides for 30 minutes at 12 km/h. Explain why converting 30 minutes to 0.5 hours is necessary before using d = s × t.
Evaluate the statement: “If a bus travels 150 km in 3 hours, its speed is 45 km/h.” Is the statement correct? Justify.
A train runs at 90 km/h. How far will it travel in 1 hour 20 minutes? Show the conversion step.
CISCE exam‑style: A car covers 180 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. Find its average speed in km/h.
HOTS: Two friends start from the same point. One walks at 4 km/h, the other cycles at 12 km/h. After 45 minutes, how much farther has the cyclist travelled than the walker?
Application: A delivery van travels 240 km at 60 km/h, then continues 150 km at 50 km/h. What is the total distance covered? (Only distance is asked.)
Comparison: Compare the distance covered by a car at 80 km/h for 1.5 hours with a bike at 20 km/h for 6 hours. Which is greater and by how much?
CISCE past‑paper pattern: A train 200 m long passes a pole in 10 seconds. Find the speed of the train in km/h.

State the formula for time from distance and speed and the two proportionality directions. Solve: a goods train covers 252 km at a uniform 42 km/h. Find its running time, and state how the time changes if the distance grows to 294 km at the same speed.

Convert, showing the ÷60 or ×60 line: (a) 3 h 42 min to decimal hours; (b) 4.2 h to h-min; (c) 215 minutes to h-min; (d) A student converts 3 h 42 min to "3.42 h". Diagnose the error and quantify the theft in minutes.

Convert in both directions with the rules stated: (a) 18:45 to 12-hour clock; (b) 7:20 a.m. to 24-hour clock; (c) 00:30 to 12-hour clock; (d) 12:00 noon and 12:00 night — state the 24-hour readings and why the board's "12 a.m." convention is treated carefully in timetables.

In the CISCE examination style: (a) A cyclist covers 27 km at 9 km/h. Find the time taken in hours and minutes. (2 marks) (b) Express 2 h 48 min in decimal hours, showing the division. (2 marks) (c) A flight departs at 23:55 and lands at 05:40 the next day. Find the flight duration, showing the hops. (3 marks)

A city clock runs 4 minutes fast every hour (it advances 64 minutes per true 60). It is set right at 06:00 true time. (a) What does the faulty clock show at 13:00 true time? (b) An appointment is "at 15:30 by the faulty clock". Find the true time. (c) The owner claims "I can just subtract 4 minutes per hour to fix it — 9½ hours fast means 38 minutes slow to fix." Evaluate the claim against your (b).

A two-watch puzzle: watch A gains 90 seconds per day; watch B loses 2 minutes per day. Both are set correct on Monday 10:00. (a) State each watch's reading the FOLLOWING Monday 10:00 true time. (b) Which watch is closer to true time after 3½ days, and by how much? (c) After how many whole days does watch B first read more than 30 minutes slow?

A delivery app's rider plan: pick up at 11:42, ride 6.3 km at 21 km/h, wait 8 minutes at the customer's gate, then ride 4.2 km at 18 km/h. (a) Find each riding leg's minutes and the total delivery duration. (b) Find the delivery-completion time. (c) The app's SLA counts only moving time and demands completion within 40 minutes of pickup.
