दो विद्यार्थियों ने एक ही मंदिर-यात्रा का वर्णन दिया। विद्यार्थी प: "मंदिर पहाड़ी पर है, 300 सीढ़ियाँ हैं, मूर्ति संगमरमर की है, मेला साल में दो बार होता है, यहाँ भोजन-स्थल भी है।" विद्यार्थी फ: "पहाड़ी की सीढ़ियाँ चढ़ते हुए पीछले पड़ाव का शहर छोटा-सा नक्शा-सा दिखता गया; ऊपर पहुँचकर संगमरमर की ठंडी मूर्ति के सामने शोर अपने आप दूर चला गया।" (क) दोनों का मूल्यांकन वर्णन-कसौटी पर कीजिए। (ख) प के वर्णन में क्या है जो फ के वर्णन में नहीं — और वह पर्याप्त क्यों नहीं? (ग) फ के वर्णन में कौन-सा एक आधार विशेष रूप से प्रबल है?

आपको दो विषयों में से चुनकर एक वर्णन देना है: (1) रेलवे-स्टेशन की सुबह-भीड़, (2) अपने घर की छत पर एक शाम। (क) दोनों के लिए उपयुक्त क्रम-सीढ़ी सुझाइए (कारण भी)। (ख) प्रत्येक के लिए एक आरंभ-कुंजी-वाक्य और एक संवेदना-पंक्ति लिखिए। (ग) किस विषय में तथ्य-अनुशासन की ज़रूरत अधिक होगी और क्यों?

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) वर्णन के तीन आधारों के नाम लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) प्रदर्शनी-वर्णन की चार-पड़ाव क्रम-सीढ़ी लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ग) इस वाक्य की दो त्रुटियाँ पहचानिए: "बहुत सुंदर, अद्भुत, अति विशाल प्रदर्शनी-भवन में बहुत ही सुंदर मॉडल थे और मैं बहुत ख़ुश हुआ।" (2 अंक) (घ) आपदा-वर्णन की पाँच-स्तर सीढ़ी के चौथे स्तर का नाम और उसका एक काम लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ई) निम्न में से ऐतिहासिक स्थल के वर्णन के लिए उपयुक्त पहला पड़ाव चुनिए, कारण सहित: (1) "इस इमारत के बारे में कहा जाता है कि इसकी नींव एक रात में रखी गई थी।" (2) "बस से उतरते ही लाल बलुआ पत्थर की ऊँची दीवारें सामने थीं।" (2 अंक) (च) बताइए कि (ई) में चुने न गए विकल्प को वर्णन में कहाँ और कैसे रखा जा सकता था। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-शैली में: (क) समूह-चर्चा की तीन भूमिकाओं के नाम और प्रत्येक का एक काम लिखिए। (3 अंक) (ख) सार-निष्कर्ष में तीन बातों का ध्यान रखा जाता है — वे क्या हैं? (3 अंक) (ग) टिप्पणी-पत्रक पर क्या-क्या दर्ज होता है — दो बातें। (2 अंक) (घ) समूह-चर्चा की चार कसौटियों के नाम लिखिए। (2 अंक)

आपके विद्यालय में नई परियोजना है: 'प्रत्येक कक्षा अपना सफ़ाई-नियम स्वयं बनाएगी।' आपकी कक्षा की चर्चा का आयोजन आपको करना है। (क) आरंभ-कथन की तीन कतारें सुझाइए। (ख) चर्चा को निष्कर्ष तक ले जाने की तीन-चरण योजना (समय-विभाजन सहित, कुल 20 मिनट) लिखिए। (ग) चर्चा की सफलता की जाँच के लिए दो मापनीय लक्षण लिखिए।

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) समूह-चर्चा की तीन भूमिकाएँ लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) विषय 'परीक्षा-भय कैसे कम हो' — आरंभ-कथन (तीन कतारों सहित) लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ग) एक साथी की बात काटकर अपनी पंक्ति बोलने वाले प्रतिभागी की त्रुटि बताते हुए उसे सही जुड़ाव-पंक्ति का एक नमूना दिखाइए — मान लीजिए साथी ने कहा था: "भय तैयारी की कमी से आता है।" (2 अंक) (घ) चर्चा के अंत का तीन-बिंदु सार लिखिए — तीन बिंदु ये थे: तैयारी-योजना, सोच-बदल (भय सामान्य है), और श्वास/विश्राम-तकनीक। (2 अंक) (ई) निम्न सार-पंक्ति में एक त्रुटि पहचानिए: "सार: हमारी चर्चा अच्छी रही; मेरी राय है कि भय तो बस बहाना है; सबने तैयारी पर ज़ोर दिया।" (2 अंक) (च) बताइए कि (घ) के सार में कौन-सी कसौटी पूरी हुई और (ई) में कौन-सी टूटी। (1 अंक)

CISCE परीक्षा पैटर्न में "सुनना और बोलना" आंतरिक मूल्यांकन के लिए एक सामान्य कार्य दिया जाता है: "एक ऑडियो सुनकर ५ प्रश्नों के उत्तर दें, फिर १‑मिनट का भाषण दें।" इस कार्य में सफलता के लिए कौन‑से तीन कौशल सर्वाधिक महत्वपूर्ण हैं?

एक 5-अंक का प्रश्न है: "(क) आरंभ-वाक्य लिखिए। (2) (ख) दो संवेदना-पंक्तियाँ लिखिए। (2) (ग) समापन-वाक्य लिखिए। (1)।" अंक-आवंटन को उत्तर-योजना में बदलिए, और बताइए कि 2-अंक वाले भाग का उत्तर 1-अंक वाले से कैसे भिन्न वज़न का होना चाहिए।

परीक्षा-शैली में: (क) अध्याय के कौशलों की साझा जड़ एक वाक्य में लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) छह प्रश्न-प्रकारों के नाम लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ग) मूल्यांकन-प्रकार के उत्तर-कंकाल के तीन चरण लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) दो सामान्य परीक्षा-त्रुटियों के नाम और उनके निवारक आदतें लिखिए। (3 अंक) (ङ) 4-अंक के उत्तर को अंकों की तराज़ू पर बाँटने का एक नियम लिखिए। (2 अंक)

तीन विद्यार्थियों ने एक ही प्रश्न ("समूह-चर्चा में संचालक की भूमिका समझाइए — 3 अंक") के तीन उत्तर दिए: अ — एक लंबा पैराग्राफ जिसमें संचालक की छह-सात बातें मिश्रित हैं; ब — तीन क्रमबद्ध बिंदु (क्रम-सँभाल, बारी-संतुलन, भटकाव-निवारण), प्रत्येक में एक नमूना-पंक्ति; स — केवल तीन नामों की सूची। (क) अंक-तराज़ू के आधार पर तीनों को अंक-श्रेणी (पूर्ण/आंशिक/न्यून) दीजिए। (ख) अ को उसकी सारी जानकारी के बावजूद आंशिक अंक क्यों? (ग) स का उत्तर आगे कैसे पूरा हो — न्यूनतम जोड़ लिखिए।

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) अध्याय के कौशलों की साझा जड़ लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न दो प्रश्नों के प्रकार पहचानिए: (1) "प्रस्तुति और आशुभाषण की तैयारी में अंतर लिखिए।" (2) "रिया का आशुभाषण-उत्तर: 'मैं बस शुरू कर देती हूँ, तैयारी की ज़रूरत नहीं।' मूल्यांकन कीजिए।" (2 अंक) (ग) प्रश्न (ख)-2 का पूरा उत्तर-कंकाल लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) एक 4-अंक प्रश्न की सबूत-योजना लिखिए — जिसके भाग हैं: क (2 अंक), ख (1 अंक), ग (1 अंक)। (2 अंक) (ई) सात-दिन चक्र का दिन सात क्यों विशेष है — एक कारण। (1 अंक) (च) निम्न में से कौन-सा उत्तर-आरंभ तुलना-प्रश्न के लिए सही है — (1) "प्रस्तुति बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है..." (2) "दोनों में क्रम एक जैसा, तैयारी की गहराई अलग..."? कारण दीजिए। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-शैली में: (क) कविता के कोई तीन आधारभूत तत्वों के नाम लिखिए। (1½ अंक) (ख) 'केंद्रीय भाव' पहचानने की एक कसौटी लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ग) शीर्षक सुझाते समय क्या जोड़ना अनिवार्य है और क्यों — एक उदाहरण से स्पष्ट कीजिए। (2½ अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) कविता की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न दो प्रश्नों के उत्तर-कंकाल की पहली पंक्ति लिखिए: (1) "पंक्तियों का भाव गद्य में स्पष्ट कीजिए।" (2) "उपयुक्त शीर्षक सुझाइए।" (2 अंक) (ग) तुलना-प्रकार का कविता-प्रश्न कैसा हो सकता है — एक उदाहरण लिखिए और उसके उत्तर की समानांतर-कसौटी बताइए। (2 अंक) (घ) एक 4-अंक के भाव-प्रश्न की सबूत-योजना लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ई) मूल्यांकन-प्रकार के कविता-प्रश्न में कसौटी कौन चुनेगा और क्यों? (1 अंक) (च) बताइए कि 'कविता रटने की चीज़ है' की सोच परीक्षा के किस प्रश्न-प्रकार में सबसे पहले टूटती है और क्यों। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-शैली में: (क) कहानी के तीन आधारभूत अंगों के नाम लिखिए। (1½ अंक) (ख) कथा-सार लिखने के तीन नियम बताइए। (1½ अंक) (ग) 'क्यों' प्रकार के प्रश्न (कारण-स्पष्टीकरण) के उत्तर का कंकाल एक उदाहरण से स्पष्ट कीजिए। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) कहानी की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न दो प्रश्नों के उत्तर की पहली पंक्ति लिखिए: (1) "मुख्य पात्र का चरित्र-चित्रण कीजिए।" (2) "कथा-सार लिखिए।" (2 अंक) (ग) 4-अंक के चरित्र-प्रश्न की सबूत-योजना लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) तुलना-प्रकार का कथा-प्रश्न एक उदाहरण से लिखिए और उसकी समानांतर-कसौटी बताइए। (2 अंक) (ई) मूल्यांकन-प्रकार में दिए गए सार की जाँच के तीन बिंदु लिखिए। (1 अंक) (च) 'कहानी में सबसे महत्वपूर्ण अंत है' — इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कसौटी सहित कीजिए। (2 अंक)

पात्र-वाचन पद्धति क्या है? इसे लागू करके बताइए कि निम्न तीन संवाद किस प्रकार के स्वभाव के पात्र की ओर संकेत करते हैं — (1) "तुम्हें कुछ नहीं पता, मैंने तो बीस बरस इसी मोहल्ले में देखे हैं।" (2) "अच्छा तो सुन लूँ, फिर सोचूँगी।" (3) "हँसो मत, मैजी की बात है यह।"

आपकी कक्षा एकांकी-वाचन (पात्रों के संवाद पढ़ने) की गतिविधि कर रही है। (क) गतिविधि से पहले एकांकी की पढ़ाई किस क्रम में करेंगे — चार-परत पद्धति से। (2 अंक) (ख) वाचन में मंच-निर्देशों का क्या उपयोग होगा — दो उपयोग लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ग) वाचन के बाद कक्षा में कौन-सा एक चर्चा-प्रश्न उठाएँगे और क्यों? (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-शैली में: (क) एकांकी के कोई तीन अंग/विशेषताओं के नाम लिखिए। (1½ अंक) (ख) 'मंच-निर्देश का काम' बताने वाले उत्तर के तीन अनिवार्य तत्व लिखिए। (1½ अंक) (ग) एकांकी के अंत के तीन प्रकार बताकर प्रत्येक का एक-एक शब्दों में काम लिखिए। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) एकांकी की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न दो प्रश्नों के उत्तर की पहली पंक्ति लिखिए: (1) "निम्न मंच-निर्देश का महत्व स्पष्ट कीजिए।" (2) "एकांकी और कहानी में अंतर लिखिए।" (2 अंक) (ग) 4-अंक के पात्र-प्रश्न (एकांकी के पात्र का चरित्र-चित्रण) की सबूत-योजना लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) मूल्यांकन-प्रकार में दिए गए पात्र-उत्तर की जाँच के तीन बिंदु लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ई) 'एकांकी छोटी कहानी है' — इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कसौटी सहित कीजिए। (2 अंक) (च) तुलना-प्रकार का एकांकी-प्रश्न कैसा बन सकता है — एक उदाहरण और उसकी समानांतर-कसौटी। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-शैली में: (क) निबंध के त्रि-स्तरीय ढाँचे के तीनों स्तरों के नाम क्रम से लिखिए। (1½ अंक) (ख) बिंदु-सार बनाते समय रखी जाने वाली तीन सावधानियाँ लिखिए। (1½ अंक) (ग) 'विचार-वाक्य का अर्थ स्पष्ट कीजिए' प्रश्न के उत्तर के तीन अनिवार्य चरण लिखिए। (2 अंक)

दो विद्यार्थियों ने एक ही निबंध का केंद्रीय विचार लिखा: अ — "निबंध समय-अनुशासन पर है।"; ब — "लेखक समय-अनुशासन को व्यक्तिगत सफलता और सामाजिक विश्वास दोनों की नींव मानता है।" (क) किसका उत्तर श्रेष्ठ — केंद्रीय-विचार कसौटी से तौलिए। (ख) अ के उत्तर को आगे बढ़ाकर पूर्ण बनाने का नियम लिखिए। (ग) क्या ऐसी स्थिति होती है जहाँ अ का रूप उपयोगी हो? (1 अंक-मूल्य का स्पष्ट उत्तर)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) निबंध की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न दो प्रश्नों के उत्तर की पहली पंक्ति लिखिए: (1) "निबंध के मुख्य बिंदु लिखिए।" (2) "निबंध का प्रकार बताइए।" (2 अंक) (ग) 4-अंक के 'विचार-वाक्य का अर्थ' प्रश्न की सबूत-योजना लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) तुलना-प्रकार का निबंध-प्रश्न कैसा हो सकता है — एक उदाहरण और समानांतर-कसौटी। (2 अंक) (ई) 'निबंध केवल जानकारी का ढेर है' — इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कसौटी सहित कीजिए। (2 अंक) (च) बताइए कि 'पूरा पढ़ लेना ही पढ़ाई है' की सोच परीक्षा में कहाँ सबसे पहले टूटती है। (1 अंक)
उपमा और रूपक की परिभाषा पहचान-संकेत सहित लिखिए, और निम्न दोनों वाक्यों में भेद कीजिए — (1) "राधिका कमल के समान कोमल है।" (2) "राधिका इस घर की लक्ष्मी है।"

पहचान-प्रश्न: निम्न तीन वाक्यों में से प्रत्येक में क्या है (उपमा/रूपक/व्यंग्य) — संकेत-शब्द उद्धृत करके लिखिए: (1) "उसकी बातें नवंबर की हवा जैसी ठंडी थीं।" (2) "परीक्षा कक्षा चुनौतियों का अखाड़ा है।" (3) "वाह, तुम तो गणित में ऋषि-मुनियों की वंशज निकले — वही सूत्र हर बार नई भूल के साथ!"

परीक्षा-शैली में: (क) उपमा-रूपक की पहचान की एक साझी जाँच-तरकीब लिखिए। (1 अंक) (ख) व्यंग्य के उत्तर में 'दोहरा अर्थ' किन दो अंगों में दिखाना होता है? (1½ अंक) (ग) निम्न अंश का संकेत-उद्धरण सहित भेद कीजिए — "यह घड़ी तो सचमुच चमत्कारी है — हर रोज़ दस मिनट अपने आप बढ़ा लेती है।" (2½ अंक)

आपको कहानी के एक पात्र के वर्णन में आए उपमा-रूपकों की सूची बनाकर उनका काम बताना है। (क) सूची बनाते समय प्रत्येक प्रविष्टि में कितने और कौन-कौन तत्व रखेंगे? (2 अंक) (ख) पात्र-वर्णन की दृष्टि से बताइए कि उपमा और रूपक का काम किस चीज़ में भिन्न होता है — एक उदाहरण-जोड़ी से। (2 अंक) (ग) यदि एक ही पात्र के वर्णन में बार-बार एक ही उपमान (जैसे 'शेर') आए तो यह किस बात का संकेत है? (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) व्यंग्य की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न दो प्रश्नों के उत्तर की पहली पंक्ति लिखिए: (1) "निम्न वाक्य में सज्जा-रूप पहचानिए।" (2) "उपर्युक्त व्यंग्य का अर्थ स्पष्ट कीजिए।" (2 अंक) (ग) 4-अंक के अर्थ-स्पष्टीकरण प्रश्न (सज्जा-युक्त अंश) की सबूत-योजना लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) तुलना-प्रकार का प्रश्न इस पाठ से कैसा बन सकता है — एक उदाहरण और समानांतर-कसौटी। (2 अंक) (ई) 'मज़ाक की बात ही व्यंग्य है' — इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कसौटी सहित कीजिए। (1 अंक) (च) बताइए कि 'शब्दों की सतह पर चलना' परीक्षा में किन दो प्रश्न-प्रकारों में सबसे पहले चोट खाता है। (2 अंक)

निम्न स्थितियों में से प्रत्येक के लिए पत्र-प्रकार चुनकर उसका कारण एक वाक्य में लिखिए: (1) अंकल अमर को दीपावली की शुभकामनाएँ। (2) नगर-निगम अधिकारी को मोहल्ले में जमा पानी की शिकायत। (3) बड़ी बहन को परीक्षा-सफलता की बधाई।

परीक्षा-शैली में: (क) प्रार्थना-पत्र की त्रिकोणीय बनावट के तीनों तत्व लिखिए। (1½ अंक) (ख) रजिस्टर-जाँच के तीन सूत्र लिखिए। (1½ अंक) (ग) पत्र-लेखन की क़दम-वार पद्धति के पाँचों क़दम क्रम से लिखिए। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) पत्र की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न दो प्रश्नों के उत्तर की पहली क्रिया लिखिए: (1) "निम्न स्थिति के लिए पूर्ण पत्र लिखिए।" (2) "निम्न पत्र में ढाँचा-त्रुटियाँ पहचानकर सुधारिए।" (2 अंक) (ग) 4-अंक के पूर्ण-पत्र प्रश्न की सबूत-योजना (अंक-विभाजन सहित) लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) तुलना-प्रकार का पत्र-प्रश्न कैसा बन सकता है — उदाहरण और समानांतर-कसौटी। (2 अंक) (ई) 'पत्र लेखन अब व्यर्थ है' — इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कसौटी सहित। (1 अंक) (च) बताइए कि 'पहले लिखना शुरू कर देना' की आदत पत्र-परीक्षा में कहाँ चोट खाती है। (2 अंक)
CISCE परीक्षा में डायरी लेखन के लिए दिए गए विषय “अपने पहले रेल यात्रा का वर्णन करो” पर ८०-१०० शब्दों में प्रविष्टि लिखो।

निम्न तीन स्थितियों के लिए नोटिस का 'विशेषता-तत्व' क्या होगा — एक-एक वाक्य में लिखिए: (1) कक्षा 8 के लिए विज्ञान-क्विज़ प्रतियोगिता की नोटिस। (2) हानि-नोटिस — विद्यालय पुस्तकालय की एक पुस्तक खो गई। (3) वार्षिकोत्सव की नोटिस।
स्थिति: आप सोमनाथ विद्यालय के खेल-सचिव हैं। पूर्ण नोटिस लिखिए — निम्न जानकारियों से: अंतर्विद्यालय क्रिकेट-प्रतियोगिता, 20-22 अक्टूबर, विद्यालय-मैदान, कक्षा 7-8, नाम 15 अक्टूबर तक खेल-प्रभारी को।

परीक्षा-शैली में: (क) नोटिस और पत्र के भेद के तीन आधार लिखिए। (1½ अंक) (ख) हानि-नोटिस में 'पहचान-चिह्न' क्यों अनिवार्य है — एक कारण। (1 अंक) (ग) निम्न नोटिस-अंश में दो त्रुटियाँ पहचानकर सुधारिए — "प्रिय विद्यार्थियों, हमारी प्रतियोगिता बहुत रोचक होगी, सभी अवश्य आएँ, याद रखें देखते हैं।"

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) नोटिस की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न दो प्रश्नों के उत्तर की पहली क्रिया लिखिए: (1) "निम्न स्थिति के लिए नोटिस लिखिए।" (2) "निम्न नोटिस में त्रुटियाँ पहचानकर सुधारिए।" (2 अंक) (ग) 4-अंक के नोटिस-प्रश्न की सबूत-योजना (अंक-विभाजन सहित) लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) तुलना-प्रकार का प्रश्न इस पाठ से कैसा बन सकता है — उदाहरण और समानांतर-कसौटी। (2 अंक) (ई) 'नोटिस पत्र का छोटा रूप है' — इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कसौटी सहित। (1 अंक) (च) बताइए कि 'भावना-शब्दों का प्रवेश' नोटिस-परीक्षा में कहाँ-कहाँ अंक काटता है — दो स्थान। (2 अंक)
आपको अपने विद्यालय की "पुस्तक मेला" रिपोर्ट प्रधानाचार्य को देनी है। प्रतिवेदन के किस भाग में आप "पुस्तक मेला २०२५" लिखेंगे और क्यों?

एक ही समाचार के लिए तीन सुर्खियाँ दी गई हैं — (1) "पेड़" (2) "नगर निगम की बैठक में अनेक विषयों पर विचार हुआ" (3) "तीन सौ पेड़ों की कटान को निगम ने दी हरी झंडी"। कसौटी के चार तोलों से श्रेष्ठ सुर्खी चुनिए और प्रत्येक का मूल्यांकन एक-एक पंक्ति में कीजिए।

परीक्षा-शैली में: (क) श्रेष्ठ-सुर्खी चयन के चारों तोलों के नाम लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ख) 'तथ्य-मोती' से क्या तात्पर्य है — एक उदाहरण से स्पष्ट कीजिए। (2 अंक) (ग) निम्न समाचार के लिए एक सुर्खी गढ़िए — "विद्यालय की स्वच्छता-समिति ने रविवार को मोहल्ले की सार्वजनिक झील की सफ़ाई अभियान चलाया। लगभग दो सौ किलोग्राम कचरा निकाला गया।" (2 अंक)

आपके सहपाठी ने सुर्खी-प्रश्न में यह उत्तर लिखा — "सुर्खी: विद्यालय का वार्षिकोत्सव बहुत ही शानदार और यादगार रहा। सभी ने खूब सराहना की। यह गर्व का क्षण था।" (क) त्रुटियाँ गिनिए। (ख) सुधरी सुर्खी लिखिए (समाचार के मुख्य तथ्य मानकर: वार्षिकोत्सव 18 नवंबर को, बारह सांस्कृतिक कार्यक्रम, लगभग चार सौ दर्शक)। (ग) यह त्रुटि आई क्यों — मूल सोच बताइए।

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) सुर्खी की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न दो प्रश्नों के उत्तर की पहली क्रिया लिखिए: (1) "समाचार पढ़कर सुर्खी लिखिए।" (2) "दी गई दो सुर्खियों में से श्रेष्ठ का चयन कारण सहित कीजिए।" (2 अंक) (ग) 4-अंक के सुर्खी-प्रश्न की सबूत-योजना (अंक-विभाजन सहित) लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) 'सुर्खी और शीर्षक एक ही चीज़ हैं' — इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कसौटी सहित कीजिए। (2 अंक) (ई) बताइए कि 'पहली पंक्ति पढ़कर ही सुर्खी बनाना' की आदत परीक्षा में कहाँ चोट खाती है। (1 अंक) (च) तुलना-प्रकार का प्रश्न इस पाठ से कैसा बन सकता है — उदाहरण और समानांतर-कसौटी। (2 अंक)

स्थिति: आप अपनी नगर में पुराने मकान का एक कमरा किराये पर देना चाहते हैं। वर्गीकृत विज्ञापन के चारों खाने भरकर पूर्ण विज्ञापन लिखिए (जानकारियाँ: कक्षा 8-ब, दो कमरे, अलग प्रवेश-द्वार, किराया ₹3,000 मासिक, गांधी नगर)।

एक ही स्थिति ('विद्यालय की पुस्तकालय-किताबें खरीदने हेतु विक्रेताओं से प्रस्ताव आमंत्रण') के लिए दो लेखन उत्तर दिए गए हैं — अ: "भर्ती / पुस्तकें ख़रीदनी हैं। अच्छी कंपनी की हों। संपर्क: पुस्तकालय।" ब: "प्रस्ताव आमंत्रण / पुस्तकालय हेतु हिंदी-अंग्रेज़ी पुस्तकों की आपूर्ति हेतु विक्रेताओं से शुल्क-प्रस्ताव आमंत्रित; नमूना-सूची सहित आवेदन 15 मई तक। संपर्क सूत्र: पुस्तकालय-प्रभारी।" — तौलिए कौन पूर्ण है और क्यों।

परीक्षा-शैली में: (क) वर्गीकृत विज्ञापन के चारों तत्वों में से किन्हीं तीन के नाम और काम लिखिए। (1½ अंक) (ख) नाम-वाक्यांश स्वर का अर्थ एक उदाहरण-जोड़ी (ग़लत/सही) से स्पष्ट कीजिए। (2 अंक) (ग) निम्न स्थिति के लिए पूर्ण वर्गीकृत विज्ञापन लिखिए — आपकी साइकिल (हीरो कंपनी, एक वर्ष पुरानी, अच्छी अवस्था) बिक्री हेतु है; मूल्य ₹2,500; संपर्क: कक्षा 8-अ। (2½ अंक)

आपको अपने विद्यालय के विज्ञान-क्लब हेतु एक रसायन-सेट ख़रीदना है और आप सोच रहे हैं कि इसकी जानकारी वर्गीकृत विज्ञापन से कैसे ली जाए। (क) 'ख़रीदना है' प्रस्ताव के लिए वर्ग-शीर्षक क्या होगा और विवरण-खाने कौन-कौन से? (2 अंक) (ख) स्थिति में वर्गीकृत विज्ञापन पढ़ते समय (लेखन की नहीं, खोज की दृष्टि से) आप किन तीन जाँचों से विज्ञापन की विश्वसनीयता तोलेंगे? (3 अंक) (ग) लेखक-दृष्टि और खोजक-दृष्टि — दोनों में से किसमें चार-खाने का उल्टा क्रम उपयोगी होता है (संपर्क → विवरण → प्रस्ताव → वर्ग)? कारण दीजिए। (1 अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) वर्गीकृत विज्ञापन की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न दो प्रश्नों के उत्तर की पहली क्रिया लिखिए: (1) "स्थिति के अनुसार वर्गीकृत विज्ञापन लिखिए।" (2) "निम्न विज्ञापन की त्रुटियाँ सुधारिए।" (2 अंक) (ग) 4-अंक के वर्गीकृत विज्ञापन-प्रश्न की सबूत-योजना (अंक-विभाजन सहित) लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) 'वर्गीकृत विज्ञापन और नोटिस एक ही हैं' — इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कसौटी सहित। (2 अंक) (ई) बताइए कि 'उत्पाद-विज्ञापन की शैली का वर्गीकृत पर वहन' कहाँ-कहाँ अंक काटता है — दो स्थान। (2 अंक) (च) तुलना-प्रकार का प्रश्न इस पाठ से कैसा बन सकता है — उदाहरण और समानांतर-कसौटी। (2 अंक)
विषय: सड़क-सुरक्षा। (क) एक नारा गढ़िए। (2 अंक) (ख) नारे के बाद की कारण-पंक्ति और कार्य-आह्वान लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ग) बताइए कि यह विज्ञापन वर्गीकृत से स्वर में किस चीज़ में भिन्न है — एक बिंदु। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-शैली में: (क) जनहित विज्ञापन की पाँच भाषा-संरचनात्मक विशेषताएँ में से कोई तीन लिखिए। (1½ अंक) (ख) निम्न जनहित-अंश की दो त्रुटियाँ पहचानकर सुधारिए — "पानी की कमी हो रही है। लोग अपने-अपने घर में पानी बचाएँ। — जल विभाग"। (2½ अंक) (ग) 'धुरी-प्रथम' नियम क्या है और यह क्यों आवश्यक है — एक कारण। (1 अंक)

आपको विद्यालय के वार्षिकोत्सव के लिए 'पुस्तक-दान' पर जनहित विज्ञापन तैयार करना है जो पोस्टर और घोषणा-पत्री दोनों पर लगेगा। (क) पोस्टर-स्वर में आप कौन-सा एक नारा और कौन-सी दो पंक्तियाँ चुनेंगे — क्यों? (2 अंक) (ख) पोस्टर पर जारीकर्ता-पहचान क्यों आवश्यक है — दो कारण। (2 अंक) (ग) एक ही नारा यदि रेडियो/घोषणा के लिए हो तो उसमें क्या एक संशोधन उपयोगी होगा — कारण सहित। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) जनहित विज्ञापन की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न दो प्रश्नों के उत्तर की पहली क्रिया लिखिए: (1) "विषय पर जनहित विज्ञापन लिखिए।" (2) "तीनों विज्ञापन-प्रकारों में भेद स्पष्ट कीजिए।" (2 अंक) (ग) 4-अंक के जनहित-प्रश्न की सबूत-योजना (अंक-विभाजन सहित) लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) 'जनहित और उत्पाद-विज्ञापन एक जैसे हैं' — इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कसौटी सहित। (2 अंक) (ई) बताइए कि 'केवल नारा लिख देना' की आदत परीक्षा में कहाँ-कहाँ चोट खाती है — दो स्थान। (2 अंक) (च) तुलना-प्रकार का प्रश्न इस पाठ से कैसा बन सकता है — उदाहरण और समानांतर-कसौटी। (2 अंक)

एक ही वस्तु (ताज़ा फल-रस की बोतल) के लिए दो विज्ञापन-पंक्तियाँ दी गई हैं — अ: "फल-रस: एक लीटर, ₹90। बिक्री-केंद्र: विद्यालय-कैंटीन।" ब: "पेड़ का रस, पेड़ की ताज़गी! देसी फलों से बना शुद्ध रस — बिना चीनी की मिलावट। वार्षिकोत्सव-विशेष: एक के साथ एक मुफ़्त! आज ही विद्यालय-कैंटीन में।" — तौलिए कौन पूर्ण उत्पाद-विज्ञापन है और क्यों।

परीक्षा-शैली में: (क) उत्पाद-विज्ञापन की पाँच भाषा-विशेषताएँ में से कोई तीन लिखिए। (1½ अंक) (ख) निम्न विज्ञापन की दो त्रुटियाँ पहचानकर सुधारिए — "जूस की बोतलें। अच्छे जूस। सबको ख़रीदना चाहिए। — राहुल"। (2½ अंक) (ग) लक्ष्य-पाठक-प्रथम नियम क्या है — एक उदाहरण से स्पष्ट कीजिए। (1 अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) उत्पाद-बिक्री विज्ञापन की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) निम्न दो प्रश्नों के उत्तर की पहली क्रिया लिखिए: (1) "वस्तु के लिए विज्ञापन लिखिए।" (2) "तीन विज्ञापन-प्रकारों में भेद स्पष्ट कीजिए।" (2 अंक) (ग) 4-अंक के उत्पाद-विज्ञापन प्रश्न की सबूत-योजना (अंक-विभाजन सहित) लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) 'उत्पाद-विज्ञापन और वर्गीकृत विज्ञापन एक ही हैं' — इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कसौटी सहित। (2 अंक) (ई) बताइए कि 'गुण-सूची लंबी लिख देना' की आदत परीक्षा में कहाँ-कहाँ चोट खाती है — दो स्थान। (2 अंक) (च) तुलना-प्रकार का प्रश्न इस पाठ से कैसा बन सकता है — उदाहरण और समानांतर-कसौटी। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: 'वृद्धा' (प्रेमचंद — गद्य-कथा) और 'काकी' (सियारामशरण गुप्त — कविता) — दोनों पाठों में वृद्ध-स्त्री की उपेक्षा का विषय है। (क) तुलना-कसौटी लिखिए — किन तीन बिंदुओं पर दोनों को साथ तौलेंगे। (2 अंक) (ख) प्रत्येक बिंदु पर दोनों का भेद एक-एक पंक्ति में। (3 अंक) (ग) तुलना का एक-वाक्य निष्कर्ष। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) पद-विधा की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) "मेरो तो गिरधर गोपाल, दूसरो न कोय" का भावार्थ लिखिए और बताइए कि यह मीरा की किस धारा का उदाहरण है। (3 अंक) (ग) साखी और पद की तुलना-तालिका के चार बिंदु लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) किसी पद का भावार्थ लिखते समय कौन-से तीन चरण चलाना होगा — क्रम सहित। (2 अंक) (ई) 'मीरा केवल भजन-कवयित्री हैं' — इस कथन का मूल्यांकन दो परतों की कसौटी से। (2 अंक) (च) इस इकाई से एक तुलना-प्रश्न (साखी-पद) कैसे बनेगा — प्रश्न-रूप और कसौटी लिखिए। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) वर्णन (चित्र-काव्य) शैली की परिभाषा एक वाक्य में दीजिए। (1 अंक) (ख) वात्सल्य रस के दो स्वर (दोनों पात्रों के मन) लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ग) सूर के वर्णन-पदों के पाँच तत्व क्रम से लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) मीरा-सूर भेद की दो कसौटियाँ बताइए। (2 अंक) (ई) 'सूर के चित्र बातूनी हैं' — इसका अर्थ और महत्व दो वाक्यों में। (2 अंक) (च) इस इकाई से एक रस-तुलना प्रश्न कैसे बनेगा — प्रश्न-रूप और कसौटी लिखिए। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) उत्पत्ति के आधार पर शब्द के चार भेद एक-एक उदाहरण सहित लिखिए। (2 अंक) (ख) तद्भव शब्दों से तत्सम लिखिए — नाँव, खेत, छह — और प्रत्येक का नियम-रेखा बताइए। (3 अंक) (ग) 'बेकार' और 'लिखावट' में पहचान-कार्य करके बताइए कि उपसर्ग-प्रत्यय का भेद-सूत्र क्या है। (2 अंक) (घ) 'पंकज' का अर्थ-निर्णय भेद-कसौटी से कीजिए। (2 अंक) (ई) बताइए कि तीन वर्गीकरण एक-दूसरे के विकल्प क्यों नहीं हैं। (2 अंक) (च) इस पाठ से एक द्वि-दिशा रूपांतरण प्रश्न कैसे बनेगा — प्रश्न-रूप और कसौटी लिखिए। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) संज्ञा के तीन भेद एक-एक उदाहरण सहित। (2 अंक) (ख) वाक्य में कारक-पहचान: "पिताजी ने बहन के लिए बाज़ार से मिठाई लाए" — चार कारक और चिह्न। (2 अंक) (ग) सर्वनाम के छह भेदों के नाम। (1 अंक) (घ) विशेषण के चार भेद एक-एक उदाहरण सहित। (2 अंक) (ई) 'अच्छा लड़का' को स्त्रीलिंग बहुवचन और कर्म-कारक में बदलकर नियम-नाम लिखिए। (2 अंक) (च) इस पाठ से एक शोधन-प्रश्न कैसे बनेगा — प्रश्न-रूप और कसौटी लिखिए। (2 अंक)

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) क्रिया के तीन भेदों (प्रेरणार्थक, संयुक्त, मिश्र) के नाम एक-एक उदाहरण सहित। (2 अंक) (ख) 'सीता ने चित्र बनाए।' का कर्मवाच्य त्रिकदम-नियम सहित। (2 अंक) (ग) वाक्य-भेद (रचना-आधार) के तीनों नाम जोड़-धागे के संकेत सहित। (2 अंक) (घ) अव्यय की पाँच श्रेणियों के नाम। (1 अंक) (ई) दो मुहावरों के अर्थ और वाक्य-प्रयोग लिखिए। (2 अंक) (च) इस पाठ से एक द्वि-क्षेत्र शोधन-प्रश्न (क्रिया + विराम-चिह्न) कैसे बनेगा — प्रश्न-रूप और कसौटी लिखिए। (2 अंक)
थीम 3 (व्याकरण और भाषा) के तीन क्षेत्रों के नाम और प्रत्येक की एक-एक मुख्य कसौटी लिखिए।
अंक-तराज़ू की अपेक्षाएँ समझाइए: 'संज्ञा के तीन भेद उदाहरण सहित (3 अंक)' और 'दो मुहावरों का अर्थ और वाक्य-प्रयोग (4 अंक)' — प्रत्येक में अंक कैसे बँटे होंगे और उत्तर-पूर्णता क्या होगी?

परीक्षा-पद्धति में: (क) तीन क्षेत्रों के नाम + प्रत्येक की मुख्य कसौटी। (2 अंक) (ख) पाँच प्रश्न-प्रकारों के नाम। (1 अंक) (ग) दो कंकालों (रूपांतरण-शोधन) के खाने लिखिए। (2 अंक) (घ) 'अंक-संख्या से बिंदु-गणना' नियम एक उदाहरण से। (2 अंक) (ई) तीन सामान्य त्रुटियों के तीन निवारक (क्रियान्वयन-रूप में)। (3 अंक) (च) सप्ताह-चक्र का बंद-सूत्र एक वाक्य में। (1 अंक) (छ) इस अध्याय से एक द्वि-क्षेत्र मिश्रित प्रश्न कैसे बनेगा — प्रश्न-रूप और उसकी परख-कसौटी। (2 अंक)
A student writes: “The Renaissance began in 1500 because that is when Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa.” Apply correct chronological reasoning to correct the statement.
Create a one‑sentence definition of the Renaissance that a Class 8 student could use in a timeline project.
If you were a patron in 1500 Florence, which Renaissance feature would you most likely support and why?
Past‑paper style: “Explain two ways in which the Renaissance contributed to the growth of scientific thinking in Europe.” (4 marks)

SOURCE-BASED: At the Diet of Worms (1521), tradition records Luther's refusal in words like these: "Unless I am convinced by Scripture and by plain reason — I do not accept the authority of popes and councils, for they have contradicted each other — my conscience is captive to the Word of God. I cannot and will not recant, for to go against conscience is neither right nor safe." State TWO authorities Luther rejects in this extract, the ONE authority he accepts, and what the extract reveals about why the Reformation could not be settled by a simple order.

On a timeline strip appear: 1450s (Gutenberg), 1517, 1521, 1529, 1534, 1536, 1540, 1545–63. Place each date's event and label each as SPARK, TRIAL, NAME, STATUTE, DOCTRINE, WEAPON, or ANSWER — then state which two dates belong to forces OUTSIDE the strictly religious story and what each brought to it.

APPLICATION: Your school library receives a facsimile " Geneva Bible-room kit" — facsimile pages, a card reading "by 1560 Europe's vernacular Bibles numbered in the dozens of editions", and a question stand for visitors. Draft the three questions the stand should pose, each answerable from the Reformation chapter, and state what each question TEACHES — then answer your own three questions in one line each.
"It is wrong to say Europe before 1750 had no machines or industry." Evaluate this claim, using TWO pieces of evidence from mining and metals and TWO from milling and manufacturing.

On a timeline strip appear: 1660, 1688, 1694, 1701, 1709, 1712, and "from the mid-1700s". Place each date's event and label each as KNOWLEDGE, STABILITY, CREDIT, SEED, METAL, POWER, or FOOD-AND-LABOUR — then state which two labels belong to preparations so quiet that a newspaper of the day would never have printed them, and why that silence matters to a historian.
How did the Factory Act of 1833 attempt to mitigate a negative impact of the Industrial Revolution?
Apply the concept of “technological unemployment” to the displacement of Indian hand‑loom weavers after 1813.

DESIGN: plan a classroom wall map for "Three Doors, Thirty Years (1488–1522)": state the four route-lines you will draw with their captain and date, the three symbols you will place (with what each represents), the one Indian port that must be starred and why, and the caption sentence beneath the map that carries the chapter's theme.

On a timeline strip appear: 1453, 1460, 1488, 1492, 1494, 1498, 1510, 1519–22. Place each date's event and label each as SQUEEZE, ORGANISER, DOOR, WRONG-WAY, DIVISION, DELIVERY, FOOTHOLD, ROUND-WORLD — then state which two labels belong to consequences that no planner of the voyages intended, and what each unintended thing grew into.

SOURCE-BASED: Francis Bacon wrote in his *Novum Organum* (1620) that the invention of printing, gunpowder and the compass (the magnet) had "changed the whole face and state of things throughout the world" — in learning, in warfare, and in navigation. Identify which chapter movements Bacon's three inventions each belong to or enabled, explain why he calls their effect "changed... the whole face and state of things", and give ONE invention absent from his list that the chapter shows was equally world-changing — with your defence of its absence being forgivable.

On a timeline strip appear: 1453, 1450s, 1488, 1498, 1517, 1648, 1712, 1769. Place each date's event and label each as SQUEEZE, PRESS, DOOR, DELIVERY, SPARK, RECKONING, POWER, VALVE — then state which two labels mark MOMENTS OF COST rather than of achievement, and what each cost was.

CISCE past-paper pattern: "Assess the statement: 'Between 1450 and 1800 Europe was remade — and the world with it.'" Answer in four heads: (a) the remaking of the mind (two facts); (b) the remaking of faith and states (two facts); (c) the remaking of work and wealth (two facts); (d) the remaking of the WORLD beyond Europe — with its two-sided cost-and-gain balance — and your one-line final verdict.

DESIGN: build the blueprint for a 40-mark class test on this chapter: its two sections, the question forms and mark splits in each, the coverage rule (which parts of the chapter each section must touch), the timing instruction you would print on top, and one deliberate trap you would set to reward the spine-commanded student.

HOTS: Two scripts answer "Why did the Industrial Revolution begin in Britain?" HOTS: Place the uprising beside the earlier risings of Chapter 05 (Kol 1831–32; Santhal Hul 1855–56; Indigo Revolt 1859–60) on three axes — CAUSE (whose grievance), SCALE (who joined), and STAKE (what was claimed) — and give the verdict: was 1857 a new KIND of rising, or the old kind grown large? A man sells two cycles for ₹2,400 each — one at 20% profit and the other at 20% loss. Find his total profit or loss percent.
A hawker buys 100 oranges at ₹3 each; 10 oranges spoil. He sells the rest at ₹3.60 each. Find his overall gain or loss percent.
A trader sells an article at 10% profit. Had he sold it for ₹45 more, he would have gained 15%. Find the cost price, and explain why the ₹45 equals 5% of CP and not 15% of CP.
(HOTS) The profit made in selling 25 articles equals the cost price of 5 articles. Find the profit percent, and state the general rule when profit on selling n articles equals CP of m articles.

(Application) A wholesaler sells rice at 8% profit. A retailer buys 500 kg, but 20 kg is spoiled in storage. At what percent above his purchase price per kg must the retailer sell the remaining rice to make a 20% profit on his total investment?
(Evaluation) Two shopkeepers sell the same model of shoes at ₹1,650. One claims "10% profit", the other "10% loss". A customer concludes both earned the same money. Evaluate.
(Past-paper pattern) A person sells an article at a loss of 12%. Had he sold it for ₹104 more, he would have gained 14%. Find the cost price of the article and both selling prices. (ICSE-style.)
A trader buys a sewing machine for ₹9,000 and spends ₹600 on transport and ₹400 on a new belt. He sells it for ₹11,000. Find his profit percent.
A merchant wants a 20% profit on a freezer he bought for ₹18,000, after spending ₹1,500 on delivery and ₹500 on a stabilizer. At what price must he sell it?
By selling aused scooter for ₹23,100, a dealer made a 10% profit after spending ₹1,100 on repairs. What was his purchase price?
A bookseller buys 50 dictionaries at ₹320 each, pays ₹800 freight on the lot, and sells every copy for ₹400. Find his profit percent.

(HOTS) A dealer sells a washing machine at 15% profit on the net cost price. He spends 10% of the purchase price on transport. Show that his profit on the bare purchase price is 16.5%, and explain why the profit rate is higher on the smaller base.

(HOTS) An article's net cost price is made of purchase price P and overheads equal to 25% of P. If it is sold at 10% loss on net CP, express the loss as a percentage of P, and find P when the loss amounts to ₹150.

(Application) A Kirana wholesaler buys 200 tins of oil at ₹180 each; freight for the lot is ₹2,400. He sells 150 tins at ₹210 each and the remaining 50 tins at ₹195 each during a clearance. Find his overall profit or loss percent.

(Past-paper pattern) A man buys an article and spends ₹350 on its repair. He sells it for ₹4,860 at a profit of 20% on his total outlay. Find the purchase price, and the profit he would have made had he sold it at the same price WITHOUT spending on repairs (profit on purchase price alone, stated as a percent). (ICSE-style two-part.)
What is the discount amount when an article marked ₹1,200 is sold for ₹1,020?
A pair of shoes is marked ₹2,500. The shopkeeper allows a discount of 12 %. Find the selling price.
Evaluate: “If the discount percent is 20 %, the selling price is 80 % of the cost price.”
A trader marks his goods 30 % above the cost price and then allows a discount of 10 % on the marked price. If the cost price is ₹500, find the selling price.
A shopkeeper allows a discount of 8 % on a toy and still makes a profit of 12 %. If the cost price of the toy is ₹250, find the marked price.

A shopkeeper marks an article 40 % above its cost price and then gives a discount of 25 % on the marked price. Is the shopkeeper making a profit or a loss? Justify with calculations assuming CP = ₹500.
A customer sees a jacket marked ₹3,000 with a tag “15 % off”. He also has a coupon for an additional ₹200 off the discounted price. What is the final price he pays?
Critique the statement: “If a shopkeeper gives a discount of 10 % and then increases the marked price by 10 %, the selling price returns to the original marked price.”
Compare the effective discount when a single discount of 30 % is given versus two successive discounts of 20 % and 10 % on the same marked price. Which is better for the buyer?
A past ICSE question: “The marked price of a fan is ₹1,200. The shopkeeper allows a discount of 10 % and still gains 20 %. Find the cost price of the fan.”
A pair of shoes is priced at ₹1,600 and GST is 12%. Find the amount a customer pays.
A tourist pays ₹5,310 for a handicraft item including 18% GST. Find the price of the item before tax and the tax amount.
An article is marked at ₹3,000. The shop allows a 15% discount and charges 12% GST on the balance. Find the final bill and the GST amount.
An intra-state sale attracts GST of 18%. On a taxable value of ₹7,500, state the CGST and SGST amounts and the total bill.
A trader buys a fan for ₹1,200 (his cost) and sells it for ₹1,500 plus 18% GST. State his profit, and explain whether GST affects it.
(HOTS) A shopkeeper sells an article for ₹5,400 including 8% GST. He claims, "My taxable value is 5,400 − 8% of 5,400 = ₹4,968." Reconstruct the correct taxable value and quantify his error.
(HOTS) An article's bill with 18% GST exceeds its bill with 5% GST by ₹988. Find the taxable value, and express the two bills as a percentage of it.

(Application) A trader sells a sofa for ₹16,000 plus 18% GST. The customer has a store credit coupon worth ₹1,000 that is applied to the taxable value before tax. Compute the bill, and state the taxable value on which GST is legally charged.
(Past-paper pattern) The price of a mobile phone is ₹13,000. The shop gives a discount of 10% and then charges GST. If the customer pays ₹13,860 in all, find the rate of GST. (ICSE-style.)
What is the simple interest on ₹8,000 at 9% per annum for 2 years?
A sum of ₹5,000 is invested at 8% p.a. compounded yearly for 3 years. Find the compound interest.
Evaluate: For the same principal, rate, and time (2 years), which is larger — simple interest or compound interest compounded half‑yearly? Justify.
Apply: Ravi borrows ₹12,000 at 6% p.a. simple interest for 3 years. Sita deposits ₹12,000 at 6% p.a. compounded yearly for 3 years. Who pays/receives more interest and by how much?

Create a word problem where the difference between simple interest and half‑yearly compound interest for 1.5 years (3 half‑yearly steps) on ₹20,000 at 12% p.a. is exactly ₹108. Provide the problem statement and the solution.
CISCE exam‑style: A sum of money amounts to ₹13,310 in 3 years at 10% p.a. compounded yearly. Find the principal and the simple interest on the same principal for 3 years at the same rate.
**HOTS:** If the difference between compound interest (yearly) and simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 5% p.a. is ₹25, find the sum.

**Application:** A farmer takes a loan of ₹1,00,000 at 12% p.a. simple interest for 3 years. The bank offers an alternative: same principal, 12% p.a. compounded half‑yearly for 3 years (6 steps). Which option costs less interest and by how much?

**Evaluation/Critique:** A textbook states: “For any principal, rate, and time, compound interest compounded half‑yearly is always greater than compound interest compounded yearly.” Critique this statement for the domain of this node (up to 3 years yearly, up to 3 half‑yearly steps).

**Comparison:** Compare the growth of ₹5,000 at 10% p.a. under (a) simple interest for 3 years, (b) yearly compound interest for 3 years, (c) half‑yearly compound interest for 1.5 years (3 steps). Rank the final amounts from smallest to largest.
**CISCE past‑paper pattern:** A sum of money becomes ₹14,641 in 2 years at 10% p.a. compounded yearly. Find the sum and the simple interest on it for 3 years at the same rate.
For each pair decide whether y varies directly or inversely with x, and give the constant: (a) x = 3, 5, 8 with y = 6, 10, 16; (b) x = 4, 6, 10 with y = 15, 10, 6.
On a road map, 3 cm represents 70 km. Two cities are 9.6 cm apart on the map. Find the actual distance.
A tank is filled by 8 pipes in 6 hours. How long will 12 pipes of the same kind take to fill it?
A bus covers 360 km at a steady speed of 60 km/h. (a) How long does the journey take? (b) If it re-runs the route at 90 km/h, find the new time, and name the variation involved.
(HOTS) If x varies directly as y² and x = 72 when y = 3, find x when y = 6, and explain why "x doubles when y doubles" is wrong here.
(HOTS) a varies directly as b, and b varies inversely as c. Given a = 20 when b = 4 and c = 3, find a when c = 2, and derive a general formula for a in terms of c.

(Application) A 1.5-metre stick casts a 2-metre shadow at a certain hour. At the same hour, a temple gopuram's shadow measures 44 metres. Find the gopuram's height, and state why the SAME HOUR condition is essential.

(Evaluation) A student claims: "If 6 taps fill a tank in 8 hours, then 12 taps fill it in 16 hours, because double the taps do double the filling." Identify the error, give the correct answer, and explain what quantity the student confused.
(Past-paper pattern) A garrison of 800 men has provisions for 30 days. Reinforcements arrive and the provisions now last only 24 days. Find the number of men in the reinforcements. (ICSE-style.)
If a mason completes a wall in 9 days, what fraction of the wall does he build in one day, and in 4 days?
A can embroider a saree in 12 days and B in 18 days. In how many days will they finish one saree working together?
A and B together build a fence in 6 days; A alone builds it in 10 days. How long will B alone take?
A pipe fills a tank in 4 hours, but a leak at the bottom empties the full tank in 12 hours. With both working, how long will the tank take to fill?
Ram and Shyam take 10 and 15 days respectively for a painting contract worth ₹4,000, and work together till it is done. How should the money be divided?
12 men can complete an assignment in 20 days. They work for 4 days, after which 4 men leave. In how many more days will the remaining men finish the assignment?

(HOTS) A is twice as efficient as B, and together they finish a report in 14 days. Find each one's solo time, and derive a general formula for the pair's time when A is k times as efficient as B and B alone would take b days.

(HOTS) Pipes P and Q fill a tank in 20 and 30 hours. They are opened alternately for one hour each, starting with P. How long does the tank take to fill? Compare with the time if both run together continuously.

(Application) A contractor's crew of 9 equal workers finishes a floor in 16 days. After 6 days he adds 3 more workers of the same strength but also loses half a day to rain (no work done). In how many days from the start is the floor finished?

(Evaluation) A student solves "A takes 10 days, B takes 15" by writing: combined time = (10 × 15)/(10 + 15) = 6 days. For a third worker C taking 20 days, the student claims the trio's time is the average (10 + 15 + 20)/3 = 15 days, "since averages work for equal partners". Assess both computations and give the correct trio time.
(Past-paper pattern) A can do 3/5 of a piece of work in 12 days and B can do 2/7 of the same work in 8 days. In how many days can they complete the work together? (ICSE-style.)
What is the amount after 2 years if ₹2 000 is invested at 5 % p.a. compounded yearly?
Find the compound interest on ₹3 000 for 1½ years at 8 % p.a. compounded half‑yearly.
Create a word problem that requires the compound‑interest formula for yearly compounding with n = 3.
CISCE‑style: “The amount on a certain sum at 10 % p.a. compounded yearly for 2 years is ₹1 210. Find the principal.”
**HOTS:** “If the compound interest for the second year on a certain sum at 10 % p.a. compounded yearly is ₹110, find the principal.”
**Application:** “A farmer invests ₹15 000 at 12 % p.a. compounded half‑yearly. How much will he receive after 1 year?”
**Comparison:** “Compare the final amounts for ₹5 000 at 8 % p.a. for 2 years when compounded yearly vs. half‑yearly.”
**CISCE past‑paper pattern:** “The compound interest on a sum for 2 years at 5 % p.a. compounded yearly is ₹205. Find the sum.”
On a scale drawing with 1 cm representing 2 m, what drawn length represents a 12 m corridor, and what real length does a 4.5 cm line represent?
On a 10 × 10 grid, shade 37 squares fully and half of one more square. What percentage and what fraction of the grid is shaded, and what fraction remains?
On a pan balance, 3 identical cubes balance 15 identical marbles. State the marble-value of one cube, and explain the balance reasoning as a proportion statement.
In the mock shop, a toy has CP ₹80, tag ₹100, and a sale bill of ₹90 before tax. Identify each percentage step in rupees, and state why the seller's profit is NOT ₹20.

(HOTS) In the mock shop the following sequence is run instead of the standard one: tax of 10% is added to the tag first, and THEN the "10% off" discount is applied to the tax-inclusive price. Compare the customer's final payment with the standard sequence (discount first, then tax) and prove the general result for any tag T and equal rates r.

(HOTS) A student draws the school's L-shaped boundary on graph paper using 1 cm = 2 m for horizontal edges and 1 cm = 4 m for vertical edges "so it fits the page". The drawn figure is 10 cm by 6 cm. Find the REAL dimensions and the percentage by which the drawing misrepresents the true ratio of width to length.

(Evaluation) Two students verify the answer "A and B together finish a job in 6 days (A alone 10, B alone 15)". Student X lays out 30 counters and lets A remove 3 per day and B remove 2 per day, counting 6 days to clear the board. Student Y re-does the algebra and gets 6 days again. Which verification is stronger, and what does the weaker one miss?

(Past-paper pattern) On a map drawn to the scale 1 : 50,000, two towns are 8.6 cm apart. Find the actual distance in kilometres. If the map is photocopied at 120% enlargement, what distance do the towns now show on the enlarged copy, and what scale statement must accompany the copy? (ICSE-style.)
Identify the terms, coefficients, variables, and constants in the expression 4a²b – 7ab + 3.
Evaluate the claim: "The degree of the expression 2x³y² – 4xy + 7 is 3 because the highest exponent on x is 3."
Simplify the expression 6m²n – 2mn² + 3m²n + 5mn² – 4.

Create an algebraic expression for the following situation: "Riya buys p pens at ₹8 each and q notebooks at ₹12 each, and she also pays a fixed ₹5 for a bag." Then state the terms, coefficients, variables, and constant.
A CISCE Class 8 exam question: "Write the algebraic expression for 'the sum of twice a number x and three times the square of another number y, decreased by 7' and identify its degree."

HOTS: The expression A = 2x²y – 3xy² + 4x – 5y + 6 is given. If each variable is replaced by its negative (x → –x, y → –y), write the new expression and determine whether the value of A changes for all x, y. Justify.
Application: A rectangular garden has length (2m + 3n) metres and breadth (m – n) metres. Write an algebraic expression for its area. If m = 5 and n = 2, compute the area in square metres.
Evaluation/Critique: A textbook states "The degree of the polynomial 4x³y² – 2x²y³ + 7 is 3 because the highest power of x is 3." Critique this statement.
CISCE past‑paper pattern: "Simplify: (5x²y – 3xy²) + (2x²y + 7xy² – 4x) – (x²y – 2xy² + 5)." Write the simplified expression and state its degree.
Explain why (2x + 3)(x – 4) expands to 2x² – 5x – 12.
Multiply (2x + 3)(3x – 1) and state the coefficient of x.
If (ax + b)(cx + d) = 6x² + 11x + 3, find all possible integer quadruples (a, b, c, d).
A student claims that (2x + 3) ÷ (x + 1) simplifies to 2 + 3/x. Critique this statement.
Multiply (3x + 4)(2x – 5) and write the coefficient of x.
A square garden has side (x+5) m. If the side is increased by 2 m, express the new area using the identity.
If (x+1/x)² = 25, find x²+1/(x²).
If *–3x > 9*, what is the correct first step to isolate *x* and why does the inequality sign change?
Solve the inequality **5 – 2x ≤ 13** and represent the solution on a number line.
A student writes: “Since *–4 < –2*, multiplying both sides by –1 gives *4 < 2*.” Identify the error and correct it.
CISCE exam‑style: Solve **3(2x – 1) > 5x + 4** and write the solution set in interval notation.
**HOTS:** If *a > b > 0* and *c < d < 0*, compare *ac* and *bd* without calculating numeric values. Justify your answer using inequality properties.
**Application:** A shopkeeper marks a product at ₹200. He offers a discount of *x*% such that the selling price is **at least ₹150**. Write an inequality for *x* and solve it.
**Evaluation/Critique:** A textbook states: “To solve *–4x < 12*, divide both sides by –4 to get *x < –3*.” Critique this statement.
**Comparison:** Compare the solution sets of **3x – 5 > 7** and **–3x + 5 < –7**. Are they the same? Explain.
**CISCE past‑paper pattern:** Solve the inequality **5 – 3(2x – 1) ≥ 2x + 9** and represent the solution on a number line.
Application: A rectangular sheet has length (3x + 3y) cm and breadth 5 cm. Express the area in factorised form.
Factorise: x² + 12x + 36.
Two students factorise 4y² + 12y + 9. Anu writes (2y + 3)²; Bala writes (2y + 9)(2y + 1). Evaluate both answers.
Factorise completely: 18x² + 60x + 50.
HOTS: For which value(s) of the integer k is x² + kx + 81 a perfect-square trinomial? Give every possibility, its bracket, and the check that each is genuine.

Application: A square mela stall of side (5a + 3) m has its floor fully carpeted. (i) Write the carpet area as a trinomial. (ii) The organiser claims the carpet can be re-laid without cutting as a different perfect square whose side is (5a − 3) m. Is the area the same? Justify and check with a = 1.
Evaluation/Critique: Anu factorises 16x² + 40x + 25 as (4x + 5)². Bala factorises it as (8x + 5)(2x + 5). Decide who is correct by expanding Bala's answer, and settle the verdict with x = 1.

Comparison: Compare the factorisation routes for x² + 10x + 25 and x² + 10x + 24. Why does the perfect-square route serve only the first, and what distinguishes the second's eventual bracket structure?
Evaluate whether 49 − 25 can be computed using the difference‑of‑squares identity, and if so, show the steps.
(HOTS) If (x + y)(x ‑ y) = 24 and x + y = 8, find x ‑ y and then x and y (assume x, y are positive integers).
(Application) A square garden of side 30 m has a square pond of side 12 m at its centre. Find the area of the garden excluding the pond using the difference‑of‑squares identity.
Expand: (x + 4)(x + 9).
A student writes (x + 6)(x + 2) = x² + 12x + 12. Evaluate the claim, correct it, and name the exact confusion.
Expand: (x − 7)(x + 10).
Find integers a and b such that (x + a)(x + b) = x² − 9x + 20, and verify by expanding your brackets.
Expand: (t + 8)(t − 5), and state what the shortcut gives for the sum and product.
HOTS: A positive-integer pair (a, b) with a ≤ b satisfies (x + a)(x + b) = x² + 13x + 36. Find the pair by testing factor candidates systematically, and explain why the answer is unique.

Application: A stage in the school hall is (x + 12) m wide and (x − 7) m deep. (i) Write its floor area in expanded form. (ii) For the area to be positive, what must be true about x? (iii) Check the formula at x = 9.
Evaluation/Critique: Anu expands (x − 3)(x + 5) as x² + 2x − 15. Bala expands it as x² + 2x + 15. Decide who is correct, expose the exact step Bala mishandled, and settle with x = 1.
Comparison: Compare (x + 4)(x + 6) with (x + 5)². Both have middle term 10x. Explain why the constants differ, compute both expansions, and state which one is a perfect square and why.
CISCE past-paper pattern: Expand (x + 12)(x − 7) and (x − 12)(x + 7). How are the two results related, and what single act transforms one into the other?

When building (x + 3)(x + 4) on the board, the two strip cells hold 4 strips and 3 strips. Explain why these strips may be counted together in one middle term, while the unit tiles must be multiplied, not added.
A student builds (x + 2)(x + 5) and reads off x² + 10x + 10 from the board. Evaluate the reading, correct it, and identify which cell was miscounted.
Build (x − 3)(x + 4) with tiles, including the zero-pair cancellations, and state the resulting expression. Verify it at x = 1.
Create a tile arrangement that proves x² + 8x + 15 is the area of a rectangle, and state the rectangle's side expressions.
Using tiles, expand (x + 4)(x + 4), and explain what is special about the tile picture compared with (x + 3)(x + 5), whose expansion has the same strip count.

HOTS: A student claims the kit can directly build (2x + 3)(x + 4) by simply using two x-tiles stuck together as a "2x strip". Assess the claim: what must the corner cell of a 2x-by-x region contain, why does no standard kit tile show it, and what is the correct expansion that any faithful model must produce?

Application: For the school exhibition, a model plot of area x² + 10x + 21 must be shown as a single rectangle on a tile board, with the sides labelled. Find the labels, describe the tile inventory used, and confirm the boundary length (perimeter) expression.

Evaluation/Critique: A teacher-in-training says, "Tiles are only for beginners — they cannot handle negative numbers, so serious algebra must drop them." Critique this claim by showing how the kit handles (x − 4)(x + 6), and state the one genuine limitation tiles have.

Comparison: A group builds (x + 7)(x + 2) with tiles while another solves it symbolically. Compare the two routes: what does each count, where can each go wrong, and what identical final expression must both produce?

CISCE past-paper pattern: A rectangle built on the algebra board has one side labelled (x + 3) and contains 1 x²-tile, 10 x-tiles and 21 unit tiles. Find the other side, write the area as a product and as an expanded expression, and justify the uniqueness of your answer from the tile inventory.
Given a quadrilateral with side lengths 5 cm, 7 cm, 5 cm, 7 cm in order, can you conclude it is a parallelogram? Explain.
A student draws a quadrilateral with opposite sides 6 cm and 6 cm, and the other pair 8 cm and 9 cm. Is this a parallelogram? Evaluate.
If a parallelogram has one side 10 cm and the adjacent side 6 cm, what are the lengths of the other two sides?
In parallelogram ABCD, AB = 8 cm, BC = 5 cm. Find the perimeter.
If a parallelogram has sides expressed as algebraic expressions: AB = 2y + 3, BC = y + 5, CD = 2y + 3, DA = y + 5. For what value of y does the parallelogram become a rhombus?
A garden plot is in the shape of a parallelogram with sides 12 m and 9 m. Find the cost of fencing at ₹50 per metre.
In parallelogram ABCD, AB = 10 cm, BC = 6 cm. The diagonal AC divides the parallelogram into two triangles. Prove that triangle ABC ≅ triangle CDA.
If one angle of a parallelogram is 70°, what are the other three angles? Explain.
In parallelogram PQRS, ∠P = 110°. Find ∠Q, ∠R, ∠S.
Design a parallelogram on a geoboard where one angle is 60°. Show how you would verify opposite angles are equal.
A carpenter needs to cut a wooden piece in the shape of a parallelogram with one angle 85°. He cuts the opposite angle also 85°. Explain why this ensures the piece is a parallelogram.
In parallelogram ABCD the diagonals meet at O, AC = 9.0 cm and BD = 7.2 cm. State AO, OC, BO and OD with the property used.
In parallelogram PQRS, AC-analogue diagonal PR = 11.6 cm and BO-analogue half-diagonal QO = 3.4 cm, where O is the intersection. Find all four sub-segments PO, OR, QO, SO.

You must draw a parallelogram whose diagonals are 12 cm and 8 cm, meeting at their common midpoint O. Describe how the midpoint fact lets you lay out the figure with a ruler alone, and state the four corner distances from O.
The diagonals of parallelogram ABCD meet at O. AO = 3x + 1 cm, OC = 2x + 4 cm, and BO = 5 cm. Find x, AO, OC, AC and BD.

Application: A parallelogram gate panel has diagonals AC = 1.8 m and BD = 1.2 m, crossing at O. A lamp is to be mounted exactly at O, and two small reflector bolts at the midpoints of OA and OB. Find: (i) the distances from the lamp to each of the four corners; (ii) the distance from the lamp to each bolt; (iii) the total diagonal length of steel strip needed to run along both diagonals corner to corner.

Evaluation/Critique: A verification table from a fast worker shows AO = 4.5, OC = 4.6, BO = 3.6, OD = 3.6 cm for one figure, and identical readings repeated for the other two figures. Assess the evidence for the bisection property and prescribe the corrective action.
CISCE past-paper pattern: In parallelogram ABCD, the diagonals meet at O. AO = 2x + 3 cm, OC = 4x − 7 cm, and BD = 2x + 8 cm. Find x, all four half-diagonals, and both full diagonals.

A cuboid of dimensions 6 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm contains a smaller cuboid of dimensions 2 cm × 2 cm × 2 cm placed centrally. Draw the front view and top view, indicating hidden edges. Provide the lengths of visible and hidden edges in the front view.

Design a 2‑D representation (front and side views) for a solid consisting of a cylinder (diameter 4 cm, height 5 cm) with a coaxial cone (base diameter 4 cm, height 3 cm) on top. Show all hidden lines.

In the given figure (describe), identify the number of visible edges, hidden edges, and centre lines in the front view of a nested solid consisting of a cube (side 6 cm) with a centred square pyramid (base 4 cm, height 3 cm) on top.
**HOTS:** A polyhedron has 10 vertices, each of degree 4. How many edges does it have?
Describe the compass construction for bisecting a segment AC = 8 cm, and state the radius condition on the arcs.

A student constructs a quadrilateral by drawing AC = 8 cm, bisecting it to O, and drawing BD = 6 cm through O — but forgets to copy the 60° angle and lets the second diagonal fall at roughly 85°. Evaluate the result.
A parallelogram is to be constructed with diagonals 10 cm and 6 cm meeting at 90°. Describe the construction and name the special member of the family that results.
Design the full construction plan (steps plus justifications) for a parallelogram with diagonals 9 cm and 5 cm meeting at 45°.
Given the data "diagonals 8 cm and 8 cm, meeting at 70°", state which special parallelogram is forced and describe how its construction differs from the general Route B.

HOTS: A student claims Route B constructs "the" parallelogram with the given diagonals and angle — a unique figure. Assess the uniqueness claim: how many non-congruent parallelograms satisfy "diagonals 8 and 6 at 60°", and what does the construction actually fix versus leave free?

Application: A mason must lay out a rectangular garden bed with diagonals of 13 m on ground where only rope and pegs are available. Describe the rope-and-peg version of Route B: how the 13 m rope is halved at the centre peg, how the right angle between the diagonals is enforced with a scaled 5-12-13 rope triangle (2.5 m, 6 m, 6.5 m), and state the final check that confirms the layout is rectangular.

Evaluation/Critique: A student's Route A construction (sides 5 and 3 at 60°) shows the two locating arcs crossing at two points, and the student has chosen the crossing on the SAME side of AB as D, producing a crossed-looking quadrilateral. Diagnose the error and state which crossing is correct and why.
CISCE past-paper pattern: Construct (describe step-by-step) a rhombus with diagonals 10 cm and 24 cm, and state the length of each side with the arithmetic that yields it.
A point P sits 5 grid squares to the left of a vertical mirror line. Where is its image P', and what happens to a point Q that lies exactly on the mirror line?
On squared paper, triangle XYZ has vertices X(0,1), Y(0,4), Z(3,1) with a vertical mirror line along the grid line x = 5. Give the image vertices and describe the reflected triangle.

A half-figure is drawn to the left of a vertical mirror line: half of a rangoli arch with endpoints on the mirror line and one outer peak 4 squares away. State the procedure to complete the figure and the two checks that certify completion.

Application: A jaali (lattice) panel repeats a diamond motif cut in a rectangular frame. The single diamond (a rhombus) has 2 lines of symmetry. (i) What happens to the symmetry count when the diamond is centred in the rectangle frame so its diagonals lie along the frame's own symmetry lines? (ii) If the diamond is mounted off-centre, how many lines survive for the combined panel? (iii) State the principle this comparison teaches about symmetry of combined figures.

Evaluation/Critique: A workbook claims "every figure with two lines of symmetry also has a third". A student offers the rectangle (2 lines only) as a counterexample, but another student objects that the rectangle "obviously" has a third line along a diagonal. Judge the workbook claim, adjudicate the objection, and state the correct general statement about figures with exactly two perpendicular symmetry lines.

CISCE past-paper pattern: On squared paper, square ABCD has corners A(1,1), B(4,1), C(4,4), D(1,4). It is reflected across the vertical line x = 6 to give A'B'C'D', and then A'B'C'D' is reflected across the horizontal line y = 6 to give A''B''C''D''. Write all three sets of vertices, and state which single transformation maps ABCD directly onto A''B''C''D''.
A circle has radius 4.2 cm. State its diameter with the computation, and state where its centre lies relative to the diameter.
Explain, using the string-and-nail picture, why all radii of one circle are equal, and why that forces diameter = 2 × radius for every diameter.
Three chords of a circle of radius 5 cm measure 9.0 cm, 6.0 cm and 10.0 cm. Which chord is the diameter, and what two checks confirm the identification?
Chords are drawn at distances 0 cm, 2.1 cm and 3.9 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. Arrange the chords by length and state the length of the first chord.

With compasses set to 3.5 cm, a circle is drawn with centre O. On its circumference, points P and Q are joined by a chord PQ that misses O, and point R is joined through O to the point S where the line RO meets the circle again. State the lengths of PQ and RS, and classify each segment.
A bangle of inner diameter 6.4 cm is checked with a strip of known radius marks. State the bangle's inner radius, and decide whether a circular card of radius 3.1 cm will slip through the inner hole.

HOTS: A student claims: "Since the diameter is the longest chord, any chord shorter than the diameter is closer to the rim, so chord length ALONE tells you the chord's distance from the centre." Assess the claim: given only that a chord measures 6 cm in a circle of radius 5 cm, can you tell its exact distance from the centre? What extra information would settle it, and what does this say about position versus length?

Application: A potter's wheel has its spike at O, and its rim is a circle of radius 30 cm. (i) A clay lump is centred at O and shaped into a perfect ring of outer radius 12 cm: where does the ring sit relative to the rim circle? (ii) A stick of length 58 cm is laid across the wheel in a straight line with its two ends resting ON the rim: can such a stick pass through the centre, and what is the longest straight stick that can lie entirely across the wheel from rim to rim?

Evaluation/Critique: A workbook diagram shows a circle with centre O and three segments labelled "chord A (8 cm), chord B (8 cm), chord C (8 cm)" in a circle of radius 5 cm, and the caption claims "all three chords are the same length, so all three are equally distant from the centre, and one of them is the diameter." Judge every part of the caption.

CISCE past-paper pattern: In a circle of centre O and radius 6.5 cm, AB is a diameter and CD is a chord of length 7 cm. (i) State the length of AB. (ii) Triangle OCD is formed by joining O to C and D: state OC and OD with reason, and state the perimeter of triangle OCD. (iii) Explain what happens to the shape and perimeter of triangle OCD as the chord CD is moved closer and closer to being a diameter.
A circle has radius 10 cm. A chord is 12 cm long. Find the distance of the chord from the centre.
A chord of a circle of radius 7 cm subtends a central angle of 90°. Calculate the length of the chord.
In a circle of radius 5 cm, two chords AB and CD are equidistant from the centre. If AB = 8 cm, what is the length of CD?
A chord of a circle is 24 cm long and its distance from the centre is 5 cm. Find the radius of the circle.
A circular window of radius 1.5 m has a horizontal bar (chord) placed 0.9 m below the centre. What is the length of the bar?
Compare the chord length for a central angle of 60° in circles of radii 5 cm and 10 cm. What is the ratio of the two chord lengths?
A past ICSE paper asks: “In a circle of radius 10 cm, a chord is drawn 6 cm from the centre. Find the length of the chord.” Provide the solution as expected in the exam.
Two radii of a circle of radius 6 cm make an angle of 210° at the centre. Classify the sector between them, compute its area, and state the area of the complementary sector.
The minute hand of a wall clock is 12 cm long. Find the length of the arc its tip traces and the area it sweeps in 20 minutes (π = 22/7).

A circular pizza of radius 14 cm is cut into 8 equal slices through the centre. For one slice, find the central angle, the area, the length of crust (arc), and the full perimeter of the slice (π = 22/7).
A sector cut from a circle of radius 21 cm has area 231 cm². Find its central angle, and state what fraction of the circle it occupies.

HOTS: Two sectors have the same central angle 90°, one cut from a circle of radius 7 cm and one from a circle of radius 14 cm. A student claims: "Same angle, so the same fraction, so the same area." Evaluate the claim by computing both areas, and state precisely what the angle alone determines and what it does not.

Application: A circular roti of radius 7 cm is shared equally by 4 children, each cut running from the centre to the rim. (i) State the shape and central angle of each child's piece. (ii) Compute the length of roti-crust (arc) and the total boundary length of one piece (π = 22/7). (iii) One child insists her piece is "a segment because it has a curved side". Correct her with the boundary-part test.

Evaluation/Critique: A workbook shows a shaded region bounded by chord PQ and arc PQ of a circle of radius 7 cm, where the chord subtends 90° at the centre. The caption reads: "This region is a sector of 90°, so its area is (90/360) × (22/7) × 49 = 38.5 cm²." Judge each part of the caption and supply the corrected computation.

CISCE past-paper pattern: In a circle of radius 21 cm, two radii OA and OB are drawn with ∠AOB = 120°. (i) Find the length of arc AB and the area of sector OAB (π = 22/7). (ii) Find the perimeter of the sector. (iii) The remaining part of the circle is also a sector: state its central angle and its area, and verify that the two sector areas add to the circle's area.
If a cuboid has dimensions 4 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm, list the dimensions of the three distinct rectangle types that appear in its net.
Draw a net for a cuboid of length 6 cm, breadth 4 cm, height 3 cm. Then calculate its total surface area using the net.
Create two different nets for a cuboid of dimensions 5 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm. Explain how you know both are valid.

In an ICSE exam, a question shows four flat patterns labelled P, Q, R, S. Only one folds into a cuboid of dimensions 7 cm × 5 cm × 3 cm. Pattern P has six rectangles: two 7 × 5, two 7 × 3, two 5 × 3, but the two 7 × 5 rectangles share an edge. Pattern Q has the same rectangles but the two 7 × 5 are separated. Pattern R has five rectangles. Pattern S has six rectangles but one is a square 5 × 5. Which pattern is the correct net? Justify.
**HOTS:** A cuboid has dimensions l, b, h. Prove that the number of distinct nets of a cuboid is 11, independent of the actual values of l, b, h (provided they are all different).

**APPLICATION:** A packaging designer needs a net for a cuboidal box of inner dimensions 20 cm × 15 cm × 10 cm, with flaps of 2 cm on every edge for gluing. Sketch the net including flaps and calculate the total area of cardboard required.

**EVALUATION/CRITIQUE:** A textbook shows a net for a cuboid where two opposite faces are drawn as squares of side 5 cm, and the other four faces are rectangles 5 cm × 3 cm. The caption says “Net of a cuboid 5 cm × 5 cm × 3 cm”. Critique this representation.

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** The diagram shows a net of a cuboid with dimensions marked on some edges. The net consists of a central rectangle 8 cm × 6 cm, with rectangles attached to its four sides: top 8 cm × 4 cm, bottom 8 cm × 4 cm, left 6 cm × 4 cm, right 6 cm × 4 cm, and a final rectangle attached to the top edge of the top rectangle, also 8 cm × 6 cm. Find the total surface area of the cuboid.
If the edge of a cube is 5 cm, what is the length of its face diagonal? Show the reasoning.
A cubic gift box has edge 12 cm. How much wrapping paper (in cm²) is needed to cover its entire surface? Assume no overlap.
CISCE exam‑style: A solid cube of side 8 cm is cut into 64 smaller cubes of equal size. What is the total surface area of all the small cubes combined? (Answer in cm²)
HOTS: A cube is inscribed in a sphere such that all eight vertices touch the sphere. If the sphere’s radius is 6 cm, find the cube’s volume.
Application: A carpenter needs to make a cubic wooden box of inner edge 30 cm using 2 cm thick planks. What is the outer edge length, and how much wood (volume of planks) is used?
Evaluation/Critique: A textbook states “A cube has 12 edges, so it has 12 planes of symmetry.” Critique this statement.
Comparison: Compare the number of distinct nets of a cube (11) with that of a regular tetrahedron (2). Why does the cube have more?
CISCE past‑paper pattern: The total surface area of a cube is 150 cm². Find its volume.
A square pyramid has base side 8 cm and height 6 cm. Calculate its volume.
Design a net for a triangular pyramid (tetrahedron) with all edges 5 cm. Sketch it and label dimensions.
CISCE exam‑style: A right square pyramid has base side 10 cm and slant height 13 cm. Find its total surface area.
**Application:** A tent is shaped like a square pyramid with base side 3 m and slant height 2.5 m. How much canvas (in m²) is needed to cover the lateral surface only?
**CISCE past‑paper pattern:** A right square pyramid has a base perimeter of 40 cm and a slant height of 13 cm. Find its lateral surface area.
What is the volume of a right triangular prism whose base is a triangle with base 6 cm, height 4 cm, and prism height 12 cm?
A right prism has a regular pentagonal base of side 3 cm. Its height is 8 cm. Which expression gives the lateral surface area?
A right prism has a base shaped like a right trapezoid with parallel sides 5 cm and 9 cm, distance between them 4 cm. The prism height is 10 cm. Find its total surface area.
Create a net for a right triangular prism with base sides 3 cm, 4 cm, 5 cm and height 7 cm. List the dimensions of each face in the net.
A CISCE exam question: “A right prism has a regular hexagonal base of side 2 cm and height 5 cm. Find its volume.” (Use √3 ≈ 1.732)
A right prism has a base that is a kite with diagonals 8 cm and 6 cm. The prism height is 12 cm. Find its volume.
A student draws the net of a right square prism (cube) but labels one lateral face as a square of side 5 cm while the base square is 4 cm. Explain why this net cannot fold into a right square prism.
Compare the volume of a right triangular prism (base right triangle legs 3 cm, 4 cm; height 10 cm) with a right rectangular prism of base 3 cm × 4 cm and same height.
A past CISCE paper asks: “The total surface area of a right prism with a regular hexagonal base of side 2 cm is 150 cm². Find its height.” (Use √3 = 1.732)

Construct a triangle with sides 5 cm, 6 cm, and 7 cm using compass and straightedge. What is the length of the altitude from the vertex opposite the 7 cm side? (Use construction to find approximate length, then calculate using Heron’s formula for verification.)
Design a construction sequence to draw a regular hexagon of side 4 cm using only compass and straightedge. How many distinct compass/straightedge actions are required at minimum? Justify your count.

A student constructs a triangle with sides 4 cm, 5 cm, and 9 cm. The arcs from the endpoints of the 9 cm base do not intersect. The student concludes that the construction is impossible because the compass was not opened wide enough. Evaluate this reasoning.

A past CISCE paper asks: “Using ruler and compass only, construct a triangle ABC in which AB = 6 cm, BC = 5 cm and ∠ABC = 60°. Measure AC.” Provide the construction steps and the expected measured length of AC (to the nearest millimetre).
Construct a 60° angle at a point O on a ray using compasses alone, and give the WHY for each step, ending with the verification.
Construct the perpendicular bisector of a 7 cm segment AB. State the radius condition, the steps, the WHY of each, and what goes wrong with radius exactly 3.5 cm or unequal radii.
Copy a given 40° angle onto a new ray using compasses, and justify the construction (which classical fact makes the copy exact?).

A student's perpendicular bisector of an 8 cm segment comes out crossing at 3.7 cm and 4.3 cm, and the crossing angle reads 88°. Diagnose the likely tool causes, ranked, and state the remedy for each.

Application: In a 40-minute exam, a question asks for (1) a line through P parallel to line l, (2) the perpendicular bisector of a 6 cm segment, (3) a 60° angle at a point, each with justification. Plan the tool-and-step budget: for each item, the fastest sound route, the time it should take, and the one-line WHY to be written beside it.

Evaluation/Critique: A student writes: "The maths kit has five tools, so a construction is safest if every tool touches the figure; using fewer tools is laziness." Judge the claim, with the 60° angle and the parallel line as test cases, and state the principle the claim violates.

CISCE past-paper pattern: Using ruler and compasses, construct triangle ABC with AB = 6 cm, ∠A = 60° (compasses only for the angle), and AC = 5 cm. (i) List the steps with the WHY for the angle step. (ii) Complete the triangle and state the instrument used for each length placed. (iii) As a check, measure BC and state the range it should fall in, and name one construction fault that would throw BC outside that range.
On a 5 × 5 geoboard, construct a rectangle with area 6 sq units and perimeter 10 units. Give the coordinates of its four vertices.
On a 10 × 10 geoboard, a rubber band forms a right triangle with vertices at (1,1), (1,6), (6,1). Find its area and the length of the hypotenuse (in units).
A past ICSE paper asks: “On a 9 × 9 geoboard, a rubber band forms a quadrilateral with vertices (1,1), (1,4), (5,6), (6,2). Find its area.” Outline the solution steps.
A student sets the compass to a radius of 3 cm but the drawn circle has a radius of 3.3 cm. Explain two possible reasons for this error.
Using a geometry box, construct a line segment of length 4.7 cm and then copy it to another location using only the divider. Describe the steps.
Design a short activity for a Class 8 peer that demonstrates why a compass must have a sharp point and a tight hinge. Outline the activity and the expected observation.
A CISCE exam question asks: “Construct ∠PQR = 75° using only a ruler and compass.” Explain why a protractor is not allowed and outline the classical construction method.
**HOTS:** A geometry box contains a 30°‑60°‑90° set square. Without using a protractor, show how to construct a 15° angle. Provide a step‑by‑step reasoning.
**APPLICATION:** A carpenter needs to mark a 60° angle on a wooden board using only a geometry box (no power tools). Describe the procedure using the set square and ruler.
**COMPARISON:** Compare the use of a divider versus a ruler for transferring a length of 5.3 cm from one diagram to another. Highlight advantages and limitations of each.

**CISCE PAST‑PAPER PATTERN:** “Using a ruler and compass only, construct a triangle ABC with AB = 5 cm, BC = 4 cm, and ∠ABC = 60°. Measure AC.” Provide the construction steps and the expected measured length of AC (to the nearest millimetre).
A trapezium has parallel sides 12 cm and 8 cm with height 5 cm. Compute its area, and verify by the split-into-triangles method.
The area of a trapezium is 45 cm² and its parallel sides measure 8 cm and 7 cm. Find its height, and verify by re-substitution.
A trapezium of area 40 cm² has one parallel side 9 cm and height 5 cm. Find the other parallel side, and verify.
An isosceles trapezium has parallel sides 11 cm and 5 cm and height 4 cm. Find its leg length and perimeter, and compute its area.

HOTS: A student claims: "The formula (1/2)(a + b)h is a NEW fact to memorise — it has nothing to do with the triangle formula (1/2)bh." Refute the claim by showing the triangle formula lives INSIDE the trapezium formula twice, and evaluate what happens to the trapezium formula as b shrinks to 0.

Application: A dam's cross-section is a trapezium: top width 6 m, base width 18 m, height 12 m. (i) Compute the cross-section area. (ii) The engineer claims: "Doubling the height to 24 m while keeping the widths doubles the area." Verify with the formula, and state what actually scales when only h changes. (iii) The widths are instead widened to 8 m and 24 m at height 12 m: does the area double? Compute and compare.

Evaluation/Critique: A student submits: "A trapezium of bases 10 and 4 and slant sides 5 each has area (1/2)(10 + 4)(5) = 35 cm²." Identify every error, compute the correct area (given the figure is isosceles), and state the check that would have caught it.

CISCE past-paper pattern: A plot is a right trapezium — parallel sides 25 m and 15 m, with the leg adjoining them at right angles measuring the height. (i) Sketch (describe) the plot, marking the right angle, and state the height if that perpendicular leg is 12 m. (ii) Compute the plot's area. (iii) The fourth (slant) side is to be wired at ₹45 per metre: find its length by Pythagoras' relation and the wiring cost, and verify that the slant side is longer than the height.
A regular pentagon has side length 10 cm and apothem 6.88 cm. Find its area.
A semi‑circular window has diameter 1.4 m. Find the area of glass needed.
The area of a regular octagon is 200 cm². If its side length is 5 cm, find its apothem. (Use √2 ≈ 1.414)
A farmer has a field shaped like a regular hexagon of side 20 m. He wants to plant grass. If grass seed covers 10 m² per kg, how many kg of seed are needed?
A textbook gives area of a regular polygon as (n s²) / (4 tan(π/n)). A student uses this for an irregular polygon. Critique.
A plot of land is in the shape of a regular pentagon of side 30 m. A semi‑circular pond of radius 10 m is dug inside the plot touching one side. Find the remaining area of the plot. (Take π = 22/7)
A cube has an edge length of 4 cm. Calculate its total surface area.
If the total surface area of a cube is 150 cm², find the length of its edge.
A gift box is a cube of side 20 cm. How many square centimetres of wrapping paper are needed to cover it completely, assuming no overlap?
Design a cube-shaped container that has a total surface area of 864 cm². What should be the edge length? Show your reasoning.
A CISCE exam question: “The total surface area of a cube is 294 cm². Find its volume.” (Hint: use the edge length from surface area.)
A cube’s edge is increased by 50 %. By what percentage does its total surface area increase?
A cubic water tank has a total surface area of 216 m². If the tank is open at the top, what is the area of the metal sheet used to make it?
Compare the total surface area of a cube of side 4 cm with that of a cuboid of dimensions 4 cm × 4 cm × 8 cm. Which has the larger surface area and by how much?
A past CISCE paper asks: “The total surface area of a cube is 150 cm². Find the length of its diagonal.” (Use √3 ≈ 1.732)
Find the height of a cuboid whose volume is 720 cm³, length 12 cm and breadth 6 cm.
Design a cuboidal box with volume 1000 cm³ that has the minimum possible total surface area. State its dimensions.
A cuboidal room measures 6 m × 5 m × 3 m. Find the cost of painting its four walls at ₹15 per m².
If the total surface area of a cuboid is 236 cm² and its length and breadth are 8 cm and 6 cm respectively, find its height.
A cuboidal tank 2.5 m long, 1.2 m wide, 1 m high is filled with water. How many litres of water does it hold?
Compare the total surface area of a cube of side 5 cm and a cuboid of dimensions 5 cm × 5 cm × 10 cm. Which has the larger surface area and by how much?
The volume of a cuboid is 480 cm³. Its length is 12 cm and breadth is 8 cm. Find its height and total surface area.
A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. If the radius is doubled while the height remains the same, how does the curved surface area change? Explain.

A cylindrical water tank of radius 0.5 m and height 2 m is to be painted on the outside (including top and bottom). If paint covers 10 m² per litre, how many litres of paint are needed? (Use π = 3.14)

Design a cylindrical container that holds exactly 1 litre of milk with minimum material (i.e., minimum total surface area). State the dimensions you would choose (radius and height) and show the reasoning.
A solid cylinder of radius 6 cm and height 15 cm is melted and recast into a solid sphere. Find the radius of the sphere. (Take π = 22/7)
A cylindrical pipe of inner radius 2 cm, outer radius 2.5 cm, and length 1 m is made of metal. Find the volume of metal used. (Use π = 3.14)
A solid cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 24 cm is melted and recast into a solid sphere. Find the radius of the sphere. (Take π = 22/7)
A closed cylindrical tin has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Compute its CSA and TSA, and verify that TSA − CSA equals the area of the two lids.
A cone has vertical height 24 cm and base radius 7 cm. Find its slant height, its CSA, and its TSA (π = 22/7).

A hemispherical steel bowl has inner radius 21 cm. Find the area of its curved inner surface and its total surface area (curved outside same radius plus the flat rim ring ignored — treat as exact hemisphere), quoting both in cm² and m².

Compare the LSA of a cuboid with the CSA of a cylinder: state both formulas, compute each for l = 10, b = 8, h = 7 (cm) and r = 7, h = 7 (cm) with π = 22/7, and explain what makes them the 'same kind' of quantity.

HOTS: A grain silo is a cylinder of radius 3.5 m and height 10 m, topped by a hemispherical cap of the same radius, standing on the ground. A painter quotes to paint the ENTIRE outside at ₹25 per m². Compute the exact paintable area, the fair price, and evaluate the painter's shortcut of computing 'cylinder TSA + hemisphere curved area'.

Application: A road roller has a cylindrical drum of diameter 84 cm and width (length) 1 m. (i) Compute the lateral (curved) area of the drum in m². (ii) In levelling a playground the drum makes 500 complete rolls — find the area levelled, assuming each roll lays down the full curved surface once, with no overlap. (iii) The playground measures 50 m × 26.4 m: what FRACTION is levelled, and what quality-check does the no-overlap assumption let you make?

Evaluation/Critique: A student claims: "The cone's TSA formula πr(l + r) is just the cylinder's TSA formula 2πr(r + h) with h replaced by l and the 2 dropped, because a cone is a cylinder tapering to a point." Identify what the claim gets right, what it gets wrong, and settle the matter by computing both TSAs for r = 7, h = 24, l = 25.

Comparison: Arrange the five round-surface formulas for r = 7 (cylinder CSA, cylinder TSA h = 10, cone CSA l = 25, sphere, hemisphere TSA) in increasing order, and explain — without recomputing — which pairs the master relation TSA = CSA + flat ends connects, using the computed values as evidence.

CISCE past-paper pattern: A wooden toy is a cone of slant height 25 cm mounted exactly on a hemisphere of radius 7 cm (the cone's base coincides with the hemisphere's flat face). (i) Find the cone's base radius given its vertical height is 24 cm, verifying consistency with the slant. (ii) Compute the toy's total surface area (the flat joint face is internal).
